      from `package_digest`**. That exclusion is the load-bearing part: the records already
      encode the grid they were resolved on, so a re-resolution changes the digest through
      them. Digesting the pin as well would add nothing to change detection and would
      report **every stored run as drifted** the moment this landed, for no change in what
      any package builds.
      Stamped in `GeoPackageSource._metadata`, which every one of the seven list BCs
      reaches, so one line pins `chd`/`ghb`/`drn`/`riv`/`wel`/`rch`/`evt`.
      **A hand-written package stays unpinned, deliberately.** `mf.chd(stress_period_data=
      {...})` names no source mesh -- the caller typed the cell numbers and the library was
      never told what they meant -- so there is nothing to pin, and 249's range check plus
      its documented gap remain exactly as necessary as before. A pin can only speak for
      records the library resolved.
      **Deferred from the plan's commit 5, deliberately:** the `recipe` field,
      the `concrete_for` dispatcher and `model.myflopy_resolved`. Each is plumbing whose
      only consumer is the lazy `.gpkg` path in commit B2, and landing a field that nothing
      reads is how dead code arrives. They come with B2. Worth recording from the
      2026-09-13 survey: the recipe **cannot** ride in the existing `PackageSpec.inputs`
      field, which looked like a free slot -- `inputs` is splatted into the builder as
      kwargs at build time, so it works only where the builder is a myflopy function, and
      a spec built by a bare FloPy class (most list BCs) raises `TypeError`.
      `mf.sfr`/`mf.lak`/`mf.uzf` are not pinned yet; they resolve through their own
      builders rather than through `GeoPackageSource`, and their pins land with C1.
      `tests/test_grid_pin.py` (14 tests) pins the fingerprint's stability, that two meshes
      differ and two instances of one mesh agree, the local-origin and renumbering cases,
      an unreadable grid answering `None` rather than raising, the stamp, the refusal and
      its two-hash message, both controls, the unpinned hand-written package, the digest
      exclusion, and the `to_dict` round trip. Nine mutants, all killed.

251. **A run whose packages held an array could not be rebuilt at all (2026-09-13).**
      Phase 2 commit **A3**. A run's manifest stores a recipe, `SimulationSpec.to_dict()`,
      and a recipe cannot hold an array -- `to_dict` refuses `numpy.ndarray` outright. So
      a model carrying an inline `k` or `strt` wrote `spec_recipe=None`, `reopen_run(name)
      .spec` came back `None`, and `Run.build` raised "A reopened run without a spec cannot
      be rebuilt". Everything expressed as `mf.ref` survived, because those arrays live in
      the package library; everything inline did not.
      `project/freeze.py` writes the resolved simulation to `<run>/.myflopy/frozen.npz` at
      the end of `Run.build` -- structure as JSON, every array beside it, plus the grid's
      vertices, cells, CRS and layer elevations. A reopened run thaws that and reads no
      source file. **AMENDED AGAIN 2026-09-14: none of this worked on a real grid until
      ledger 263.** `freeze_simulation` ends at `lifted.to_dict()`, and `_json_value`
      refused the `numpy.int64` vertex indices flopy's `VoronoiGrid` emits -- so no
      snapshot was written at all, `Run._freeze` swallowed the failure as a warning, and
      the run reported success. Every test here used a hand-built grid whose `iverts`
      are python ints, which is the one shape that cannot show it.
      **AMENDED 2026-09-13, same day:** as first committed that last claim
      was only true of a model whose grid was already built. A declared `ModelSpec`
      carries the grid RECIPE, and `ModelSpec.build` resolves it into a LOCAL context --
      so freezing `Run.spec` captured no grid at all for a DEFERRED grid, and left the
      recipe in place. A reopened run went straight back to its boundary and refinement
      GeoPackages and died on `pyogrio.errors.DataSourceError` naming the missing file,
      with the snapshot sitting beside it and no myflopy frame in the traceback. Freeze
      now takes the contexts the build RESOLVED (`Run.built.models[...].context`), the
      thaw clears `ModelSpec.grid` because the snapshot's grid is authoritative, and
      **the snapshot WINS over the manifest's recipe on reopen** -- a recipe is
      instructions and re-running them re-resolves, while the snapshot is what the run
      actually built. Prepare the run again to re-resolve. Found by a scoping workflow
      asking a different question entirely. Measured on a real Ten Trails run: **2.78 MB against 22.2 MB of MF6
      input and a 1,023 MB run -- 0.27%**, because binary beats MF6's ~15 characters per
      number and a repetitive array compresses to nothing (`tentrails.rch_pond`, 597,636
      numbers, 9.53 MB of text to 10 KB). Unconditional, on the user's call.
      **The first version of this was defective in six ways, all found by an adversarial
      review before it was committed. They are recorded because each was a plausible
      design, not a slip.**
      - **A stale snapshot rebuilt the previous model in silence.** `prepare_run(
        overwrite=True)` reuses a run directory (D5, ledger 191) and nothing invalidated
        the snapshot, which carried no run name and no stamp -- so re-preparing a run and
        rebuilding it returned the OLD simulation. That was a REGRESSION: the same path
        used to raise. It is now stamped with its run name, refused on a mismatch, and
        DISCARDED by `prepare_run` whenever a directory is reused, so a run staged with
        `build=False` holds no answer it was never asked for.
      - **An object-dtype array froze and could never be thawed.** `savez` is permissive
        and stores one by PICKLING; `load` is strict and refuses a pickle, which is right,
        because reading one can execute code. FloPy's own list-BC recarray is exactly that
        shape -- `[('cellid', 'O'), ('head', '<f8'), ('boundname', 'O')]`, a tuple and a
        string -- so the snapshot reported success and the rebuild died on a bare numpy
        message naming neither the run nor the package. `_refuse_object_array` now refuses
        at FREEZE time, naming the model, the package, the option and the offending
        fields, which is where it can be acted on.
      - **`context.surfaces` was dropped silently**, and the rebuilt grid had no
        `gdf_topbtm`, so both arms of `specs._layer_elevations` -- the single function SFR,
        LAK and `CellSurfaceOffset` resolve elevations through (ledger 209) -- came back
        `None`. A straight rebuild is byte-identical, so nothing announced it; the loss
        only appeared when editing a thawed run. The elevations are carried now, numeric
        columns in the npz and geometry restored in FIRST position (ledger 196).
      - **A thawed run never received the project's build context.** `reopen_run` set it
        only `if run.spec is not None` -- false for exactly the runs the snapshot exists
        to rescue -- so every `mf.grid_ref` and any `mf.ref` without a per-run copy failed.
      - **The write was not atomic**, though the docstring said it was: `rmtree` then
        `os.replace` is two operations, and two concurrent builds shared one staging name,
        so a loser could delete a good snapshot and fail to replace it. The snapshot is
        ONE FILE now, and `os.replace` of a file is a single atomic step.
      - **`_lift` was not invertible on its own output.** A caller's dict shaped like the
        array token was consumed by `_drop` and came back as an unrelated array, or raised
        blaming the snapshot for the caller's data. Such a dict is escaped now.
      NOT carried, and stated rather than hidden: `ModelContext.dates`, which `to_dict`
      does not serialize either and which no resolved package reads. Snapshots are format
      **2**; format 1 was never released.
      What survived the review unchanged is worth recording too: eleven
      build/write/freeze/thaw/write comparisons came back identical across every file, and
      a thawed run still resolves `mf.ref` from its own `<run>/_library/` copies, so it
      builds what the library path would (ledger 230 holds).
      `tests/test_frozen_runs.py` (21 tests) pins the round trip, dtype preservation,
      cellids and period keys, the grid pinning identically (ledger 250) -- the first
      version stored polygon centroids and landed 24.18 length units off its own DISV,
      which ledger 249's guard caught immediately -- the surfaces, the domain's VALUES not
      merely its shape, both refusals, the token escape, the single-file write, and that a
      failed freeze never fails a build. The whole-directory comparison ignores FloPy's
      header line, which stamps the wall-clock SECOND and made the first version of that
      test flaky at 3-5%.

## Map colour scales and custom geometry (2026-09-13)

252. **`logscale=True` now reads in real units everywhere, and its limits are DATA
    units (2026-09-13).**
    - What: ledger 74 recorded that every `logscale` map labelled its colorbar in
      log10 units (`-3 … 2` for a field running 0.001 to 100) while its hover showed
      real values, and that only the PEST field maps relabelled it. The fix is now
      where 74 said it belonged -- on `Choro`, which knows it is log-scaled. The
      trace still carries `log10(value)` (Plotly has no log colour axis) and
      `Choro._trace_color_kwargs` puts decade ticks labelled in real units on it
      through ONE helper, `viz.log_decade_colorbar`, which `Choro`, `viz.mosaic`
      and `ies._log_decade_colorbar` all call. `plot_mpl` draws a log map through
      `matplotlib.colors.LogNorm` over the DATA-unit values (`Choro.linear_zs`), so
      its colorbar is a true log axis; caller `tickvals`/`ticktext` are raised to
      data units and applied by `plot_mpl` itself (`_apply_caller_colorbar_ticks`),
      which is what keeps the PEST change map's `0.1x / 1x / 10x`. `viz.mosaic`
      relabels a grid of log panels from the pooled limits by itself and REFUSES
      to pool a log panel with a linear one (one axis cannot mean both). `Choro.ani`
      rebuilds the labels over the SHARED frame range. `contours=True` on a log map
      contours the real field, not the exponents.
    - **`zmin`/`zmax`/`zmid` are now DATA units under `logscale=True`** (user
      decision, 2026-09-13): `zmin=1e-4, zmax=10` means K from 0.0001 to 10, matching
      the bar and the hover; a non-positive limit raises at the call. This is a
      behaviour change for any caller who passed log10 limits before -- the only
      in-repo one, `ies._field_map_policy("change")`, now returns `10 ** ±half` and
      `zmid=1.0`, and its tests moved with it. Stored notebook outputs of log maps
      (the concern 74 raised) change on re-run: their colorbars now read real units.
    - Compromises: matplotlib's own decade labels are mathtext (`10^{-3}`) unless a
      caller passes ticks, while the Plotly bar writes `0.001`; the two read the same
      numbers in different typography. Fewer than three whole decades in range gives
      five evenly spaced real-unit labels rather than one or two ticks. A `colorbar=`
      given to a mosaic still wins over the automatic relabel, and `ies.
      _log_decade_colorbar_for_mosaic` stays as the explicit spelling. `SliderAnimation`
      (the `png` animate backend) inherits the `LogNorm` picture frame by frame and
      was not separately measured.
    - Revisit: if a caller needs a symmetric log scale for SIGNED fields (a
      `symlog`), that is a new option, not a change to this one. Ledger 71's mosaic
      question and 74's "why not fixed generally" are closed by this entry.
    - Tests: `tests/test_map_colorscale_and_features.py` (logscale section) plus the
      updated `test_colorscale_policy.py` expectations (`test_mf6_pest.py`'s held
      unchanged, which is the point: a PEST caller sees the same picture).
    - **Review pass, same day** (three-lens adversarial review, ledger 255): the
      LEGACY hover (`hover_dict`, taken by a bare-grid map with no `hover_spec`) still
      listed the log10 exponent under `zs` -- now `linear_zs`; the NOUN-tier static
      composers (`SpatialView._mpl_mosaic` / `_mpl_animation`) read `choro.zs` through a
      hard-coded linear `viridis`, so a static log mosaic read `-3 ... 2` under a real-unit
      label -- now `_mpl_shared_scale`: the panel's own colorscale, `linear_zs`, a
      `LogNorm` for log panels, and a refusal to mix; `plot.animate` frames of log maps
      are now pooled onto one shared colour axis (as `.ani` already was) so the restyle
      HTML export keeps its decade labels on every frame; an infinite limit and a
      non-positive `plot_mpl(vmin=)` are refused at the call; a whole decade past a
      million is written out (`1000000`), not `1e+06`.

253. **Every Plotly colorscale name is accepted, and the static colormap is built from
    Plotly's own stops (2026-09-13).**
    - What: `Choro.colorscale` validated against a hand-written list of eighteen
      names and warned-then-drew `earth` for `"Turbo"`, `"Plasma"`, `"viridis_r"` and
      the other ~80 Plotly ships. It now validates through
      `plotly.colors.get_colorscale` (`viz.plotly_colorscale_stops`, re-exported by
      `choros`): every named
      scale, case-insensitively, with `_r` reversing one. `mpl_colormap_for` builds
      a `LinearSegmentedColormap` from the SAME stops for a name as it already did
      for explicit stops, which retires the plotly-to-matplotlib hand table that
      mapped `'rdbu'` to matplotlib's REVERSED colormap and every other name to
      `gist_earth` -- ledger 69/70's mirrored-diverging wart is gone (user decision:
      "derive from Plotly's own stops", 2026-09-13).
    - Consequence: the STATIC output of any map that passed a NAME changes. `earth`
      was `gist_earth` and is now Plotly's own brown-to-blue ramp; `Hot`/`Jet`/`Blues`
      now render as Plotly draws them rather than as matplotlib's same-named maps;
      a named `RdBu` is no longer mirrored. Interactive output is unchanged.
    - Kept deliberately: an unknown name still WARNS and falls back to `earth` --
      the deliberate inverse of `_field_map_policy`, which raises -- because a typo
      in a notebook cell should cost a warning, not the figure. The "ship the exchange
      scales as STOPS" rule also stays, for a different reason than before: the
      helpers own the ORIENTATION (which end is gaining), which a name cannot carry.
    - Compromise: `mpl_colormap_for(name)` now returns a `Colormap` object rather
      than a matplotlib name string; every caller passes it to `cmap=`, which takes
      both, and `viz.mpl_color` parses Plotly's `rgb(...)` spelling for it. The three
      helpers live in `viz` (layer 0) so the noun-tier static composers import them at
      module level rather than adding to the deferred-import ratchet.
    - Tests: `test_every_plotly_named_colorscale_is_accepted`,
      `test_the_static_colormap_is_built_from_the_plotly_stops`,
      `test_an_unknown_colorscale_name_warns_and_falls_back_to_earth`.

254. **`locs=` is deprecated for `features=`, and the retired spelling is drawn
    through the new engine (2026-09-13).**
    - What: `map(features=...)` at every scope -- the free verb, `model.plot`,
      `vor.plot`, `stack.plot.map(basemap=True)` and every noun, through
      `NOUN_MAP_PARAMS` -- takes a vector file path, a `GeoDataFrame`/`GeoSeries`, a
      shapely geometry, a `myflopy.plot.Feature` spec (`name`/`layer`/`color`/
      `width`/`size`/`fill`/`opacity`/`label`/`hover`/`crs`/`show_legend`), or a
      list/dict of those. `utils/datatypes/features.py` is ONE resolver
      (`resolve_features`: read, CRS-place, WGS84, colour, hover columns) and TWO
      renderers (`feature_traces` for Plotly, `draw_features_mpl` for matplotlib),
      so the backends cannot disagree about a layer. One `Scattermap` per layer and
      geometry kind sharing a `legendgroup`, so a 500-well file is one legend entry
      and not 500; hover is `<b>label</b>` plus the attribute columns; colours come
      from `viz.category_colors`, so "Wells" is the same colour on every figure.
      Resolved eagerly in `Choro.__init__` (a missing file or unknown GeoPackage layer
      raises at the call, like `select=`); rides `overlay_traces()`, so `mosaic`,
      `animate` and `.ani` keep it.
    - `locs=` (user decision: deprecate, 2026-09-13) is a *behaviour* deprecation
      (`since` 0.2.0; not an alias, so not in `__compatibility__`): removed from every
      `def` line and from `NOUN_MAP_PARAMS`, caught in the `**kwargs` tail by
      `Choro.__init__`, warned with `warn_deprecated("myflopy.plot.map(locs=)",
      "features=")`, and drawn as a `Feature` named "locations". `Choro.locs`,
      `add_locs` and `_locs_traces` are GONE (policy D12: nothing an editor reads may
      echo the retired spelling). **Its picture changed**: a legend entry, a house
      colour and an attribute hover instead of unlabelled black markers; LineStrings
      are drawn (they were skipped); the per-row `ExploName` trace names are gone (the
      name is in the hover instead); a `str` path now works (it used to warn and draw
      nothing). `test_real_choro_overlays_survive_composition` moved to `features=`.
    - Deliberately NOT offered, each with a reason: `symbol=` for markers (Maplibre
      symbols need the basemap's sprite icons and ignore `size`/`color` on anything
      but `circle`, so the parameter would act on one style and not another); text
      labels on the map (`mode="text"` clutters a wells file; the label heads the
      hover instead); `features=` on `plot.grid` (the 2-D mesh draws in grid
      coordinates with no CRS, which is its point); a hole in a FILLED polygon is not
      cut out (the outline trace draws every ring, the fill trace covers the
      exterior; a pond with an island fills over the island); hover on a filled
      polygon fires only at its vertices (Plotly); the hover lists at most
      `MAX_HOVER_COLUMNS = 12` attribute columns (an INFO log says so; `hover=[...]`
      chooses); a bare multi-layer GeoPackage path reads the first layer with GDAL's
      own `UserWarning`, as `select=` does; `plot_mpl` still ignores raw
      `add_overlay` traces (Plotly objects). A `Feature.crs=` given for a source that
      ALREADY declares a different CRS raises rather than overriding: a silent
      override misplaces every well.
    - Revisit triggers: a request for well symbols by type (then a marker-symbol
      column mapped through Maplibre sprites, with the `circle` caveat documented);
      a request to label features on the map; ponds with islands.
    - Tests: `tests/test_map_colorscale_and_features.py` (features section and the
      retired-spelling section, incl. the signature guard); `derive_docstrings.py`
      re-run so every noun documents `features` and none documents `locs`.
    - **Review pass, same day** (ledger 255): the engine imported the grid package's
      vector reader at module level, and that package's `__init__` imports the
      choropleth, which imports the engine -- a cycle invisible to the suite (conftest
      primes the package) and to the static acyclicity test (which drops package-init
      edges), but fatal to `import myflopy.modflow.utils.datatypes.choros` in a fresh
      interpreter. The reader is now local to the engine and a subprocess test imports
      both modules cold. Also fixed: `_split` read the column LABELLED `geometry`
      rather than the ACTIVE geometry column (a frame after `set_geometry` drew its
      stale, un-reprojected column on Plotly and the right one on matplotlib); hover
      values are HTML-escaped, `None`/`NA`/`NaT` count as missing and booleans print as
      such; `_unique` re-checks its own suffixes; the retired option's layer never
      clobbers a caller's own dict key; nested `GeometryCollection`s explode fully on
      matplotlib; `Feature(color=)` is validated at construction against what BOTH
      backends parse; `.ani` now carries every overlay (features, contours, highlight)
      into each frame -- it never had, for any overlay -- so the claim above is true;
      the deprecation warning is attributed to the first frame outside `myflopy`, so a
      notebook under the stock warning filters actually shows it.

255. **Review-pass findings NOT acted on, 2026-09-13.**
    - `Feature.color` narrowed to what matplotlib parses (hex, `rgb()`/`rgba()`, CSS
      names): Plotly also takes `hsl()`, which the static backend cannot; refusing at the
      call beats failing at render on one backend.
    - Signed-exchange nouns (`results.q`, the surface-water exchanges, the group maps)
      default symmetric `zmin`/`zmax`/`zmid=0`; with a caller's `logscale=True` the
      choropleth now refuses those defaults with a message naming a limit the caller
      never typed. Left as is: a signed field has no log scale, the refusal is right, and
      the message now says the limits may be the noun's own policy. Revisit if a
      magnitude-of-q map is asked for.
    - A hole in a FILLED polygon is still covered by the fill (outline draws the ring);
      hover on a filled polygon fires only at vertices; markers have no `symbol=`.
    - Ledger 71's symmetric-centering half (`diff=True`) is unchanged.

256. **A saved project was a set of references into whatever directory it was authored in (2026-09-14).**
      Phase 2 commit **A4**. `Project.save(bundle_sources=True)` copies every file the
      project's GRIDS are built from into `<root>/inputs/`, repoints the saved recipes at
      those copies, and repoints the LIVE registry too -- otherwise a later plain `save()`
      writes the original paths back and quietly un-bundles the project. `SaveReport`
      gains `bundled`, the `(from, to)` pairs.
      **AMENDED 2026-09-18: the "grids only" premise below was true when written and is
      now HALF false.** Ledgers 279/284/285 made the seven `.gpkg` list BCs lazy when
      declared without `context=`, so a saved package can hold a PATH and does read a file
      at build -- re-running this entry's own instrument on one model gives eager 0 reads,
      lazy 3 (`gpd.read_file` on the GeoPackage, `open` for its fingerprint,
      `rasterio.open` for a lazy DISV's surface). The eager clause still stands; it is
      simply no longer the whole class. Carrying package sources is its own commit; ledger
      292 fixed the bundler this one shipped, first.
      **GRIDS ONLY, and that is a measurement rather than a scope cut.** The plan's text
      for this commit was "copy every source a RECIPE names", which assumed the recipe
      field deferred from A2. A scoping workflow measured the premise instead of
      assuming it, and it is false in both directions:
      - **Package sources are eager, unread, and mostly unrecorded.** An instrumented
        `gpd.read_file`/`rasterio.open`/`open` recorder scoped to `PackageSpec.build`
        saw **zero reads across 306 passing tests**; a project whose GeoPackage was
        DELETED loaded in a fresh process and rebuilt with all 11 CHD records intact;
        `metadata['source_path']` (written by ledger 250) is read by **nothing**; and
        `mf.sfr(streams=)`, `mf.lak`, `mf.hfb.gpkg` and `mf.uzf` record no path at all.
        Bundling those today copies files nothing opens. That half belongs with the
        commit that makes package resolution lazy.
      - **Grid sources are live.** `ModelSpec.build` re-resolves its `GridSpec` on EVERY
        build, so boundary/refinement/breaklines/points/script/`inputs`/`pickle_path` are
        read every time. `rasters` and `idomain_path` are read LATER still -- the first
        `gdf_topbtm`, the first edge query -- and are bundled too, because a project that
        builds and then dies on its first cross-section is not archived.
      **The anchoring half is a prerequisite, not a bonus.** Bundling stores paths
      RELATIVE to the project root, and a relative source is anchored by
      `grid_spec_resolver._source_path` to `SpecBuildContext.project_root` -- which
      `Project.reopen_run` sets and `Run.reopen`/`load_run` did not, because
      `Run._context_for_build` returned `None` outright when a run had no package
      snapshot. So the same run rebuilt from a different working directory looked for
      `inputs/domain.gpkg` beside wherever the interpreter happened to be, and died on a
      raw `pyogrio.errors.DataSourceError`. A run now RECORDS its project root in its
      manifest and anchors to that. A manifest written before this simply has none, and
      behaves as it did.
      Judgment calls, each deliberate:
      - **A source marked `external=True` IS bundled**, and the flag is cleared on the
        copy. `external` means "never anchor to the project root", which was true while
        the file lived outside it and is false once a copy is inside. Asking for a bundle
        is asking for self-containment; the copy is reported rather than silent.
      - **A name already taken in `inputs/` by DIFFERENT bytes gets a digest suffix.**
        Checked against the directory, not just this call's bookkeeping: each grid is
        bundled separately and a project may be saved twice, and an in-memory map alone
        let two grids collide -- measured, two `domain.gpkg` sources landing on one file
        with the survivor answering for both.
      - **A directory source is copied whole** (`shutil.copytree`): a `.gdb` is a
        directory, and copying only its "file" bundles nothing.
      - **A missing source is reported, not fatal.** The resolver already names a missing
        source at build; refusing to save the project because one file moved would lose
        everything else it would have written.
      NOT done: no de-duplication of identical content under different names, and no size
      accounting. A bundled Ten Trails project would copy ~22 MB of vector and raster
      input beside a 9.5 GB run tree, so neither has earned its complexity yet.
      `tests/test_bundled_sources.py` (13 tests) pins the delete-the-source round trip,
      the project-relative rewrite, both tiers (library grid and a `GridSpec` inline on a
      model), that a later plain `save()` cannot undo it, the basename collision, a source
      already inside `inputs/`, a missing source, a directory source, the complete list of
      named paths, the two lazy option paths, and both anchoring cases.

257. **A model's grid guard evaporated when the project was saved and loaded (2026-09-14).**
      Phase 2 commit **A5a**. `ModelSpec.to_dict` cannot carry `context.grid`,
      `.domain` or `.surfaces`, and dropped them in SILENCE -- and every branch of
      `_discretization_complaints` (ledger 249) is gated on the context holding them.
      Measured: a model whose DISV has 16 cells against a 25-cell context grid RAISES
      live, and after `Project.save()` + `Project.load()` the same simulation **builds
      clean**. `save()` reported `skipped=()`. The per-package grid pin (ledger 250) is
      worse -- it SURVIVES the save and is then never compared, because
      `model_pin = grid_pin(None)` is `None` and the comparison loop never runs. So the
      two guards that had just landed were both undone by an ordinary save and reload.
      **Sixteen characters fix it.** `disv_pin(disv)` takes the same connectivity
      fingerprint from a BUILT DISV package that `grid_pin(grid)` takes from a grid, and
      `to_dict` records the grid's pin into `context.metadata`. With no grid object the
      guard compares the built DISV against the recorded pin. Inlining the grid stays
      refused: ledger **193** considered and refused it because it floods
      `Project.validate` and breaks `to_yaml`, and it measures ~3.3 MB per model at
      9,405 cells (grid 1.17 MB + domain 0.25 + surfaces 1.93).
      **The refusal was real but the citation was STALE, in two places.** This code and
      ledger 227 both cited "ledger 180", which ledger **194**'s renumbering had already
      moved to 193 -- and both citations were written five days AFTER that renumbering,
      so 194's "those citations moved" could not have covered them. 180 today is the
      docstring generator. Both fixed. Worth recording: the DROP itself was never a
      decision at all. It dates from an untitled bulk commit (796294e, 2026-06-17) with
      the four fields absent from day one; 193 is a later refusal-to-FIX, scoped "for
      this pass".
      **Four defects in the first version of this, all found by adversarial review
      before commit, all reproduced:**
      - **A recorded pin FROZE.** `if grid is not None and GRID_PIN not in metadata`
        meant the first pin ever written outlived its mesh: load, re-grid the model
        coherently, save -- the file still named the ORIGINAL mesh, and the model was
        then refused forever, naming a grid the project no longer contained. A present
        grid is the declaration and now always wins.
      - **`nvert` was hashed, and FloPy computes it at write time.** A DISV that leaves
        it out has `nvert.get_data() is None`, so a correct model fingerprinted
        differently from its own grid and was refused after a reload. It is out of BOTH
        payloads now; the vertex indices already carry the connectivity.
      - **The fingerprint meant "this serialization of this mesh", not "this mesh".** A
        vertex ring rotated, or wound the other way, is the same polygon -- and hashing
        the raw list made two identical meshes disagree, so the reloaded guard REFUSED
        what the live guard accepts. That is worse than a weaker check. `_canonical_ring`
        rotates to the lowest index and takes the lesser winding.
      - **The save warning overclaimed.** It said "a swapped mesh is still caught"; a
        mesh with the same connectivity and different coordinates -- a rescale, a
        mirror, a feet-to-metres conversion -- is NOT caught, because `grid_pin` hashes
        connectivity only, which is exactly what makes it frame-free (ledger 250). The
        warning and the refusal both say so now, and a test pins the blind spot. It also
        counted `(model, field)` PAIRS as model contexts.
      `SaveReport.context_dropped` records the `(model, field)` pairs, so `skipped=0`
      stops reading as "nothing was lost". The warning is emitted from `Project.save`
      rather than from `to_dict`, which is called by `validate`, by
      `_why_unserializable`, by `to_yaml` and by the save itself -- the same
      de-duplication problem ledger 227 hit with its own warning.
      NOT reported: `context.dates`. Nothing in the library reads it (`grep -rn '\.dates'
      src/myflopy/` outside the vendored tree returns zero), so losing it costs nothing
      and naming it would be noise -- the same reasoning ledger 251 gave for leaving it
      out of the frozen snapshot.
      **A5b, `LayerStack` serialization, moves to sit with B1** and is NOT in this
      commit. It has no consumer until `with_grid` must rebuild a stack on a new mesh,
      and B1 is what decides its open questions -- above all whether `default_pinch`
      rides in the recipe, since it rewrites the whole idomain and lives on the
      `build()` call, so a round-tripped stack does not determine its own arrays.
      Shipping it now would repeat the dead-code mistake the plan already declined when
      it moved `recipe`/`concrete_for` to B2.
      `tests/test_context_across_a_save.py` (17 tests) pins the fingerprint equivalence,
      the reloaded refusal and its control, the message, the re-grid case, the
      nvert-less DISV, the ring canonicalisation, the coordinate blind spot, a model
      saved before pins existed, and both halves of the drop report.
258. **`show_layer_elevs` was inert on every map but heads, and the composers named
    no drawing options at all (2026-09-14).**
    - Reported against `packages.npf.k.mosaic(logscale=True, features=[...],
      show_layer_elevs=True)`: everything drew except the elevations. Two defects,
      one behind the other, plus a third that hid both from the editor.
    - **(a) The elevations were fetched inside the heads branch.**
      `Choro._build_hover_context` built `top`/`botm` from `vor.gdf_topbtm` only
      when `self._depvar_attr is not None or self.hover_heads`. Every input,
      record and static-array noun passes `hover_heads=False`, so the flag reached
      the spec, the spec asked for surfaces, and the context had no elevations to
      hand it. The layer frame is the GRID's and has nothing to do with the mapped
      field, so it is now fetched whenever the resolved spec asks -- `_wants_surfaces()`
      -- and still ONLY then, because `gdf_topbtm` is lazy and samples rasters. A map
      with no model falls back to the frame's own width for `nlay`, since `nlay`
      dereferences `model.gwf`.
    - **(b) The surfaces-only table could never render.** `HoverSpec._effective_blocks`
      answers a surfaces request on a map with no per-layer field by appending
      `LayerTable(fields=("__surface__",), surfaces=True)` -- and `"__surface__"`
      appeared exactly ONCE in the repository, at that line. Nothing has ever
      populated it, so `LayerTable.build` returned at `if not arrays: return`.
      `LayerTable` now falls back to `_build_surfaces_only`: a `Top` row and one row
      per layer, active layer accented, the same shape as the full table minus the
      field column. Where a per-layer field DOES exist the elevations still merge
      into that table as a second column, unchanged.
    - **(c) Tier move.** `show_layer_elevs` and `hover_surfaces` left
      `LAYER_FIELD_MAP_PARAMS` for `NOUN_MAP_PARAMS`: measured live on every spatial
      noun once (a) and (b) landed, so hiding them was the defect the tier comment
      itself names. Named on 15 noun signatures and forwarded explicitly.
      `hover_layers` STAYED in Tier 2 -- it needs a per-layer FIELD, which a record
      noun does not carry, and it is still measured inert there (0 rows).
    - **(d) The composers named no drawing options.** `SpatialView.mosaic` named 11
      parameters and `animate` 9, none of them drawing options, so
      `mosaic(logscale=True, ...)` showed a caller nothing in an editor -- the
      user's actual complaint. Both now name all 23 per-panel options plus
      `backend` (34 and 32 named), with descriptions spliced from `plot.map` and
      their own `See Also`/`Examples`. Defined once on the mixin, so one signature
      serves every noun.
      - Only options the caller actually SET are forwarded, via `_explicit_options`
        (moved down from `prt_maps` to `package_plotting`, where both callers reach
        it): a default riding along would override each noun's own colour policy on
        every panel.
      - They are REFUSED, not ignored, on `kind="plot"`/`"section"`, which draw no
        choropleth (`refuse_panel_drawing_options`). The `**kwargs` tail still rides
        to the section branch, which has drawing options of its own -- which is also
        why both composers keep a tail, taking `UNDOCUMENTED_TAILS` from 15 to 17.
    - **Why (d) rotted, structurally:** `tests/test_noun_signatures.py::_discovered`
      keys on a method body that mentions `plot.map(` or `_choropleth_factory`. A
      composer's body mentions neither -- it goes through `_facet_panels` /
      `_frame_panels` -- so the whole composer tier was invisible to the 8.8
      enforcement by construction, in both directions. The file now sweeps them
      explicitly (named / documented in the SOURCE literal / forwards only what was
      set / refuses non-map kinds).
    - Compromises: the fenced splice emits no `.. end generated` marker when the
      generated block is LAST, so a composer's own `See Also`/`Examples` must sit
      BEFORE the fence in the source or the next regeneration swallows them (cost a
      round trip). `SpatialView.section` was NOT converted -- it forwards to the
      section builder, not to a choropleth, and none of these options apply.
      `mosaic(kind="section")` still passes section options through an undocumented
      tail. The PRT derived views (`travel_time`/`endpoints`/`capture`) define their
      own `map` with no `**kwargs` tail and were untouched.
    - Tests: `tests/test_hover_integration.py` (five cases: both spellings on a
      static-array map, record nouns, the head map's merged table unchanged, the
      not-fetched-unless-asked guard, and every mosaic panel) and the composer
      section of `tests/test_noun_signatures.py`.

259. **A conductivity map answered half the question (2026-09-14).**
    - Asked for directly: "when I plot k or k33, I also want to show the other in the
      hover ... not bold like k, but still there for easy reference." `npf.k.map()`
      showed the cell, `k`, the layer and the period, and nothing else.
    - The mechanism already existed one tier over. `cell_input_hover(extra_fields=)`
      renders a package's OTHER record fields under the coloured one -- reading a GHB
      map means asking "what head, against what conductance" -- and
      `StaticArrayFieldExplorer.map` already called it. It passed
      `_sibling_input_fields("npf", "k")`, which asks the package REGISTRY, and the
      registry names no input fields for an array package: the call returned `()`
      on every static-array map since the day it was written. The payload could not
      have carried them anyway -- it is built from this field's own frame.
    - So the field table that already declares what is drawable
      (`StaticArrayPackageExplorer`: `ic.strt`; `npf.k`/`k22`/`k33`; `sto.ss`/`sy`) is
      now also the declaration of what to list. The namespace passes each field its
      `siblings=`, and `_sibling_arrays(layer)` reads them at the SAME layer into the
      hover payload. Declared DOWNWARD rather than looked up, because the namespace
      owns the table and a field explorer reaching back up for it is a cycle.
    - **A sibling with no finite values is skipped, and that is measured, not
      defensive.** FloPy answers `npf.k22` with a live object on every model, and its
      `.array` is `None` on the many that never set it -- so the attribute test that
      reads correctly (`getattr(package, name, None) is None`) let `k22` through and
      the hover gained a row that was blank on all 441 cells, under a real field
      name. A row empty on every cell is the same defect as naming a parameter that
      cannot act. The canonical model is such a model, so the guard has a live
      subject in the suite rather than a synthetic one.
    - Deliberately NOT done: no k/k33 special case (`sto.ss` gets `sy` from the same
      rule, and `ic.strt` correctly gets nothing); no ratio row (a K:K33 anisotropy
      line is a derived quantity and a different request); the siblings are NOT
      offered as a parameter, because the field table is the declaration and a
      per-call override has no caller yet. `_sibling_input_fields` stays as it is --
      it is the list-package path and remains correct there.
    - Cost: one extra array read per sibling per map, from FloPy's in-memory package.
      No raster sampling, unlike the layer elevations in ledger 258.
    - Tests: `tests/test_hover_integration.py` -- the pair both ways with the
      sibling's own values checked against the array, the bold/plain styling the
      request named, the unset-`k22` skip, `sto`, and `ic.strt` unchanged.

260. **A surfaces-only elevation table pushed a map's own values out of sight
    (2026-09-14).**
    - Reported the same day as 259: with `show_layer_elevs=True`, `k33` rendered
      BELOW the five-row elevation table rather than beside `k`. "The k and k33
      values should be together."
    - `HoverSpec._effective_blocks` PREPENDED whichever `LayerTable` it synthesized,
      ahead of the spec's own blocks. For a head map that is right -- the table is
      the primary value read across the layers, so it belongs against the value it
      elaborates. For a surfaces-only table it is not: that table carries no reading
      of the mapped field at all. It is the grid's layer frame, context of the same
      kind as the `layer` row beside it, and going first it separated a value from
      its own siblings by five rows.
    - So the two cases now differ, on the distinction that was already there and
      unused: a per-layer table OF THE PRIMARY stays first; a surfaces-only table is
      appended last, after the spec's own blocks and before the footer. The head
      hover is byte-identical; only maps that carry no per-layer field move.
    - Not done: no per-block ordering knob on `HoverSpec`. The two positions follow
      from what the block IS, and a spec that has to be told where its own context
      goes has moved the decision to every caller.
    - Test: `test_the_sibling_sits_with_the_value_even_when_elevations_are_shown`
      pins the adjacency and that the elevations still follow.

261. **The xugrid export carried no layer elevations (2026-09-14).**
    - Asked: "can I export to xugrid and have all layer elevations attached to show
      in QGIS?" Measured first, and the answer was no on both halves.
      `model.to_xugrid()` returned the head field alone, and nothing anywhere in the
      export path read `gdf_topbtm`. The elevations could be attached by hand
      through `vor.to_xugrid({...})`, which is what this entry turns into a
      parameter.
    - `to_xugrid(surfaces=True)` on `VoronoiGridPlus`, `HeadsPlus` and
      `SimulationBase` now attaches the layer frame, built by a new
      `VoronoiGridPlus.layer_surface_fields()`: `top` and `botm_1` ... `botm_n`,
      read positionally from the geometry-first `gdf_topbtm` (column 1 is the top,
      `2 + n` the bottom of layer n -- the convention the hover and the cross
      sections already use, and the one that survives the two different column
      NAMINGS `attach_to_grid()` and `LayerStack.to_disv()` publish).
    - **One variable PER LAYER, and that shape is the whole point.** A mesh dataset
      in QGIS is one value per face (optionally per time), so a variable still
      carrying a `layer` dimension has no place in that data model -- and QGIS drops
      it SILENTLY. Measured through the QGIS 4.2.2 Python bindings on the
      development machine, loading the written NetCDF through MDAL: a `(nlay, ncpl)`
      `botm` produced a valid mesh layer with NO elevation datasets listed at all,
      while the flattened form listed `top` and every `botm_<n>` as face datasets
      with the CRS carried. The same run retired a guess worth recording: the UGRID
      `location="face"` / `mesh=` attributes, which xugrid does not write on these
      variables, turn out NOT to matter -- MDAL matches on the face dimension, and
      tagging them by hand changed nothing.
    - **The field is still layered, deliberately.** `surfaces=True` does not reshape
      the heads: `(time, layer, cell)` is what differencing and aggregation want.
      For QGIS the documented recipe is one call --
      `model.to_xugrid(surfaces=True).isel(time=-1, layer=0)` -- which flattens the
      field and cannot touch the elevations, since they carry neither dimension.
      Verified in QGIS: head plus all five elevation datasets.
    - Compromises and deliberate omissions:
      - `surfaces=True` changes the RETURN TYPE to `UgridDataset` (from
        `UgridDataArray` for a single field). Unavoidable -- there is more than one
        variable -- and documented on all three methods; the default is untouched,
        so no existing call changes shape.
      - An explicit `data` entry WINS over a derived surface of the same name,
        rather than raising on the collision: explicit beats derived, and a caller
        passing their own `top` means it.
      - A grid with no surfaces RAISES rather than returning a quietly emptier
        file -- the caller asked for something that is not there.
      - QGIS also lists `mesh2d_nFaces`, the face-index coordinate, as a spurious
        dataset group. That is xugrid's writer and MDAL's reader between them; not
        worth a myflopy workaround.
      - No GeoPackage export verb was added. Cell polygons plus elevation columns
        already open in QGIS as an ordinary vector layer (verified, 441 features,
        every attribute visible) and that is three lines of GeoPandas; a verb for it
        would be a second way to do something the grammar does not own.
    - Tests: `tests/test_to_xugrid.py` -- the flat shape and the declared
      thicknesses (so a transposed or reversed frame fails), the refusal with no
      surfaces, the Dataset return, the explicit-value precedence, the model-level
      export, and the `isel` round trip through NetCDF.

262. **The xugrid export could not be profiled in QGIS at all, whatever the settings
    (2026-09-14).**
    - Follow-up to 261, and the reason it was only half an answer. Reported: "I
      can't figure out what to choose [in the Elevation tab] to make the layer show
      on the profile as an elevation. Right now it just plots a flat line at zero."
    - **No setting could have worked, and that is measured.** A QGIS mesh layer
      takes its elevation from the mesh VERTEX Z. The UGRID file declares
      `node_coordinates = "mesh2d_node_x mesh2d_node_y"` -- X and Y, no Z -- so
      every vertex sits at zero. Profiling the exported mesh through the QGIS 4.2.2
      bindings returned 102 samples, all `0.00`: exactly the reported line. And
      `Qgis.MeshElevationMode` offers only `FixedElevationRange`, `FromVertices`
      (the default) and `FixedRangePerGroup` -- none of which reads a dataset
      group, so the `top`/`botm_n` datasets 261 attaches can colour a mesh but can
      never raise it. Ledger 261 stands for interchange; it does not deliver a
      profile.
    - `VoronoiGridPlus.to_gpkg(path, data=None, surfaces=False, layer="cells")` is
      the answer: a flat `cells` layer carrying any per-cell values, plus -- with
      `surfaces=True` -- one GeoPackage layer PER SURFACE whose geometry carries
      that surface's elevation as **Z**. Measured on the written file: all five
      surfaces profiled, in order (`top` 101.27-146.19 down to `botm_4`
      1.27-46.19), with **one** setting changed, `Clamping: Absolute`. The
      attribute-driven alternative (`Clamping` + `Binding` + a data-defined
      `ZOffset` expression) profiles identically and needs three settings and an
      expression per layer, so the Z is baked into the geometry instead.
    - One layer per surface, not one layer with a surface column, because elevation
      in QGIS is a per-LAYER property: several surfaces on one profile means
      several map layers. The flat `cells` layer still carries every surface as a
      COLUMN, for labelling and queries.
    - The surfaces are resolved BEFORE the first write, so a grid without them
      raises with nothing written rather than leaving a GeoPackage holding `cells`
      and none of what was asked for (asserted).
    - Deliberately NOT done, each measured or reasoned:
      - **No raster export.** QGIS profiles an elevation raster natively and that
        is the conventional route, but rasterising a Voronoi field is a resolution
        choice myflopy would have to invent, and the vector route needs no
        resampling. (`Surface.resolve_source()` already hands back the GeoTIFF for a
        raster- or contour-backed `mf.Surface`, which covers the case where a real
        raster exists.) Recorded as the one open alternative.
      - **No model-level `to_gpkg`.** `data=` composes: `vor.to_gpkg(p,
        data={"head": model.hds.array(layer=0)}, surfaces=True)`. A second entry
        point would own the same decision twice.
      - **No Z on the `cells` layer.** It is the flat plan-view layer; giving it Z
        would make one layer answer two questions.
    - Not established: whether an elevation RASTER profiles in this headless
      harness. `QgsRasterLayer.createProfileGenerator(...).generateProfile()`
      returned True and zero samples for a valid raster that samples correctly at a
      point, under both elevation modes. Treated as a limitation of driving the
      profile API without a map canvas, NOT as a claim about QGIS, and left out of
      the docs rather than asserted either way.
    - Tests: `tests/test_grid_gpkg_export.py` -- the plain layer, data columns and
      their length check, the Z on every surface layer matching its attribute, the
      declared thicknesses (so a scrambled or reversed frame fails), the surface
      columns on `cells`, the nothing-written refusal, the layer name, and a
      created parent directory.

263. **Every test grid was the one shape that hid the bug, so three commits shipped broken (2026-09-14).**
      `_json_value` passes `str`, `int`, `float` and `bool` and raises on everything
      else. `numpy.float64` **subclasses** `float`, so a grid's coordinates sailed
      through; `numpy.int64` does **not** subclass `int`, so its vertex indices raised.
      flopy's own `VoronoiGrid` emits exactly that mix -- measured on one cell:
      `['int', 'float64', 'float64', 'int', 'int64', 'int', 'int', 'int', 'int64']`.
      So on a grid a user actually builds, `SimulationSpec.to_dict()` raised, the
      manifest wrote `spec_recipe=None`, `freeze_simulation` died at its own
      `lifted.to_dict()`, `Run._freeze` swallowed that as a warning, `run.frozen` was
      `None`, and reopening the run raised "neither a rebuildable recipe nor a frozen
      snapshot" -- while the run itself executed under **Normal termination**.
      **Ledger 251 therefore did not do what it says on any real model**, and 249, 256
      and 257 were all validated against a grid that could not exhibit the failure.
      That entry is amended below rather than left standing.
      **The cause was the FIXTURE, not the feature.** `rectangular_voronoi` is the grid
      behind essentially every test in the suite, and its cell2d vertex indices are all
      python `int`, which is the one shape that cannot show this. 3,315 tests passed
      while the thing they were written to prove did not work outside them.
      **AMENDED 2026-09-14 (entry 265), because the mechanism above was stated without
      being measured and is wrong.** As first written this entry said the fixture
      "hand-builds its `iverts` from python `range` objects, so every cell is a plain
      `int` and every cell has the same width". Measured: `rectangular_voronoi` calls
      `irregular_voronoi_grid` (`modflow/mf6/canonical.py:327`), which runs a **real
      `scipy.spatial.Voronoi`** clipped to a box -- no `range` anywhere in it -- and its
      cells are **not** uniform. At 4x4 it is ncpl 16 with vertex counts `{4,5,6,7}`, 16
      distinct areas from 5,458 to 14,055, and bbox widths from 59.0 to 157.3;
      `canonical.py:132` raises if the cells ever ARE uniform. The **only** property that
      separates the two grids is the vertex-index dtype: 82 python `int` against the
      triangulated grid's 114 `numpy.int64` + 36 `int`. Raggedness was never the
      discriminator, so any test asserting it is asserting something both grids satisfy.
      - `tests/conftest.py` gains **`triangulated_grid`**, a session-scoped grid built
        through `GridSpec.voronoi` the way a model is. `tests/test_real_grid_round_trip.py`
        runs serialization, freeze, reopen, fingerprinting and save/load against it.
        **Five of its seven tests fail with this fix reverted.**
      - `test_the_fixture_really_is_the_awkward_shape` asserts the fixture still yields
        numpy ints AND cells of differing widths. Without it a future flopy release
        could normalise its output and turn the whole module back into a duplicate of
        the canonical-grid tests, silently.
      **The fix is one clause, and it is a correction rather than an accommodation.** A
      numpy scalar IS a number; whether one reached the raise was an accident of
      subclassing, which the float64/int64 asymmetry proves. `_json_value` now converts
      any 0-d value exposing `.item()` -- the scalar protocol -- and recurses, so
      `int64`, `float32`, `bool_` and a 0-d array all land as true Python primitives.
      No numpy import was needed and no other refusal was relaxed: an ndarray still
      raises, which is what ledger 193's refusal is about.
      **What this says about the rest of the work.** Every guard, pin and snapshot added
      in 249-257 was measured against one grid shape. The lesson is not "add a fixture"
      but that a test fixture is an ASSUMPTION, and this one was load-bearing and
      unstated. Anything that serializes, fingerprints or freezes a grid is now expected
      to run against `triangulated_grid` too.

264. **The guards told the truth only in the circumstances they were tested in (2026-09-14).**
      A repair pass over ledgers 249-257, prompted by an audit. Four defects, one
      extraction, three false claims.
      - **A failed freeze was completely silent.** `_logging` attaches a `NullHandler` to
        the `myflopy` root, which suppresses Python's fallback stderr handler -- so a
        library `logger.warning()` prints **nothing** unless the application configured
        logging. `Run._freeze` caught everything and logged at WARNING, so a run whose
        snapshot failed reported `status="built"`, `frozen=None`, and said nothing --
        while `prepare_run` had already announced the run was rebuildable from it. That
        is the mechanism that hid ledger 263's bug through five commits. It now also
        `warnings.warn`s, the channel `_warn_artifact_versions` already used for exactly
        this reason.
      - **The guard still evaporated LIVE.** Ledger 257 closed the save/load path. A model
        whose context has no grid AND no recorded pin -- `mf.gwf(name, packages=[...])`,
        which this repo's own examples use -- still left `model_pin` as `None`, so the
        package-pin loop never ran: a CHD resolved on a 4x4 grid BUILT CLEAN on an 8x8
        model. The built DISV answers for the mesh when the context cannot.
        **The fix was made wrong first, and that is worth recording**: taking the DISV's
        fingerprint BEFORE the recorded pin makes it agree with itself and silently
        disabled 257's reload check, while every other test still passed. Three tests
        now fail on that ordering.
      - **Eleven of eighteen grid-bound helpers carried no pin.** Ledger 250 claimed it
        closed the gap "for every package the library resolved itself"; it closed it for
        the seven `.gpkg` forms. Measured: `mf.rch(context=)` resolves per-cell records
        through `RCHBuilder`, and built on a 36-cell grid put recharge on **the wrong 16
        cells with MF6 running to completion**. `pin_metadata(context)` is now the one
        place a builder stamps its mesh, spread into the existing `with_metadata` calls
        in `uzf.py`, `sfr.py` and `areal.py` (rch/evt, LIST form).
        **AMENDED 2026-09-15: "list and array forms" was wrong, and measured wrong the
        way the rest of this entry warns about -- read, not run.** `mf.rch.array` does
        not go through `areal.py` at all; it reaches `advanced.py::_array_bc_spec`, which
        stamps nothing. Measured on a 100-cell grid: `mf.rch.array(recharge=0.001,
        context=ctx)` returns a spec whose `irch` is a per-cell `(100,)` array derived
        from the context's DOMAIN -- genuinely grid-bound -- and whose metadata carries
        no `GRID_PIN`. So a same-`ncpl` mesh swap still applies the wrong per-cell layer
        indices, which is precisely the gap this bullet claims to have closed. Scoped
        into B1.
        NOT pinned, with reasons: `mf.hfb` is FACE-indexed -- its records are cell PAIRS
        and it has no cellid column -- and `mf.mvr` carries package names and indices
        rather than cells and holds no context at all. Both need the symbolic form the
        plan already names, which is separate work.
      - **Three claims were false.** The build guard does not compare `context.surfaces`
        (removed during 249's own review, for want of a "rows are cells" invariant) --
        CLAUDE.md said it did. The pin does not hash the vertex count (257 removed it,
        because FloPy computes `NVERT` at write time) -- ledger 250, CLAUDE.md and
        `grid_pin`'s own docstring all said it did. And 250's scope claim above. All
        corrected in place.
      - **`myflopy/grid_identity.py`**, extracted from `specs.py` unchanged: the ten mesh
        functions plus `GRID_PIN` and `DROPPED_CONTEXT_FIELDS`, 362 lines that referenced
        exactly three names from the rest of the file, two of which they owned.
        `specs.py` had grown 3,293 -> 3,913 lines in four days against its own docstring
        promising "intentionally small" spec classes; it is 3,568 now. Everything is
        re-exported from `specs`, so no caller changed.
      **What the audit said about HOW this happened, which is the part worth keeping:**
      `_json_value` was written 120 lines below a `_canonical` that already handled numpy
      scalars correctly and whose docstring names the exact hazard, and three more
      normalizers elsewhere in `src/` were already right. The failure was not sprawl but
      new code not consulting what the file already knew. Grep for an existing helper
      before writing one; test a claim before writing it down.

265. **The fixture rule from 263 named the wrong property, and six numpy defects were sitting behind it (2026-09-14).**
      Ledger 263 concluded "use a real grid fixture" and 264 acted on it. Measuring the
      two grids before adopting the fixture across ~15 modules showed the rule's stated
      reason was **false**: `rectangular_voronoi` is a real SciPy Voronoi with ragged,
      unequal cells (ncpl 16, vertex counts `{4,5,6,7}`, 16 distinct widths from 59.0 to
      157.3 ft), not a `range`-built uniform mesh. The **only** property it cannot show
      is the vertex-index dtype. 263 is amended above; the same false mechanism was
      corrected in CLAUDE.md, `tests/conftest.py`, `test_real_grid_round_trip.py` and the
      session memory. A rule with a false reason is worse than no rule: it sends the next
      reader hunting raggedness bugs that do not exist.
      - **The wide adoption was NOT done, and the reason is measured.** Substituting a
        real grid across the four boundary modules broke 19 tests, every one of them a
        hardcoded cell count or a test whose subject IS two different meshes -- not a
        library failure. Worse, in `test_context_across_a_save.py` two tests go
        **silently vacuous** rather than failing, which is the exact failure mode this
        exercise exists to prevent. `test_build_grid_consistency.py`'s literal counts are
        what make its error messages readable, and they would have to go.
        Instead: a second real fixture (`triangulated_grid_finer`, ncpl 92, ~0.2 s) and
        four targeted tests in the module that already owns this -- the refusing
        direction of the pin across two real meshes, a renumbering on ragged rings, and a
        freeze/thaw that must write byte-identical MF6 input AND hand back the same
        vertices. Both halves, because the first does not imply the second and the first
        draft claimed it did: a DISV spec carries its own `vertices`/`cell2d` as package
        options, so **every vertex in the snapshot's grid block can be shifted a full
        foot and the written files are identical**. `grid_pin` cannot stand in for the
        missing half either -- it is connectivity-only by design (ledger 250), so it is
        blind to a vertex that moved. The mutation profile is the evidence: rounding the
        frozen vertices to whole feet, casting them to float32 and shifting them by 1e-3
        all survived the file comparison and all fail the added one.
      - **`tests/test_numpy_at_the_boundary.py` is the stronger guard.** Most of it needs
        no grid -- two of its tests take the real-grid fixture, for the freeze cases --
        and that is exactly why it finds what a grid fixture cannot: of the ten defects
        below, one is reachable through a mesh. Push the types through the boundary
        directly.
      **Six live defects, each reproduced before being fixed and each killed by mutation:**
      - **`to_yaml` raised for every model carrying a DISV.** `_json_value` returned
        `np.float64` and `np.str_` UNCONVERTED, because both subclass a type the
        primitive check accepts -- so 263 fixed the half that raised and left the half
        that did not. `json.dumps` accepts them; PyYAML dispatches on the exact type and
        does not. `SimulationSpec.to_yaml()` is a documented API with its own example
        directory, and `tests/test_specs_io.py` never built a DISV, so nothing looked.
      - **A package with numpy boundnames reported EDITED after a plain save/load.**
        `np.str_` IS a `numpy.generic`, so `_canonical` returned from its numpy branch
        and never reached the interning ledger 222 added -- and `np.unique` on a
        boundname column is how a GeoPackage produces one. `project.runs.drift()` reads
        those digests. **No stored run looks disturbed by the fix**, with the evidence
        stated honestly: every digest is byte-identical before and after across npf
        (scalar and array), chd with python boundnames, ic, oc and tdis, and the ONE real
        checked-in digest in the repo (`examples/mf6/variant_workflow/.../run.json`,
        `npf/high_k`) recomputes unchanged -- 13 of the 14 manifests on disk record no
        digest at all, so that is a sample of one, not a survey. Only a package that
        actually carries a `np.str_` or a 0-d array moves, and those were already
        reporting drift, which is the bug.
      - **`_canonical` and `_json_value` disagreed about a 0-d `ndarray`** (one
        normalized it, one did not), so the value changed across a save on its own.
      - **An object-dtype `context.domain` froze "successfully" and made the WHOLE
        snapshot unreadable** -- every package in it -- with `frozen_summary` reporting
        `readable: False` and no cause. `ModelContext.domain` is typed `Any` and
        validated nowhere, so a `LayerBuildResult` passed instead of its `.idomain`
        reaches `np.asarray`. It was the one write into the store with neither guard.
      - **A thawed run could not resolve a surface.** `_surfaces_block` stringified the
        elevation table's integer column labels and never restored them, so `[0, 1, 2]`
        came back `['0', '1', '2']` and the first `CellSurfaceOffset`/SFR/LAK read died
        -- the one failure that block exists to prevent.
      - **Two loud-but-wrong failures:** `_json_value` recursed forever on
        `np.longdouble` (whose `.item()` returns its own type) instead of raising its own
        message, and `PackageSpec.to_dict` wrote `enabled` raw, so a `np.bool_` there
        produced "Object of type bool is not JSON serializable" -- numpy 2's name for its
        own type, which sends you looking at the wrong one.
      **Four more, found only because the first six were reviewed -- the boundary is
      wider than the function.** Fixing `_json_value` helps a value that REACHES it:
      - **A source spec was handed to its own `to_dict`, unrecursed** -- the FIRST branch
        of `_json_value`, above every normalization, and a source writes its fields raw.
        `PackageSpec.inputs` is where source specs live. Measured: `Project.validate()`
        returned `[]` and `Project.save()` then died inside `json.dumps` having already
        written the project and simulation files, so the next `Project.load` raised
        `FileNotFoundError` on a package it never reached.
      - **`_spec_summary` wrote both metadata dicts into `run.json` raw**, by a path that
        never calls `PackageSpec.to_dict`. `spec.with_metadata(calibrated=np.True_)` or a
        context metadata value read from a table made `prepare_run` raise outright.
      - **`GridSpec.to_dict` emitted `crs` raw** and called `source.to_dict()` directly.
        `crs` documents itself as taking `2927` as well as `"EPSG:2927"`, and pandas hands
        back `numpy.int64` for an integer column, so a CRS read from a config table is the
        ordinary producer.
      - **The `enabled` fix above CREATED a defect, and this is the one worth reading.**
        `package_digest` read `name`, `enabled` and `requires` raw while `from_dict`
        normalizes them, so a `np.bool_` `enabled` digested one way live and another after
        a save -- a package nobody touched, reported EDITED by `runs.drift()`, forever.
        Before that fix the package could not be SAVED at all, so the fix is precisely
        what turned a loud failure into a silent permanent one. Every digest field goes
        through `_canonical` now. `np.bool_` is what any numpy predicate returns
        (`arr.any()`, `mask[i]`, a comparison), so this needed no unusual input.
      NOT fixed, and the reachability is the reason -- measured after the fact, because
      the first version of this paragraph implied it was live. `_canonical` has no
      source-spec branch, so a numpy value inside one drifts the digest. But **nothing in
      the library puts a source spec in `PackageSpec.inputs`**: every GIS helper resolves
      EAGERLY and stores records, so `mf.chd.gpkg(...)` measures `inputs == {}`, and
      `mf.npf(k=<np.float64 from a pandas cell>)` stores the value directly and digests
      stable across a save. The only way to reach it is to hand-build a `PackageSpec` with
      an `inputs=` source, which no test, example or notebook does. So it is LATENT, not
      live. It also cannot be fixed cheaply: canonicalizing the source through `to_dict()`
      moves the digest of ORDINARY python-valued sources too (`73373803492f3890` ->
      `8c7fe2ba2a5d59d7`), reporting every stored source-bearing run as drifted on the day
      it landed. Worth fixing when lazy package resolution lands (Phase 2 B1) and
      `inputs` starts carrying sources for real; not worth a migration before then.

      **Ledger and CLAUDE.md hygiene, in the same pass.** The ledger was 9,677 lines at
      the previous commit, 48.4% of `docs/*.md`, and its own preamble prescribed
      `What:`/`Why:`/`Impact:` fields that **42 of entries 1-132 and none of 133-264**
      carry; the preamble now states the form the entries actually have. Entries have
      doubled in length (22.1 lines each for 1-132, 50.9 for 133-264) and the growth is
      bug narrative, which belongs in the commit message -- so the preamble says what an
      entry is for. NOT done: no renumbering and no retroactive trimming.
      `scripts/derive_ledger_index.py` generates the index (265 entries over 266 rows --
      entry 42 is listed twice, once struck, which is the resolution convention) and
      `tests/test_ledger_format.py` checks the shape, the numbering, the index's currency,
      that every title closes its bold, and that every citation resolves -- that last
      check is what caught this entry missing while five files already cited it.
      **Every figure in this paragraph is the SECOND one measured, and that is the
      entry's own lesson landing on the entry.** The first pass wrote "1,527 citations,
      153 distinct, across `src/`, `tests/`, the notebooks and CLAUDE.md". All of it was
      wrong. The sweep was an `rglob` that also read the three stale repo copies under
      `.claude/worktrees/` -- **62% of the occurrences** -- so the count was neither
      reproducible nor about this repository; the regex missed the plural `ledgers N` and
      every range `ledger N-M`, 25 citations including entry 264's own; and the notebooks
      contain **no** ledger citation at all while `docs/` is the largest contributor and
      went unnamed. Over tracked files it is **689 occurrences naming 159 entries**, all
      resolving, and the test sweeps `git ls-files` now. Four more defects in the same
      hygiene code, all found by review rather than by use: the index generator raised
      `TypeError` on the documented resolution shape (sorting a `None` date against a
      string), counted rows as entries, and cut three titles mid-code-span; and the
      anti-vacuity guard was itself vacuous -- a sweep narrowed to `docs/` alone passed
      it while silently no longer checking `src/`.

266. **Two of the tests written for 265 certified the fix instead of checking it, and both byte-identical comparisons carried a wall clock (2026-09-14).**
      A completeness pass over the previous commit, which is the only reason any of this
      was found: every fix in 265 is killed by a named test, and that was verified by
      reverting all sixteen. What follows is what no test covered.
      - **The timestamp filter was inert, in the one place it was written and absent in
        the other.** FloPy stamps `# File generated by Flopy version 3.10.0 on
        09/14/2026 at 22:35:11.` into line 1 of every package file. `_body` in
        `test_frozen_runs.py` filtered `"created on"` -- a substring that header does not
        contain -- so it dropped **0 lines of 0 files**, while its own docstring said it
        existed because whole-file comparison is flaky. The new test in 265 did not
        attempt the strip at all. Measured failure rate **1.1% and 1.8% per run** on an
        idle box, higher under `-n 10`, and both fail accusing the freeze/thaw
        serialization, which is a false lead. Deterministic proof: two writes 1.1 s
        apart differ raw and are equal stripped. There is ONE helper now, the `mf6_body`
        fixture, matching the string FloPy actually writes.
        **This also explains a failure I had already explained away.** Six tests failed
        once mid-session and I attributed it to reading a file mid-write, which was a
        guess and was wrong. An unexplained failure is a finding, not noise.
      - **`test_a_package_with_numpy_boundnames_digests_as_one_with_python_ones` passed
        with its fix entirely reverted.** The defect is a missing pickle BACK-REFERENCE,
        which appears only when one object REPEATS; the test used each name once. It uses
        the same name twice now, and fails by name when reverted.
      - **`test_a_project_with_a_numpy_valued_source_saves_and_reloads` passed too**,
        because the new `TypeError` fallback silently pickled the package instead -- and
        a reload still returns something, so `is not None` could not tell a correct JSON
        save from a pickle. It asserts `report.pickled == 0` now.
      - **That fallback was the one change in 265 with no test anywhere.** Reverting it
        left every module green. It has one now, with the failure INJECTED, because the
        numpy routes into it are closed -- a safety net nothing can reach is still worth
        knowing works.
      **Where the coverage actually sits, measured, and left as it is:** of sixteen
      reverts, fourteen are caught only by `tests/test_numpy_at_the_boundary.py` and one
      by nothing outside it. That is not a defect -- it is one subject in one module --
      but a `-k` exclusion or a rename of that file silently unguards ten of eleven

267. **Three grid-bound helpers changed mesh in silence, and two ledger entries said they did not (2026-09-15).**
      B1 commit 1. Ledger 250 stamped the seven `.gpkg` forms and reported the gap closed
      "for every package the library resolved itself"; ledger 264 corrected that, stamped
      `uzf`/`sfr`/`rch`/`evt` and reported it closed again. Scoping B1 by BUILDING each
      helper and reading its metadata -- rather than reading the source, which is how both
      entries went wrong -- found three still unpinned:
      - **`mf.lak` and `mf.hfb` BUILD CLEAN on the wrong mesh.** Measured: declared on a
        28-cell grid, built on a 92-cell one, no refusal and no warning. Neither is caught
        by the range check, for different reasons. LAK's cellids live in
        `connectiondata`, which `_cellids_in` deliberately refuses to walk (a cellid sits
        at a different index per package -- SFR's `packagedata[1]` is a cellid, LAK's is a
        stage), so it finds **zero** cellids to range-check. HFB's it does find -- 10 in a
        5-segment barrier -- but every one of them is still IN RANGE on a larger mesh,
        which is the exact gap the pin exists for (ledger 250).
      - **`mf.rch.array`/`mf.evt.array` reach `advanced.py::_array_bc_spec`, not the
        `areal.py` funnel 264 named**, so the array form was never pinned. A DIFFERENT
        `ncpl` already raised, but as FloPy's `MFDataException ... Expected data
        dimensions`, which fires while the package is still building and so beats the
        guard to it -- loud and unhelpful. A SAME-`ncpl` swap said nothing and applied the
        wrong per-cell layer indices.
      **The array pin is CONDITIONAL, and that is the design decision worth recording.**
      It is decided on the resolved PAYLOAD -- does any option hold a per-column array --
      not on whether a `context=` was passed. `mf.rch.array(recharge=0.001, irch=0)`
      resolves to two scalars, means the same thing on any mesh, and must stay MOVABLE;
      pinning on the presence of a context would refuse that correct move. The default
      `irch="top_active"` resolves to an `(ncpl,)` array derived from the domain and is
      pinned, as is a per-column `recharge`. A mutant that pins unconditionally is killed
      by its own test.
      **`pin_metadata`'s docstring contradicted `_cellids_in`'s, eight lines apart.** It
      said HFB "is FACE-indexed -- its records are cell PAIRS and it has no cellid column"
      and needed a symbolic form; `_cellids_in` said it reads "two for an HFB ... what lets
      a stale barrier be caught on either side". The second is right, measured. Corrected.
      `mf.mvr` genuinely still carries none -- it names packages and record indices rather
      than cells, and holds no context at all.
      **The guard against a fourth round is a both-directions coverage test**
      (`tests/test_grid_pin.py`): it BUILDS every grid-bound helper on a real mesh and
      compares the set that pins against the set that resolves cell numbers, so adding a
      helper without a pin fails, and so does leaving a stale entry behind. Reading the
      source twice produced two wrong ledger entries; building the thing found it in one
      pass.
      NOT done here: improving FloPy's `MFDataException` on a different-`ncpl` array
      package. It is loud rather than silent, and reordering the guard to precede package
      construction is its own change.

268. **Two coupled models on different meshes built, ran, and said nothing (2026-09-15).**
      B1 commit 2. Measured: a GWF on a 3x2 Voronoi and a GWT on a 2x3, both `ncpl=6`,
      joined by `mf.exchange` -- built clean, zero warnings, and the concentration field
      is wrong. The grid pins differ; nothing compared siblings.
      `_discretization_complaints` validates each model against its OWN context and never
      looks across an exchange, and `replace_grid("flow", ...)` leaves the GWT's grid and
      the exchange untouched, so the ordinary way to reach this state is a half-finished
      grid move -- which is exactly what B1 is building.
      **MF6 agrees it is an error and cannot see it**, which is the part worth recording.
      `exg-gwfgwt.f90:224` terminates on a node-count mismatch (`nodes`/`nodesuser`) and
      `:239-255` on an idomain mismatch, per DIS type. It compares **counts and idomain
      only, never geometry** -- so a mesh of the same size with the same idomain passes
      both of its checks, and MF6 then maps node-for-node BY INDEX onto the wrong
      geometry. myflopy's pin is connectivity, so it sees what MF6 cannot.
      Scoped to the three exchanges MF6 requires to share a discretization: `gwfgwt`,
      `gwfgwe`, `gwfprt`. **`gwfgwf` is deliberately excluded** -- coupling a coarse model
      to a fine one is what that exchange is FOR, and `package_api`'s own docstring
      example is a coarse/fine pair. A mutant that includes it is killed.
      **DISV only.** The check is `disv_pin`, a DISV connectivity hash, so a structured
      pair is not compared and MF6's node-count check is all that stands behind it -- with
      the same blind spot. Not closed here: a DIS geometry hash is its own piece of work
      and this repo's models are Voronoi.
      The refusal names the exchange, both models and both pins, because "something is
      wrong" is not actionable. It is raised BEFORE the exchanges are built, since the
      failure it prevents is one MF6 would accept and run.

269. **A layer stack could not be written down, so no layered model could be SAVED (2026-09-15).**
      B1 commit 3, and the one that explains why B1 is bigger than "enable a grid move".
      Measured before it: `mf.disv(result)` holds the RESOLVED `top`/`botm`/`idomain`
      arrays, `to_dict` refuses an ndarray (ledger 193), so `Project.validate()` reported
      `"Simulation 's' is not serializable"`, `Project.save()` persisted **0 simulations**
      -- naming the skip in `SaveReport.skipped`, so honest rather than silent -- and
      `Project.load()` returned an EMPTY project. That is every layered model, which is
      the canonical way to build one here.
      `Surface`, `_Layer` and `LayerStack` gain tagged `to_dict`/`from_dict`, plus one arm
      each side of the spec serializer. The payload is the DECLARATION: the top surface,
      each unit's surface and its `min_thickness`/`pinch`/`split`/`names`, and the units.
      NOT carried: `vor` (a grid cannot be inlined, and a stack is declarable without one)
      and `_draft` (a cached preview grid).
      **The token is `$layer_stack`/`$surface`, not a `kind` tag, and that is not
      cosmetic.** `Surface` HAS a `kind` field of its own -- `"flat"`, `"raster"`,
      `"shift"` -- and `_spec_value` dispatches source specs on `kind`. Tagging a surface
      as `{"kind": "flat"}` makes it fall through every arm and come back a PLAIN DICT:
      no error, just a different object. The `$`-prefixed token follows `$tuple`/`$npz`.
      Duck-typed on a class attribute rather than imported, because `specs` is import
      layer 1 and `layers` is layer 6; revival uses a lazy import for the same reason.
      **`Surface.from_array` and `from_points` are REFUSED by name**, since their content
      is per-cell data and inlining arrays is exactly what ledger 193 refused (~3.3 MB per
      model at 9,405 cells). Refusing beats degrading: a stack that quietly dropped an
      array surface would round-trip into a DIFFERENT model. They stay usable; they just
      cannot be written down, which is what the run's frozen snapshot is for.
      **A stack does NOT determine its own arrays**, so this payload is a recipe and not a
      result: `reconcile`, `min_sep`, `trigger_sep` and `method` live on the
      `build()`/`to_disv()` call and move the answer, and `LayerBuildResult` has no field
