      for any of them. Commit 4 forwards all eight of `to_disv`'s build kwargs through
      `mf.disv` for exactly this reason -- the user settled it 2026-09-15.
      NOT closed here: this commit alone does not make a layered model saveable, because
      `mf.disv` still holds arrays. Commit 4 is what closes it.
      **Amended 2026-09-25: a tuple inside a token's payload comes back a tuple.**
      `_json_value` tags every tuple as `{"$tuple": [...]}`, inside a `$layer_stack`/
      `$surface`/`$spread`/`$cell_surface_offset` payload too, and `_spec_value` handed
      the payload to `from_dict` raw. A `split=(0.3, 0.7)` came back a dict and the saved
      stack would not build; a per-period `mf.Spread(("c0", "c1"))` in a lazy `.gpkg`
      boundary came back `field={'$tuple': [...]}` and the reloaded package died at
      build with `KeyError: 0` (live: 10.0 and 20.0 per period). Every payload is now
      `_untag_tuples`-ed first -- ONLY the tag, not the rest of `_spec_value`, whose
      source revival and integer-key promotion must not reach an object's own format.
      Both cases are tested through JSON and YAML (the Spread one only on review: the
      line that fixed it was tested by nothing). Same pass: `Surface.from_contours`
      kept `region_vector`/`region_raster` as the `str` it was given while `from_dict`
      revives a `Path`, so a round-tripped contour surface compared `!=` with an
      identical payload and digest; both are stored as `Path` now. That can move a
      digest only for a path `Path()` rewrites (`"./d.gpkg"` -> `"d.gpkg"`) of a file
      that could not be hashed, and a reload already rewrote it the same way; no
      manifest on disk names a region file (0 under `examples/` and the model tree).
      **Found and NOT changed** (the user's call): a ONE-SIDED `Surface.clamp(a,
      lower=b)` -- and `a.between(lower=b)` -- cannot be written down at all:
      `to_dict` calls `.to_dict()` on the `None` bound and raises `AttributeError`, so
      a gridless stack holding one cannot be declared through `mf.disv` (the error is
      raised at the call, not in silence; measured on myflopy at 90de983 too). And a
      `grass_kwargs` name `ContourSurfaceInterpolator` does not take is accepted by
      `from_contours` and refused only at the first resolution (`TypeError`).

270. **The discretization is a recipe now, and that is what finally lets a layered model be SAVED (2026-09-15).**
      B1 commit 4. `mf.disv(stack)` on a gridless `LayerStack` raised; it emits a LAZY
      `PackageSpec` that resolves the stack against whatever grid the build supplies.
      **The seam already existed** -- `mf.disv` has a `grid=` parameter and duck-types on
      `.to_disv`, and `ModelSpec.build` resolves a deferred `GridSpec` and publishes it
      onto `model.myflopy_context` BEFORE any package builds -- so laziness replaced one
      raise rather than adding machinery. One declaration now builds correctly at
      ncpl 28 and ncpl 92.
      **The headline is the save.** Before: `validate()` reported "not serializable",
      `save()` persisted **0 simulations**, `load()` returned an empty project, for every
      layered model. After: clean, 1, and a rebuild at the right `ncpl`.
      **The stack rides in `PackageSpec.inputs`, so the plan's new `recipe` field was not
      needed.** `build` splats `inputs` into the builder, and `_json_value`,
      `freeze._lift` and `package_digest` already handle it.
      **Three traps, each live in the first version:**
      - **`ModelSpec.build` passes a LOCAL `context`** to the guard and to `BuiltModel`,
        set before the package loop. Without re-reading `model.myflopy_context` after it,
        the guard condemns a CORRECT lazy build -- it raises "context domain is shaped
        (2, 28) against ncpl=92" whether or not the DISV just published a correct one.
      - **The snapshot froze the RECIPE.** Measured: a thawed lazy model's DISV held a
        `LayerStack` and no `top`/`botm`/`idomain` at all, so a reopened run went back to
        `gis/ground.tif` -- ledger 251's failure restored. `BuiltModel.resolved` records
        what a lazy builder actually produced and `Run._freeze` passes it, so the run
        stays a self-contained archive: **build from a raster top, delete `gis/` entirely,
        thaw and rebuild -- byte-identical `botm`.** This is the user's decision of
        2026-09-15, and taking the other option would have shipped the regression.
      - **Publish by REBINDING.** `ModelContext` is frozen with slots.
      **All eight of `to_disv`'s build kwargs are forwarded** (user decision, same day),
      and they are honest in both directions. A `LayerStack` has not sampled anything, so
      every one acts -- measured, `default_pinch="inactive"` takes idomain layer 0 from 28
      to 0, `default_min_thickness=5.0` moves `botm.sum` 2772.0 -> 2660.0, `reconcile=False`
      2772.0 -> 2798.6. A `LayerBuildResult` already HOLDS its arrays, so none of them can
      act there and a non-default one is **refused by name** rather than silently ignored.
      That third path -- a GRID-BOUND stack -- was found by mutation: removing its
      forwarding killed no test, because every kwarg test went through the lazy branch.
      A declared `domain` that disagrees with what the stack resolves is refused, naming
      both shapes: a lazy DISV publishes the domain it built, so declaring a different one
      describes two models.
      NOT done: `mf.disv(result)` stays EAGER. Making it lazy costs 24 option-read
      assertions across 5 test modules plus 21 `attach=True` sites; the additive form
      costs zero, and the plan's own API sketch writes `mf.disv(stack)`.
      **Amended 2026-09-25: the lazy spec holds its OWN copy of the stack.** It held the
      CALLER'S object whenever nothing in the stack named a file (the hash stamp is what
      rebuilt one), so on an all-inline stack a later `stack.add(...)` rewrote the
      declared package, a library `disv/base`, and its digest -- `packages.digests()`
      kept the cached value while a fresh one differed. The copy is rebuilt from the
      stack's own payload (`stamp_source_hashes` now always rebuilds a token-bearing
      object, stamped or not), NOT made with `for_grid`, which shares the mutable
      `_Layer` records and would drop any field a later change adds unless taught it
      too -- where `to_dict`/`from_dict` must be taught it anyway to be saved. Only a
      stack holding per-cell arrays, which cannot be written down, falls back to
      `for_grid(None)`. **No digest moves**: across the full suite, 124 declarations
      where the old code held the caller's object (121 stacks, 3 `CellSurfaceOffset`s)
      each digest the same as their copy. A `from_dict` refusing the payload its own
      `to_dict` wrote now RAISES rather than silently returning the caller's unstamped
      object. The semantics are a SNAPSHOT: to take an edit, declare the package again.
      **The EAGER form too** (same day, on review): `mf.disv(result)` /
      `result.to_disv()` held the RESULT'S OWN `top`/`botm`/`idomain` -- `np.asarray`
      does not copy -- so `result.idomain[0, :5] = 0` after the call reached the
      declared package and moved its digest. It copies now (`np.array`), which is what
      makes "a declaration owns its copy" true of every `mf.disv` form, the premise the
      excavation design's F4 (an edit verb that mutates) rests on; it moves no digest,
      the values are the same. A result handed a `grid=` of ANOTHER cell count is
      refused at the call: it wrote the new `ncpl` over the old `top`, and FloPy
      refused that only at build with an `MFDataException` naming neither count. And
      `stamp_source_hashes` takes the `{"$tuple": ...}` tag off before it rebuilds, as
      `_spec_value` has since the same day's fix for a saved tuple `split=`:
      `Spread.to_dict` runs `_json_value` on itself, so
      `stamp_source_hashes(mf.Spread(("a", "b")))` came back holding a DICT field --
      unequal to the original though it digested the same. `repoint_source_paths`,
      the third payload-to-object funnel, untags too; no shipped class writes a path
      and a tagged tuple into one payload, so there it is the rule, pinned on a
      synthetic class, rather than a live case.
      Found while documenting `mf.disv`, NOT changed: its hand-written form accepts the
      eight build keywords and does nothing with them (the result form refuses them),
      and on the lazy form `attach=False` hands the model context whatever table the
      grid already held (top 500.0 against the DISV's 100.0) -- the excavation design's
      D9, due in its lifecycle commit, and ~~not changed~~ closed there (ledger 323): the
      context gets a table built from the result.

271. **Move it, and read the report (2026-09-15).**
      B1 commit 5, the last. `SimulationSpec.with_grid(grid, *, on=, name=, grid_free=())`
      replaces `replace_grid`, which swapped the grid and re-mapped NOTHING -- every
      package kept cellids resolved on the old mesh and nothing looked (ledger 249).
      **It reports and stamps; the BUILD refuses** (user decision, 2026-09-15). The guard
      that refuses already exists and runs against what was actually built, so the refusal
      lives in one place rather than two; `move_report()` is what lets you see the verdict
      on the SPEC, before `prepare_run` raises.
      **Four verdicts.** `rebuilt` -- carries a recipe, so it resolves itself (a lazy
      DISV). `stale` -- pinned to another mesh, OR a hand-written DISV, which names no
      cellid and carries no pin but IS the old mesh: it holds that grid's `cell2d` and
      `vertices` verbatim. The first classifier called that one "unchanged".
      `unverifiable` -- names cells with no pin, because **you cannot pin cell numbers the
      caller typed**; every one is still in range on a larger mesh and every one names a
      different cell, so nothing can tell it from a correct one. `unchanged` -- names no
      cells, or the caller asserted mesh-independence with `grid_free=`.
      **The stamp is what closes the unverifiable case.** `with_grid` records the pin the
      package moved AWAY from, and the build refuses a package carrying it. Measured
      before it: a hand-written `wel` cellid built clean across a 28 -> 92 move.
      `on=None` moves **every model that has a grid**, because coupled models must share
      a mesh and MF6 cannot detect a same-size violation (ledger 268) -- moving one and
      stranding its sibling is exactly what that check exists to catch. `on=` is the
      escape hatch and is the spelling that can strand one.
      `replace_grid` is a `__getattr__`-only warned alias (D12: out of `dir()`, out of the
      api_snapshot, which filters private names). `pyproject.toml` turns a myflopy
      `DeprecationWarning` into an ERROR, so the one existing caller had to migrate and
      the deprecation test opts in with `pytest.warns` -- which is the point: any other
      caller fails the suite rather than carrying on quietly. The lineage string moves
      from `replace_grid` to `with_grid` and gains `models`/`grid_free`.
      `Run.resolution` is the same classification recomputed AFTER the build, where a
      `rebuilt` row can carry the `ncpl` the lazy DISV actually resolved to -- which
      exists nowhere else.
      **NOT done, measured:** a model whose grid is DEFERRED has no resolved mesh at
      declaration, so `with_grid` has no pin to stamp and its hand-written cellids move
      unrefused. They were never verifiable in the first place -- CLAUDE.md already says a
      hand-written package stays unpinned -- so this is the pre-existing gap rather than a
      new one, but the stamp does not close it.
      **Also NOT accepted:** `uncovered=`, `drop=`, `reducers=` from the plan's signature.
      Nothing is transferred from old cells at B1 -- the stack re-samples its own rasters
      -- so none of them could act, and `uncovered=`'s two candidate meanings are already
      owned by `gaps=` (ledger 248) or are "stale", which this refuses. A parameter that
      cannot act is the same defect as a hidden one.
      One mutant found dead code rather than a bug: the stamping condition re-tested
      `grid_free` after `package_move` had already honoured it.

272. **A lazy builder accepted any option name at all (2026-09-15).**
      `_accepted_options` inspects a FloPy package class, or a wrapper that DECLARES
      its target via `mf6_targets`. `_build_lazy_disv` is a plain function and
      declared none, so the function returned `None` and `_check_options` ABSTAINED:
      measured, `mf.disv(stack, bogus_option=1)` was accepted at the call and
      surfaced from inside FloPy at build, a whole `prepare_run` from the mistake.
      The EAGER form raised the whole time, which is what kept the gap invisible --
      the check was not weakened, it was never reached.
      One line fixes it (`_build_lazy_disv.mf6_targets = build_disv.mf6_targets`),
      and it buys a second refusal for free: `_package_scope` reads the SAME signal,
      so a lazy DISV handed to `mf.simulation(packages=[...])` was undecidable and
      waved through, to die inside FloPy as `Invalid package type`. It is refused at
      the call now, like the eager one always was.
      **Declaring the target also widens the accepted set to the builder's own
      parameters** -- `layer_stack`, `build_kwargs`, `disv_name` -- because a
      wrapper's named parameters are normally legitimate options. On a lazy spec
      they are not: they are the RECIPE, and `PackageSpec.build` splats
      `**self.inputs` and `**self.options` together, so a name in both is always
      fatal. Unchecked it read `_build_lazy_disv() got multiple values for keyword
      argument 'layer_stack'`, naming the private builder rather than the call.
      `_check_input_collisions` refuses it at declaration instead.
      **It is deliberately a SEPARATE check from `_check_options`**, whose question
      is whether a name is ACCEPTABLE. `layer_stack` is perfectly acceptable to that
      builder; the defect is that the recipe already supplied it. Folding the two
      would have to answer "acceptable, but not from you", which is not what that
      function means.
      **`inputs` carries TWO different things, and the first version of this check
      asserted it carried one.** It broke
      `test_source_payloads_are_rebuilt_by_registry_and_keep_int_keys` on the full
      suite. A lazy recipe's entries are builder keyword arguments, where a duplicate
      is a mistake; a `DataSourceSpec`/`LiteralSource` entry is an UNRESOLVED value
      for the option of the SAME name -- `inputs["k"]` says where `options["k"]`
      comes from -- so there the names matching is the whole point, and `_json_value`
      already says so where it handles them ("`PackageSpec.inputs` is exactly where
      source specs live"). The check exempts a source by TYPE.
      **The source shadow is not a working shape, measured**: nothing in `src/`
      constructs one, nothing resolves one, and a build dies as
      `ModflowGwfnpf() got multiple values for keyword argument 'k'`. Refusing it
      would have foreclosed a design rather than caught a bug -- the resolver that
      consumes a source into its option is B2's to build, and this is the same
      latency ledger c877911 recorded from the digest side. A test pins the exemption
      so it is not "tightened" over the top of that work.
      Otherwise the collision check runs on every `PackageSpec`, not only lazy ones,
      and the full suite confirms nothing legitimate carries one.
      Both halves were mutation-tested: dropping `mf6_targets` fails
      `test_a_typo_on_a_lazy_disv_is_refused_at_the_call` and
      `test_a_lazy_disv_is_refused_on_a_simulation`; dropping the collision check
      fails `test_a_recipe_name_cannot_also_be_passed_as_an_option`. Each test
      carries a control in the other direction -- a real FloPy option and a
      forwarded build kwarg must still pass -- because a refusal bought with a false
      positive is not a fix.

273. **The digest saw a package's representation, not its content (2026-09-15).**
      `package_digest` has to survive the round trip `_json_value` defines -- that
      is its whole contract. `_canonical` did not: it normalized numpy scalars and
      interned strings, then PASSED THROUGH anything else, including a `Path` and
      any object `_json_value` rewrites. So the two disagreed, and a package
      digested one way live and another after `Project.save()` + `load()`.
      **LIVE since B1, not latent.** `mf.disv(<gridless LayerStack>)` puts a stack
      in `inputs`; measured `58dd51bc12ac3736` live against `6e269fd095da3ee7`
      reloaded, so `project.runs.drift()` reported a package nobody edited as
      `edited`. The cause is ledger 222 one level deeper, INSIDE an object this
      function never entered: `'constant_thickness'` is one interned string object
      in the live stack and several after JSON, so pickle back-references it in one
      graph and writes it repeatedly in the other. **A ONE-LAYER stack does not show
      it** and would certify a fix that does nothing -- the tests build two.
      It is EDITED PERMANENTLY, not once: browsing, `drift()` and `run.write()` all
      leave a stored digest alone; only re-preparing the run rewrites it. (That
      corrects ledger 222's "reads edited ONCE".)
      **The fix is to make `_canonical` agree with `_json_value`** -- mirroring its
      first three branches, in its order, ABOVE the containers: a `PurePath` becomes
      its posix string, and a token-bearing or source object is canonicalized
      through its own `to_dict()` under a tag. Order matters for a token-bearing
      Mapping, which the dict branch would otherwise claim first, fingerprinting a
      body `_json_value` throws away.
      **It moves NO stored digest, measured, which is why it is safe without a
      version field.** 0 of the 12 real packages in the user's Ten Trails library,
      0 of the persisted `PackageSpec` files in `examples/`, and the repo's only
      stored manifest digest (`npf/high_k`) recomputes `666910e1103a5ac9`
      unchanged. Every one of the 12 has an empty `inputs` and no `Path`, source or
      token anywhere in its digested fields -- a `.gpkg` recipe lives in `metadata`,
      which the digest excludes. **Survey limit, stated honestly:** the repo tracks
      ZERO digest-bearing manifests (`.gitignore`), so a user's own stored runs
      cannot be surveyed from here. What DOES move is exactly one thing: a
      `mf.disv(<gridless stack>)` package, and only where it is a library entry
      referenced by `mf.ref` -- an inline one is never digested at all
      (`_package_digests` records only ref keys). Those users see one `edited` row
      once, against a false row that is currently permanent.
      **Re-baseline with `run.package_digests = {...}; run.save_manifest()`, NOT
      `prepare_run(overwrite=True)`** -- the latter also replaces the run's
      `_library/` copy and DELETES `frozen.npz`, destroying what ledgers 230 and 251
      exist to provide.
      **The plan's `package_digests_version` stays unbuilt**, with the number that
      justifies deferring it: zero stored packages move, and `Run.from_dict` reads
      `package_digests` with `.get`, so the field is backward-readable whenever a
      change does warrant one.
      **Two deliberate costs.** A stack whose top is `Surface.from_array` becomes
      UNFINGERPRINTED (`None`) rather than digested -- `to_dict` refuses a per-cell
      surface (ledger 269) -- and that replaces a FALSE answer, not a correct one:
      such a package is persisted by pickle and its old digest drifted across that
      very route. And the digest now sees a token object's DECLARATION, so what
      `to_dict` omits is invisible: `LayerStack._draft` and `vor` no longer move it,
      which means **two stacks bound to different grids digest alike**. That cuts
      the right way for `_draft` (previewing a stack with `.plot` used to mark its
      package edited) and is a real blind spot for `vor`, unreachable through
      `mf.disv` (a stack with a grid goes eager) but reachable through `inputs`,
      which B2 populates.
      **`package_digest`'s handler had to widen to `except Exception`.** `_canonical`
      now calls `to_dict()`, which is arbitrary code, so the failure set stopped
      being four bounded exceptions. Measured with a `to_dict` raising `KeyError`,
      the un-widened version KILLED `packages.digests()` and `runs.summary()` --
      which Jupyter calls on every bare `project.runs` -- breaking this function's
      "reports rather than raises" contract and `workspace.py`'s rule that a
      bookkeeping column must never make `prepare_run` fail. Registered in
      `test_exception_narrowness.py` with that argument.
      **NOT claimed, though an earlier draft did:** digest-ability and save-ability
      do NOT coincide. An `ndarray`, a `CellSurfaceOffset`, a `Spread` and
      `Surface.where(<shapely zone>)` all take none of the new branches -- they are
      unsaveable and fully digestable, exactly as before. The runtime
      `GeoPackageSource` likewise has no `to_dict` at all, so it still pickles its
      live mesh; the rule that it must never enter `inputs` is unchanged and
      unenforced.
      **The controls are the point of the test module.** A fix bought by making the
      digest blind is not a fix, and the round-trip tests alone cannot tell: against
      a deliberately lossy `to_dict` that drops `pinch`/`split`/`min_thickness`/
      `names`, every round-trip test stays green while the digest goes blind to all
      four. The discrimination tests sweep exactly the CONDITIONALLY-written fields,
      and fail by name when that happens.
      Cost is NEGATIVE -- digesting the real 12-package library measures 153.9 ms
      after against 182.9 ms before (0.84x), and 221.7 ms without the exact-type leaf
      fast path -- so that fast path more than pays for the recursion. Two timing
      traps caught two independent measurers before the number settled: running the
      new code first on a cold cache flattered it by 5.5x, and leaving `import`
      statements inside the hot recursive function read 2.19x instead of ~1.2x.
      Alternate the variants and hoist the imports.
      **Corrects ledger 265's deferral**, which named "Phase 2 B1" as the trigger and
      priced the fix as moving ordinary source digests. B1 put builder kwargs in
      `inputs`, not sources; the mechanism is real and its effect is empty, because
      the population of stored source-bearing packages is zero.

274. **`mf.Spread` and `mf.CellSurfaceOffset` could not be written down (2026-09-16).**
      Both are the DOCUMENTED idioms for a `.gpkg` elevation and an extensive field
      -- `mf.drn.gpkg(..., elevation=mf.CellSurfaceOffset("cell_bottom", offset=2.0),
      conductance=mf.Spread("conductance"))` -- and `_json_value` refused both, so a
      package holding one fell through `_persist_package`'s pickle fallback. A
      pickled entry is a cache, not an archive (ledger 193), and these carried a
      `versions.json` pinning five libraries. They are JSON now: `SaveReport.pickled`
      goes 1 -> 0 and the saved file carries `{"$spread": {...}}`.
      B2 needs this: a lazy `.gpkg` recipe in `PackageSpec.inputs` will carry one,
      and until now that recipe could not be serialized at all.
      **NO stored digest moves -- 0 of 12**, measured on the user's real Ten Trails
      library, plus the repo's one stored manifest digest (`npf/high_k`,
      `666910e1103a5ac9`) recomputed unchanged. That matters because ledger 273 made
      a `_SPEC_TOKEN` object digest through its `to_dict()`, so GIVING these a token
      changes how they fingerprint. **The reason is structural, not luck:** 3 of the
      12 packages DO use a `CellSurfaceOffset`, but `.gpkg` resolves EAGERLY --
      `GeoPackageSource._value` consumes the object into per-cell floats at
      declaration, and its only trace is the flat dict `_metadata_value` writes into
      `PackageSpec.metadata`, which the digest excludes by contract. **B2 is the
      point at which that stops being true**, and must re-run this survey.
      **Survey limit:** nothing under `/home/lukem/models/` was reachable.
      **One exposure route was real and is now closed rather than documented.**
      `mf.rch.array`/`mf.evt.array` ACCEPTED a live `Spread`/`CellSurfaceOffset` into
      `options`, where it pickled and digested -- and `Project.prepare_run` calls
      `save_manifest()` BEFORE `build()` (and `build=False` is supported), so a run
      could record a digest for one and this entry's headline would have had a hole.
      They are refused at the call now, which is right on its own terms: both
      describe a PER-FEATURE resolution and the array form has no features, so
      neither could ever act -- the defect CLAUDE.md names.
      **`to_dict` is NOT `_metadata_value`, deliberately.** Two converters, two jobs:
      one round-trips, omits defaults and revives into a live object; the other is
      human-readable provenance that spells every field out and stays a plain dict.
      Delegating measured wrong twice -- `PackageSpec.from_dict` runs `metadata`
      through `_spec_value`, so a `$`-tagged metadata value would come back a LIVE
      OBJECT and change what `metadata['fields']` means for every consumer, and
      omitting defaults would make a manifest a human consults sparser. They are tied
      by a field-coverage test instead of by shared code -- which immediately caught
      that `_metadata_value` dropped `Spread.warn_below`, 3 of 4 fields, under a test
      whose docstring claimed it "keeps enough to reproduce the split". Whether a
      feature losing 40% of itself warns depended on a number no artifact recorded.
      **`to_dict` normalizes through `_json_value`, where `Surface.to_dict` does
      not.** `type(np.float64(0.01)) is not float`, so an un-normalized numpy scalar
      fails the omit-defaults test, gets written, and comes back a plain float that
      IS omitted -- two payloads for one object, and a digest that moves across a
      save. It also makes a bare `to_dict()` safe for `yaml.safe_dump`, which
      dispatches on the exact type and refuses what `json.dumps` takes (ledger 265).
      **`tests/test_spec_token_registry.py` closes the class of bug rather than the
      instance.** Declaring `_SPEC_TOKEN` is enough to be WRITTEN -- `_json_value`
      duck-types on it -- while being READ is a separate hand-maintained if-chain in
      `_spec_value`. Forget the arm and the object returns a PLAIN DICT with nothing
      raised (ledger 269's trap, reproduced here for `Spread`). The test sweeps by
      AST rather than importing: 0.4 s against 4.6 s for a `pkgutil` walk. Two
      constraints follow and are asserted, not assumed: a `_SPEC_TOKEN` must be a
      string LITERAL in a class body, and an arm must be spelled `"$token" in value`
      -- `$tuple`'s `set(value) == {"$tuple"}` form is invisible to the sweep and is
      exempt BY NAME rather than silently absent. A third test guards the guard: an
      AST sweep that finds nothing would pass the other two.
      **A duck-type elsewhere had to move.** `package_api`'s `mf.disv` used
      `hasattr(layers, "_SPEC_TOKEN")` to mean "a declared gridless `LayerStack`",
      which stopped being a synonym the moment two more classes carried one:
      `mf.disv(mf.Spread("x"))` went from an immediate `AttributeError` naming the
      real problem to an ACCEPTED, persistable spec that died at build talking about
      layer stacks. It tests `to_disv` now. The lesson generalizes -- a token means
      "this serializes", never "this is a particular kind of thing".
      `myflopy.specs` gains two deferred imports (5 -> 7 on the ratchet), which
      cannot be hoisted: `specs` is layer 1, `geopackage` is layer 3, and
      `geopackage` imports `specs` at module scope, so a module-level import is both
      an upward edge and a cycle -- the same reason the `$surface`/`$layer_stack`
      arms are lazy. `package_api`'s is hoisted instead, since it already imports
      `geopackage` at module level and layer 5 -> 3 is downward.
      **Also fixed, unclaimed until measured:** revival goes through `__init__`, so
      `__post_init__` re-runs and a hand-edited payload is refused where the reader
      can act on it. `TypeError` is translated too -- a missing field otherwise read
      `Spread.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument`, naming a
      constructor the reader never called.

275. **An edited package kept the certificate that said the library resolved it
      (2026-09-16).**
      A resolved `.gpkg` package carries a pin meaning *the library resolved these
      records on this mesh*. `packages.edit`/`fork`/`with_options`/`dataclasses.replace`
      all REPLACE the option wholesale -- measured, 11 records become 1 -- and every
      one of them copied the pin through byte-identically. So the package went on
      certifying a resolution that had not produced its records.
      **The damage was not a missed refusal but an UNANSWERABLE one.** Measured across
      a 6x6 -> 10x10 move: an edited CHD reported `stale` and the build refused with
      *"re-declare it against the new grid"* -- to a user who had ALREADY typed correct
      cell numbers for that grid, in a message naming records that no longer existed.
      There was no way out: the edit route can never re-pin, because you cannot pin
      cell numbers the caller typed (ledger 250). The only two escapes measured were
      `with_metadata(grid_pin=None)` and `with_metadata(**{GRID_PIN: grid_pin(new)})`,
      both undocumented and the second a way to FORGE the library's certificate.
      **A pin now declares the options it speaks for** (`GRID_PIN_OPTIONS`, written at
      the pin site by the resolver that took it) and an edit naming one voids it into
      `PIN_VOIDED = {"was": <pin>, "options": [...]}`. Editing `stress_period_data`
      voids; renaming the file or toggling `save_flows` does not -- measured across 98
      (package, override) pairs on the seven list BCs, 91 left the built cellids
      byte-identical and the 7 that moved them were all `stress_period_data`.
      **Declared per site, not from one global list**, because the same name is
      grid-bound on one package and not another: `packagedata` carries a cellid on
      `sfr`/`uzf` and none on `lak`.
      **Voiding KEEPS the pin's value rather than deleting the key.** Measured:
      popping `GRID_PIN` removed the build-time refusal outright -- a CHD pinned to one
      mesh then BUILT CLEAN on another -- and dropped `lak`/`rch.array`/`evt.array` to
      `unchanged`, the verdict that means moves untouched. The refusal is as strong as
      before; only the sentence changed, and it now names the edit.
      **`certifies=` is a REQUIRED keyword and an empty one omits the key.** That is
      the one direction a forgotten keyword must never take: an empty list makes
      `set(touched) & set([])` empty, so nothing would EVER void it, silently. Absent
      means "void on any override" -- which is also what every pin serialized before
      this entry does, so there is no migration.
      **Keyed on the option NAME, not on a change of value.** A value oracle means a
      deep walk at every check, and `fork_package` already measures 808 ms copying a
      654,480-record EVT. The accepted cost: re-supplying an IDENTICAL dict voids a pin
      that was still true. A spurious `unverifiable` rather than a silent stale pin --
      the direction that fails safe.
      **No digest moves**: `metadata` is excluded from `package_digest` by contract
      (ledgers 186, 250), verified here -- voiding and not voiding digest identically,
      while a real records change still moves it.
      **The recipe test moved to LAST in `package_move`, which is a second live bug.**
      `if inputs: return "rebuilt"` ran BEFORE the hand-written-DISV branch, the pin and
      the cellid test, so a pinned CHD carrying any `inputs` entry read "nothing to
      check" while its pin sat unread. Harmless while only a lazy DISV carried
      `inputs`; **B2 puts a source recipe in every lazy `.gpkg`**, which is precisely a
      package with both a recipe and grid-bound content. A pin whose certified options
      are ALL supplied by the recipe now supersedes to `rebuilt` -- the contract B2's
      later commits must meet. Note that shape is only constructible with a SOURCE spec
      in `inputs`: a plain value under a certified name is refused by ledger 272's
      collision check, so the supersede branch cannot be reached by accident.
      **A voided RECIPE is refused at construction rather than given a fifth verdict.**
      Clearing `inputs` on a lazy package produced a spec that classified `unchanged`
      -- moves untouched -- and could not build on any mesh, failing later as
      `_build_lazy_disv() missing 2 required keyword-only arguments`. A label cannot
      refuse anything and the state has no legitimate producer, so `__post_init__`
      refuses it, following ledger 208's refuse-at-the-call pattern. Narrow to required
      KEYWORD-ONLY parameters, which refuses nothing that exists: 108
      `flopy.mf6.Modflow*` classes have zero, and `_build_lazy_disv` is the only
      builder in the library with any. `inspect.signature` is cached -- uncached it
      measured `mf.npf` at 44.2 -> 82.5 us/call for a check that can fire on one
      builder. The message names `builder.__name__`: `_builder_label_for_error` answers
      with the four FloPy DISV classes since ledger 272 gave the lazy builder
      `mf6_targets`, and none of them requires those names.
      **One defect, one sentence.** A voided package classifies `unverifiable`, so it
      was ALSO stamped `MOVED_FROM` and listed a second time under a different
      explanation -- measured on a real ncpl 36 -> 100 move. Voided packages are no
      longer stamped; their own complaint already refuses them.
      **Known and deliberate:** `sfr`/`uzf`/`lak` have no non-voiding edit route for
      their physics, because the cell-bearing option is also the only home of roughness,
      width, bed leakance and stage -- so `packages.edit(key, packagedata=...)` always
      voids. Correct under the rule (the caller retyped the cellids) but a real cost.
      **Left to B2:** a resolver that RE-pins must clear `PIN_VOIDED`, or a package
      carries a pin and its own contradiction, and the duplicate complaint returns.

276. **Nothing noticed when a package's source file changed (2026-09-17).**
      A `.gpkg` package records `source_path` and nothing about what the file
      CONTAINED. So a library package built from a GeoPackage that was later edited
      reports `unchanged` forever -- measured: head 9.0 -> 42.0 on disk, the stored
      spec's digest identical before and after, because the records were resolved at
      declaration and the library never re-reads the file.
      Today that is defensible: the library package genuinely is unchanged, and
      `drift()` answers about the LIBRARY. **B2 makes it a lie.** A lazy `.gpkg`
      resolves from the file at BUILD time, so a changed file means a different model
      while the recipe -- and therefore the digest -- says nothing. The scope sweep for
      B2 commit 5 measured the fingerprint INVERTED on both axes for a lazy package:
      editing the content left the digest identical, while moving the same bytes to
      another path MOVED it. Pulled forward so it is fixed before the laziness that
      would expose it, rather than discovered after.
      **`SOURCE_SHA` records a 16-character content hash at declaration**, in
      `metadata`, which `package_digest` excludes -- so it moves NO stored digest, the
      same property ledger 250 relied on when it kept the grid pin out. Verified both
      directions.
      **`drift()` gains a `source` COLUMN, not a fifth state.** The two answer
      different questions: `state` is "does this key still mean what the run used?",
      `source` is "is the file it was built from still the one it was built from?" A
      package is routinely `unchanged` AND `edited` at once -- measured -- and
      collapsing them would make one invisible. Values: `ok`, `edited`, `missing`,
      `unfingerprinted` (a package that names a source but records no hash: everything
      declared before this entry, and anything whose file could not be read), and `—`
      for the majority that name no source.
      **It hashes BYTES, not logical content.** Rewriting a GeoPackage without changing
      a feature moves the hash: SQLite rewrites pages and the file carries its own
      timestamps. Deliberate -- a false `edited` is a prompt to look, a false `ok` is
      the lie this exists to remove. Cost is negligible: chunked, 3.2 ms for the
      largest real Ten Trails input (2.4 MB), against a declaration that already reads
      and spatially resolves the same file.
      **The `SOURCE_SHA` import is HOISTED, not ratcheted.** A function-level
      `from myflopy.specs import SOURCE_SHA` in `workspace.py` took the deferred-import
      ratchet from 1 to 2 and failed `test_deferred_import_ratchet`. `workspace` already
      imports from `specs` at module scope, so the import belongs there -- the same
      correction ledger 274 made for `package_api`. Only `specs` -> `geopackage` is
      genuinely undeferrable (an upward edge AND a cycle).
      **An unreadable source returns `None` rather than raising.** Declaring a package
      must never fail because a bookkeeping column could not be filled -- the rule
      `package_digest` already follows, and `workspace.py` requires that such a column
      never make `prepare_run` fail.
      **Still NOT answered, and named here so it is not mistaken for solved:** a
      package whose source moved to a new path with identical bytes. Today the recorded
      path is absolute, so ledger 256's `bundle_sources=True` -- which repoints every
      path into `inputs/` -- would report the whole library as source-changed. The
      fingerprint is content-only and does not see the path at all, so it is unaffected;
      but the BUNDLING commit must relativize the recorded path or explain the churn.

277. **The recipe a lazy `.gpkg` will carry (2026-09-17).**
      `BoundarySource(DataSourceSpec)` in `sources.py`: everything needed to reproduce
      a list BC's records given a grid, and nothing that needs one. **Data only --
      nothing emits one yet.** B2 commit 5b is the helper that does; this lands first
      so the contract is pinned before anything depends on it, and so the commit that
      changes behaviour changes only behaviour.
      **It is not the runtime `GeoPackageSource`, and cannot be.** That class holds a
      live `ModelContext` (hence a grid) and a cached GeoDataFrame, has no `to_dict`,
      and raises on both a missing file and a gridless context in `__post_init__` --
      measured, it cannot even be CONSTRUCTED as a recipe. Its digest also moves the
      moment anything reads its cache.
      **It is not `GeoPackageSourceSpec` either**, whose `fields` maps logical keys to
      columns for GRID resolution. The value mapping here is `values`: one name meaning
      two things is how that class's own docstring says a recipe goes silently inert.
      Worth knowing while reading either -- the registry key `"GeoPackageSource"`
      belongs to the SPEC class, not to the runtime class of that name. Two classes,
      one string; `BoundarySource` reuses neither.
      **`kind` ends in "Source" deliberately.** `_spec_value` keeps an
      `endswith("Source")` arm beside the registry so an unregistered kind RAISES
      instead of degrading to a plain dict -- the silent failure of ledger 269, which
      ledger 274 had to close again for `Spread`.
      **`kw_only=True` is structural, not stylistic.** `nper` has no default and the
      inherited fields do, so without it the class fails to be created at all. It also
      closes the positional trap `GeoPackageSourceSpec` documents, where
      `GeoPackageSourceSpec("x.gpkg", "areas")` silently sets `external="areas"`.
      **It carries NO package name**, against the scope document's design. That
      document put `package_name` in the recipe; the adversarial pass measured the
      consequence -- `fork_package` renames through `_renamed_options`, which rewrites
      `options` and never touches `inputs`, so a frozen name is silently discarded by a
      rename and **two renamed forks collapse into ONE MF6 package** under a FloPy
      "Replacing existing package" warning. That is the exact defect `_renamed_options`
      already exists to prevent, reopened through a new door. Identity belongs to the
      `PackageSpec`; 5b/5c must take the name from the spec at build time. `package` is
      kept because it names the record SCHEMA, which is type, not identity.
      **`to_dict()` is deliberately not pure JSON.** A live `Spread` in `values` comes
      back as itself, because that is what `_canonical` fingerprints (ledger 273) and
      what `from_dict` rebuilds; `_json_value` is the converter and writes the
      `$spread` / `$cell_surface_offset` tokens. `json.dumps(source.to_dict())` raises,
      and that is not a defect.
      **The reverse trip works ONLY through `options`/`inputs`.** `_spec_value(...,
      int_keys=True)` is what recurses INTO a source payload and revives those tokens.
      Measured and pinned in both directions: through `inputs` the nested objects come
      back as `Spread`/`CellSurfaceOffset`; through any other field they come back as
      plain DICTS, with nothing raised. 5b must put the recipe in `inputs` and nowhere
      else.
      **Exported as `mf.BoundarySource`** for consistency: every other source class is,
      and the house position (stated in `DataSourceSpec`'s own docstring) is that these
      are public but rarely hand-built -- reached for "only when authoring a serialized
      recipe", which is exactly what someone reading `"kind": "BoundarySource"` in a
      saved project is doing. The api_snapshot diff is one line, the new name.
      Verified across all five routes a spec takes -- `to_dict`, JSON, YAML, the freeze
      lift, and `package_digest` -- plus deepcopy and pickle. Defaults are omitted from
      the payload so a later defaulted field cannot move an existing digest, and a
      discrimination test asserts all twelve fields still move it, because a payload
      that stops writing a field is a digest that stops seeing it.

278. **A builder never learned which package it was building (2026-09-17).**
      `PackageSpec.build` calls `self.builder(target, **inputs, **options)`, so a
      builder receives no name, no metadata, no spec. That is right for a FloPy class,
      which is told everything through options, and wrong for a builder that RESOLVES a
      recipe: the package it produces has to be NAMED, and the recipe deliberately does
      not carry one (ledger 277).
      **Freezing the name in the recipe instead is worse than useless, measured.**
      `fork_package` renames through `_renamed_options`, which rewrites `options` and
      never touches `inputs` -- so a frozen name survives a rename unchanged, and TWO
      renamed forks collapse into ONE MF6 package under a FloPy "Replacing existing
      package" warning, with myflopy's own bookkeeping reporting two. That is the exact
      defect `_renamed_options` already exists to prevent (its docstring records the
      same measurement), reopened through a new door. The scope document for B2 commit 5
      specified `package_name` in the recipe; the adversarial pass is what caught it.
      **`build` passes `_spec=self` to a builder that declares a keyword-only `_spec`.**
      Opt-in by SIGNATURE rather than by a flag, so every builder that does not ask is
      called exactly as before -- verified for a FloPy class and for the `functools.
      partial` list-BC builders. Cached, because it runs on every build.
      **One guard fired on the other's mechanism.** `_check_recipe_complete` (ledger
      275) reads required keyword-only parameters and refuses a spec whose recipe does
      not supply them -- and `_spec` is supplied by `build`, not by the recipe, so a
      builder asking for its own identity was refused at construction. `_spec` is
      excluded by name. Worth noting as a pattern: the checks added across ledgers
      272-277 now interact, and each new mechanism has to be run against all of them
      rather than reasoned about.
      **This is B2 commit 5's blocker 1, landed on its own** because the lazy `.gpkg`
      builder cannot be written without it, and because it is general: nothing here is
      about GeoPackages, and 5c needs the same identity for the frozen-snapshot key.

279. **A `.gpkg` boundary condition can be declared before its grid exists
      (2026-09-17).**
      `mf.chd.gpkg(path, layer=..., nper=...)` without `context=` emits a LAZY spec that
      resolves against whatever grid the build supplies. **One declaration builds
      correctly on two meshes** -- measured, chd 11 records at ncpl 36 and 13 at ncpl
      100, drn 10 and 7 carrying a `Spread` and a `CellSurfaceOffset`, each identical to
      the eager form on that mesh. That is what turns a `move_report` row from `stale`
      into `rebuilt`, and it is the reason Phase 2 exists (ledger 249).
      **With `context=` nothing changes.** The eager branch is untouched; the recipe
      branch is an early return above it. `api_snapshot` moves exactly seven rows,
      `context` required -> optional, and nothing else.
      **One generic builder bound per package with `functools.partial`**, not seven
      private functions and not one with a union `mf6_targets`. Measured: the partial
      gives `_accepted_options` the REAL package's 13 names, where a union gives 22 --
      so `mf.chd.gpkg(..., nseg=3)` is refused by the lazy form exactly as by the eager
      one, did-you-mean included. Memoized, because `_required_keyword_only` and
      `_wants_spec` are cached on the builder OBJECT and a partial hashes by identity.
      **Three preconditions, each replacing a failure that named nothing.** No grid on
      the context -> a message naming the three ways to supply one. No discretization
      built yet -> "the discretization has to be declared BEFORE it", replacing
      `MFDataException ... "stress_period_data"` five frames down. A discretization
      whose `ncpl` disagrees with the grid's -> both counts, replacing `IndexError:
      index 56 is out of bounds`. The discretization is found by `package_type`, never
      by name: `model.get_package("dis")` does a FloPy PREFIX match and returns a
      `ModflowGwfdisv`, and `requires=("disv",)` names the myflopy SPEC name, so it
      false-refuses `mf.disv(stack, name="mesh")` and a `mf.ref` whose key differs.
      **The DOMAIN falls back to the built discretization, and that is correctness.**
      `with_grid` DROPS `context.domain`, so a lazy package's context routinely carries
      none. Measured with three cells of a drain line inactive in the DISV: reading the
      built idomain gives 7 records, matching the eager form given an explicit
      `domain=`, while a resolver reading only the context gives 10 -- three drains
      written into cells the discretization makes inactive. MF6 then refuses the run,
      EXCEPT under `edges_only=True` where it runs normally on the wrong boundary. Read
      off the PACKAGE, never `model.modelgrid.idomain`: flopy SYNTHESIZES an all-ones
      float array where the package's own field says None.
      **SURFACES fall back to the discretization's top/botm**, which is what makes
      `CellSurfaceOffset` -- the documented elevation idiom for drn/riv/ghb -- work
      behind an eager or hand-written DISV, where it raises today. The order consults
      `context.surfaces`, then `grid.gdf_topbtm`, then the built package: that is PARITY
      with `_layer_elevations`, not preference, and lazy == eager is this commit's
      contract. The fallback is LOCAL to this package's resolution and is deliberately
      NOT published onto `model.myflopy_context` -- publishing would change what every
      later package reads, including the eager ones.
      **DEFERRED, and narrower than an earlier draft of this entry said.** Consulting
      `grid.gdf_topbtm` before the built discretization can give a WRONG answer, because
      two routes sample the same rasters and only one reconciles: `grid.rasters=[...]`
      reaches `get_raster_vals_at_centroids` -- raw per-cell sampling, no reconciliation
      -- while `LayerStack.build()` pushes each bottom below the one above, enforces
      `min_thickness` and applies pinch rules. Where the rasters CROSS, which real
      interpolated surfaces do, the two disagree.
      Measured here (reproducer: `docs/reproducers/raw_vs_reconciled_surfaces.py`), flat
      100 ft top against a bottom ramping 60 -> 120 ft: **18 of 36 cells differ, max
      18.94 ft**, and the raw table puts the layer bottom ABOVE the model top in 16
      cells where the reconciled one never does. It reaches a boundary condition -- a
      `drn.gpkg` with `CellSurfaceOffset("cell_bottom")` resolved 0.000 ft from the raw
      table and **18.943 ft from the DISV the same script built**, placing 5 of 10 drain
      inverts above the model top, silently.
      **THREE conditions are all required**, which is why the default path is safe: the
      grid must carry `rasters=`, the stack must be built with `attach=False`, and the
      rasters must actually cross. Measured: `attach=True` -- the DEFAULT in
      `_DISV_BUILD_DEFAULTS`, so what `mf.disv(stack)` does -- overwrites `gdf_topbtm`
      with the reconciled table and the difference is 0.000 ft. The lazy path is safe
      for the same reason: the DISV publishes the reconciled surfaces onto the context,
      which this order consults FIRST.
      Not fixed here, and deliberately not by preferring the discretization: that would
      make lazy and eager disagree, which is this commit's contract. It is an EAGER-path
      defect and belongs in its own commit.
      **A number quoted without its setup is not evidence.** An earlier draft carried
      "11.87 ft on 12 of 28 cells" from the scope sweep; no surviving script produced it,
      and the figure is a property of whatever synthetic rasters that scout built rather
      than of the library. The reproducer above is checked in so the next reader does not
      have to rebuild it -- see [[a-measurement-belongs-to-what-it-measured]].
      **The declaration-time checks are repeated in `_lazy_bc_spec` on purpose.** They
      live in `GeoPackageSource.__post_init__`, which the lazy branch never reaches, so
      without them `mf.chd.gpkg("nope.gpkg", nper=0)` was ACCEPTED and raised at BUILD.
      Neither check needs a grid, so neither belongs at build time.
      **This commit broke a guard it inherited, and had to fix it.** Ledger 272's source
      exemption let an edit to a lazy package's records through: both `with_options` and
      `fork_package` constructed fine and died at BUILD with `functools.partial(...) got
      multiple values for keyword argument 'stress_period_data'`, naming a partial
      object -- the exact failure that check exists to prevent. The exemption now has a
      limit: a source is exempt UNLESS the builder itself REQUIRES that keyword. Case
      (b) survives for a builder that does not.
      **`edges_only` is read from the package registry**, not a hand-kept list:
      `wel`/`rch`/`evt` have no such parameter and `capabilities.edges_only` already
      said so. Three generated wrappers referenced a name that did not exist there, and
      the registry is what fixed it -- §4.7's one-descriptor rule paying off.
      **NOT in this commit:** the resolved spec does not yet reach the frozen snapshot,
      so a lazy package reopens from its recipe rather than its records, and `mf.ref`
      is untested against it. Both are commit 5c. Until then a lazy `.gpkg` run is
      rebuildable only while its GeoPackage is still there -- the dependence ledger 251
      exists to remove.

280. **A lazy `.gpkg` run went back to its GeoPackage on reopen (2026-09-17).**
      Ledger 279 made the seven list BCs resolve at build time and deliberately stopped
      short of the snapshot. Without it a run froze the RECIPE, so reopening rebuilt
      from the GeoPackage -- the dependence ledger 251's snapshot exists to remove.
      Measured: delete the source and thaw, `FileNotFoundError: GeoPackage not found`.
      The builder records what it BUILT into `model._myflopy_resolved`, which
      `ModelSpec.build` collects into `BuiltModel.resolved` and `Run._freeze` passes as
      `resolved=`. Measured after: both paths thaw with the file deleted, 11 records,
      the same cells. The frozen spec carries `inputs == {}`, the records, and the new
      mesh's pin with `GRID_PIN_OPTIONS` -- so it reads `stale`, which is CORRECT for a
      resolved snapshot -- while the declared spec keeps its recipe and stays `rebuilt`.
      Two different objects, each staying itself.
      **`mf.ref` failed where inline succeeded, and it is the DOCUMENTED library path.**
      `freeze._for` reads `name` off the DECLARED entry, and a `PackageRef`'s name is
      its library KEY (`"chd/west"`), while a builder only ever knows the resolved
      spec's own name (`"chd"`). The mismatch is COMPLETELY silent: no warning, a
      readable snapshot, an identical `Run.resolution` row -- the snapshot simply keeps
      the recipe and nothing says so until the file moves. `ModelSpec.build` now aliases
      the resolved spec under the ref key as well, keying off `zip(self.packages,
      packages)` where both the declared entry and its resolution are in scope. The
      test is PARAMETRIC over inline and `mf.ref` for exactly this reason; an
      inline-only test passes with the alias deleted.
      **`Run.resolution` reports what each package actually resolved TO.**
      `resolved_ncpl` was read off `options["ncpl"]`, which a boundary condition does
      not have -- so the column said `None` for every package except the
      discretization. A lazy DISV resolves to a mesh and reports `resolved_ncpl`; a lazy
      BC resolves to RECORDS and reports `resolved_records`; a package that resolved
      nothing reports neither.
      **A test deleted a module-scoped fixture's directory** and broke every test after
      it -- the shared-fixture hazard ledger 48 records, reproduced here by the test
      written to prove the fix. It copies the GeoPackage into its own `tmp_path` first.
      A shared fixture is read-only by contract, and "my test cleans up after itself" is
      how that contract gets broken.

281. **Two ways a package escaped classification, both found by importing a real run
      (2026-09-18).**
      Rebuilding specs from a finished MF6 workspace -- the user's own workflow --
      produced a model every row of whose `Run.resolution` read `unchanged`, the verdict
      that means MOVES UNTOUCHED. Two independent causes, the same shape as ledger 280's
      freeze mis-key: **the declared entry and the thing it resolves to are different
      objects, and only one of them can be classified.**
      **(a) `Run.resolution` classified the `mf.ref`, not the package it names.** A
      `PackageRef` carries no `options`, `inputs` or `metadata`, so `package_move`
      answered "names no cells" for every entry of a model declared the DOCUMENTED
      library way. It resolves the ref against the run's own package copies first now.
      **(b) `_cellids_in` skipped a numpy RECARRAY entirely.** It accepted a list or a
      tuple of records; a recarray is neither -- and a recarray is what FloPy itself
      produces, what a `.flopy(...)` escape hatch carries, and what rebuilding a spec
      from a written run gives. Measured on the real Ten Trails boundaries: **118
      cellids through the `.gpkg` path, 0 through the identical records as a recarray**,
      and the package classified `unchanged` rather than `unverifiable`. The hand-written
      list shape was fine the whole time, which is why every synthetic test passed.
      **Neither was reachable from the test suite**, because every fixture builds its
      records through a helper that emits lists. It took importing a bare MF6 workspace
      -- no `run.json`, no `_library`, no frozen snapshot -- to walk into them. Both
      tests now assert the recarray and list shapes classify IDENTICALLY, which is the
      invariant that was actually broken: the shape of the data must not change the
      verdict.
      **What a reader should take from this:** `unchanged` is the dangerous verdict. The
      other three refuse or warn; only this one lets a package through silently, so a
      gap anywhere in the classification chain fails in that direction. Ledgers 271,
      275, 280 and this one are all the same defect found in four different places.

282. **An array-form boundary condition names its cells by POSITION, and nothing was
      reading that (2026-09-18).**
      `mf.rch.array` / `mf.evt.array` supply one value per column -- no cellid anywhere --
      so `_cellids_in` finds nothing in them and only a PIN can say which mesh they were
      shaped for. `_array_bc_spec` took `ncpl` from `context.grid`, so **every declaration
      that resolved from a domain alone, or from no context at all, was unpinned** and fell
      through `package_move` to **`"unchanged"` -- the verdict that means MOVES UNTOUCHED**.
      Six reachable shapes were in it: `irch='top_active'` against a domain-only context, a
      per-column `recharge`/`rate` with no context, an explicit `irch` array, a
      `{period: array}` mapping, the EVT twin of each. Measured end to end: **one
      declaration wrote mesh A's recharge pattern onto a DIFFERENT mesh of the same cell
      count, built clean, and warned about nothing.**
      **The same payload written as a python list was invisible a second way.**
      `_names_cells` measured a value with `getattr(value, "shape", None)`, so
      `recharge=[1e-4] * ncpl` -- an ordinary spelling that FloPy accepts -- was never
      per-column to it, while the identical numpy array was. Same data, two verdicts:
      pinned and `stale` as an array, unpinned and `unchanged` as a list. That is ledger
      281's invariant again -- **the shape of the data must not change the verdict** -- and
      `_column_count` now answers for both.
      The fix is a second, weaker signal beside the pin: `CELLWISE_OPTIONS` names the
      options a package supplies one value per cell under, stamped when the payload
      addresses cells and there was no mesh to fingerprint. It classifies `unverifiable`,
      and it MIRRORS the pin -- a recipe supplying every option it speaks for answers
      `"rebuilt"` instead, which is the contract B2's lazy array form has to meet.
      **Where there is no `ncpl`, the test is conservative rather than exact.** With a grid,
      `_names_cells` compares a payload's length to the cell count. Without one there is
      nothing to compare against -- so any array-valued option counts, on the grounds that
      under `READASARRAYS` "one value per column" is the format's own definition. It can
      say that a value addresses cells; it cannot say the length is wrong.
      **What this does NOT close:** the length. A wrong-length array still reaches FloPy,
      which refuses it (`MFDataException`, "Expected data dimensions: [92]"). This is about
      the REPORT -- `move_report()` is what you read BEFORE `prepare_run`, and it was saying
      the package needed no attention. Moves no digest: `metadata` is excluded from
      `package_digest` by contract, measured 0 of 10.
      **Why the suite missed it:** every array-form test passes a full `context=`, which is
      the one shape that pins. **`unchanged` is the dangerous verdict** -- ledgers 271, 275,
      280 and 281 are the same defect found in four other places, and this is the fifth.

283. **The array form put the ET surface at the DATUM, and two arguments went missing on
      the way to the builder (2026-09-18).**
      Three defects in the two `mf.evt` branches that B2's lazy work rewrites, none of them
      caused by it. Fixed first so three physics and API corrections are not buried inside
      a laziness refactor.
      **(a) `mf.evt.array` with `surface` omitted wrote MODFLOW's datum.** The parameter
      was put into `fields` only when it was not None, so an omitted one never reached
      FloPy and `ModflowGwfevta`'s own `surface=0.0` default landed in the period block --
      while the docstring promised "the model top when omitted". MODFLOW 6 draws the full
      rate wherever the head is at or above the ET surface, so a surface pinned at datum
      makes `depth=` inert and runs maximum ET everywhere, for the life of the model, under
      Normal termination. **Measured on two real MF6 runs**, 4x4 two-layer, top 100, heads
      95: `surface CONSTANT 0.00000000` and an EVT total of **-151.13**, against
      `CONSTANT 100.00000000` and **0.0** for the same declaration naming the top. It is
      ledger 163's `irch` trap in the sibling package -- a FloPy default that is a
      defensible number and the wrong physics. It resolves through `SurfaceResolver` now,
      the same engine the list form's `CellSurfaceOffset("model_top")` default uses, so the
      two shapes of one package agree what "the model top" means. **It RAISES when it
      cannot resolve one**: writing a number the caller never gave is the thing being
      replaced, and `ievt='top_active'` already refuses a missing context for that reason.
      `SurfaceResolver.surface_column` returns a plain float when every column agrees, so a
      flat land surface still writes `CONSTANT` and stays off the per-column pin.
      **(b) `mf.evt(context=...)` dropped `nseg` and `auxiliary`.** Both are NAMED
      parameters, so neither ever fell into `**options`, and the builder branch assembled
      its kwargs without them: a caller asking for segmented ET got single-segment ET and a
      caller asking for an auxiliary variable got none, in both cases silently.
      `_check_options` cannot catch it -- `nseg` IS an accepted `ModflowGwfevt` option. The
      defect was ASYMMETRIC inside one helper pair: `mf.rch` keeps `auxiliary` precisely
      because it has no parameter of that name. `auxiliary` is forwarded now and `nseg > 1`
      raises, naming `mf.evt.flopy` -- the same refusal `mf.evt.array` already carried.
      **(c) `_refuse_per_feature_values` was handed `fields`, not the merged values.** It
      saw `{"recharge"}` for RCH and `{"rate", "depth", "surface"}` for EVT, so `irch=`,
      `auxmultname=`, `observations=` and every other keyword sailed past it. Measured:
      `recharge=Spread(...)` refused, `irch=Spread(...)` **accepted and digested** -- which
      is exactly the exposure its own docstring claims to have closed structurally, and the
      hole ledger 274's "no stored digest can move" was resting on. It is called after the
      index is resolved now, so it sees that too.
      **What (a) changes for existing callers:** an `mf.evt.array` that omitted `surface`
      and passed no usable context now raises where it used to build. That is the intended
      direction -- what it used to build was maximum ET everywhere -- and it is also what
      makes the declaration lazy-eligible in the commit that follows: the set of
      declarations that raise is the set that becomes a recipe.

284. **Recharge and ET can be declared before their grid exists (2026-09-18).**
      `mf.rch(nper=, recharge=)` and `mf.evt(nper=, rate=, depth=)` without `context=`
      now emit a RECIPE that resolves against whatever grid the build supplies. Measured:
      one declaration built **28 records at ncpl 28 and 92 at ncpl 92**, byte-identical to
      the eager form on each mesh, both packages, both periods -- and `with_grid` reports
      it **`rebuilt`** where it read `stale` before, which is the user-visible point of B2.
      **With `context=` nothing moved.** The eager branch still resolves at declaration
      and still pins.
      **The trigger is exactly the declaration that RAISED**, and that is a rule rather
      than a coincidence: all four target forms refused before, so no stored run can hold
      one and no digest can move. The `.gpkg` commit had the same property for free; the
      array form does NOT, which is why its trigger is narrower still (next entry).
      **The precondition had to be WIDER than the `.gpkg` one, not the same.** A spy grid
      measured the areal builders touching exactly two things -- `context.domain` and
      `grid.ncpl` -- and both are on the built discretization, so demanding a grid object
      would make the lazy form refuse two shapes the EAGER form accepts: a bare
      `ModelContext(domain=idomain)`, and a model declared with no context at all, which
      this repo's own examples use. `_lazy_resolution_context` grew `needs_grid=False`
      rather than a sibling, so the ordering and ncpl-agreement rules stay in one place.
      It also synthesizes an ALL-ACTIVE domain when there is neither a context nor an
      `idomain=` on the discretization -- an absent IDOMAIN means every cell active in
      MF6, so saying so is not a guess -- because otherwise both routes to a cell count
      are None and `_ArealBuilder` dies five frames down naming neither the package nor
      the fix.
      **What a recipe may NOT carry is cell identity the caller chose**: an explicit
      `cells=` list, `name_by_cell=`, a `{cellid: value}` mapping, or a per-cell sequence.
      All four are refused at the call, naming `context=`. The `cells=` list is the sharp
      one -- measured before the refusal, a lazy `cells=[1, 2, 3]` built the SAME three
      records at ncpl 28 and at ncpl 92, reported `rebuilt`, and warned about nothing.
      `name_by_cell` does not even error on another mesh: it MISSES and falls back to a
      generated `<name>_<layer>_<cell>`, and its tuple keys do not survive JSON either.
      These stay available EAGERLY, so this refuses a combination, not a capability.
      **Two defects this commit introduced and the mutation check caught**, both worth
      recording because the obvious test passes through either:
      **(a) binding the partial to `RCHBuilder` narrowed the option check.**
      `_accepted_options` recurses into a partial's bound ARGS and never reads
      `mf6_targets` off the partial itself, so setting that attribute was dead code and
      the accepted set became `RCHBuilder`'s eight parameters -- the lazy branch REFUSED
      `print_input`, `print_flows` and `auxiliary`, real MF6 options the eager branch
      accepts. `lazy == eager` (ledger 279) is broken by NARROWING just as surely as by
      widening, and a test asserting "a typo is refused" passes the whole time. The test
      asserts both directions now, per package and per option.
      **(b) a `package="rch"` keyword on the partial MOVED THE DIGEST.**
      `package_digest` pickles `name` and the builder reference into ONE payload, so they
      share a memo table: a declared spec holds the same INTERNED string in both places
      and pickle emits a back-reference, while a spec revived from JSON holds two distinct
      equal strings and pickle writes it out twice. **168 bytes against 172** -- equal
      values, different digest, and `runs.drift()` would report every reloaded package as
      EDITED permanently. Avoided by keeping `keywords` empty and keying the builder off
      the bound FloPy class. **`package_digest` itself is NOT fixed**: pre-pickling the
      four remaining payload elements would make it memo-independent and would move every
      stored digest, which is a migration rather than a side effect of a feature commit.
      The exposure is narrow -- `options` and `inputs` are already pre-pickled, so a
      collision needs a second string equal to `name` inside the builder reference or
      `requires`, and nothing in the library puts one there. Reproducer:
      `docs/reproducers/digest_pickle_memo.py`.
      **Not carried:** `nper` is still the caller's, and nothing compares it to the
      simulation's `tdis` -- true of the eager form too, and a separate change.

285. **The array form's default could not be written down, which made the whole model
      unsaveable (2026-09-18).**
      `mf.rch.array(recharge=..., context=ctx)` at its DOCUMENTED default resolves
      `irch="top_active"` to an `(ncpl,)` layer-index array, `to_dict` refuses an ndarray
      (ledger 193), and so `Project.save()` persisted **zero simulations** and `load()`
      returned an empty project. **This is ledger 270's defect one package over** --
      exactly what made `mf.disv(stack)` have to be lazy -- and it was invisible until
      270 landed, because before that the hand-written DISV failed first. Measured with a
      lazy `mf.disv(stack)` so the discretization is not the blocker: the array default
      `simulations=0, skipped=1`, `irch=None` and the list form `simulations=1`.
      Declared without `context=` the recipe now holds the STRING and the model saves.
      One declaration produced the same `irch` array as the eager form at ncpl 28 and at
      ncpl 92, `mf.evt.array` likewise including its resolved surface, and `with_grid`
      reads `rebuilt`.
      **The trigger is NARROWER than the list form's, and that is the whole design.**
      A lazy `.gpkg` (279) and a lazy `mf.rch(...)` (284) can key on `context is None`
      because every such declaration RAISED before, so no stored run can hold one. **That
      is not true here**: `mf.rch.array(recharge=..., irch=0 | None | <array>)` with no
      context is legal, working and digestible TODAY. Relocating its payload into
      `inputs` would change `package_digest`, and `project.runs.drift()` would report
      untouched packages as EDITED the first time anyone re-ran their declaring script --
      the exact failure ledger 250 kept the pin out of the digest to avoid. So only the
      parts that genuinely need a grid defer, and they are exactly the parts that raised:
      `irch`/`ievt` left at `"top_active"`, and an omitted EVT `surface` (283). Measured:
      0 of 10 previously-legal declarations moved a digest.
      **Repeating the per-feature refusal in the lazy branch is load-bearing**, and was
      missed first time round: the branch returns before `_array_bc_values`, so
      `mf.rch.array(recharge=mf.Spread(...))` was ACCEPTED at the call and refused at
      BUILD, quietly undoing ledger 283 for every lazy declaration. Same rule as
      `_lazy_bc_spec`'s repeated `path.exists()`: a check that needs no grid belongs at
      the call.
      **`Run.resolution` gained `resolved_cells`.** An array package has neither records
      nor an `ncpl`, so both existing columns said nothing about it -- the same shape
      ledger 280 fixed for the list form.
      **What is still eager-only:** a per-column payload the caller supplies inline
      (`recharge=<ncpl array>`). Laziness cannot rescue it -- an inline array is an
      inline array -- so it stays unsaveable for ledger 193's reason and is classified
      `unverifiable` by ledger 282 rather than moving silently.

286. **A model's own options belong to no package, so importing a run dropped them
      (2026-09-18).**
      Rebuilding specs from a finished MF6 workspace reads each PACKAGE off the loaded
      model. **`NEWTON` is not in a package** -- it is in the model's name-file options
      block -- so a faithful package-by-package rebuild lost it in silence.
      **Measured on a real 18,107-cell model.** With `NEWTON` gone and every cell
      convertible (`icelltype=1` throughout): **90,408 cells converted to DRY straight
      from the initial conditions** (41 conversion blocks; the source run has ZERO),
      recharge on a dry column is skipped so the period-1 rate fell from **2,854,736 to
      1,645 ft3/d**, every head-dependent boundary -- 976 drains, 500 rivers, 263 GHB,
      120 CHD -- contributed **exactly zero**, the budget closed at **200% discrepancy**,
      and the solver diverged: first head change 13,098 ft rising to 143,000 ft in a
      model whose elevations span ~500-900 ft, residual growing monotonically, and
      backtracking frozen. Restoring that ONE option reproduced the source run's
      iteration trace **digit for digit** (`Model 1 79 52.962401`, `2 84 64.871056`,
      `3 84 76.811184`, ...) and the rebuild then ran to Normal termination.
      **The tool that should have caught it was blind in the same place.**
      `model.config` advertises "every package's OPTIONS" and builds its table by
      walking `gwf.packagelist` -- which the name file is not in. So `ref.diff(new)`'s
      config tier compared two runs differing ONLY in `NEWTON` as EQUAL. The extractor
      reads the name file now and `ModelConfig.model` joins `.tdis`/`.ims`/`.oc`.
      **`SimulationBase.model_options`** returns what the model SETS, as `mf.gwf(...)`
      keyword arguments, so the rebuild is `mf.gwf(name, ..., **run.model_options)`.
      Only what is set, so it doubles as a readable answer to "what is switched on".
      **Three traps it had to handle, each measured:**
      (a) FloPy returns `newtonoptions` in more than one nested shape -- `[(True,)]`,
      `[(True, 'UNDER_RELAXATION')]`, `(('NEWTON', 'UNDER_RELAXATION'),)` -- so the
      reader flattens and drops the leading NEWTON marker.
      (b) **`newtonoptions=""` and `[]` write NOTHING AT ALL** (measured on all four
      spellings), so normalizing the bare case to an empty form would drop exactly the
      option this exists to carry while every round-trip test still passed. It returns
      the string `"NEWTON"`.
      (c) `_options_rows` skips every `*filerecord` because an output path is noise in a
      DIFF. It is CONTENT in a rebuild, so this reader keeps them -- the same silent loss
      in miniature, one tier down. A filename option carries the SOURCE model's name,
      which is documented rather than silently rewritten.
      **The deferred import could not be hoisted**, and that is measured rather than
      assumed: `model_config` imports nothing from myflopy but `_logging`, a bare
      `import myflopy` with the import at module level SUCCEEDS, and the test suite's
      import order then hits a circular import through `myflopy.project.__init__`. The
      two call sites share one `_model_config()` accessor so the ratchet stays flat.
      **Still not carried:** the SOLVER. `mf.ims(...)` is hand-rebuilt the same way, and
      the same real model drifted `outer_maximum` 2000 -> 300. `config.ims` has always
      been able to READ it (`mf.load_mf6_run(ws).config.ims["outer_maximum"]`), so unlike
      `NEWTON` this one is visible to anyone who looks -- it wants kwargs shaping, not a
      new reader, and `usg/convert.py:_ims_spec` argues a half-copied solver block is
      worse than a named preset. Left for `project.import_run` (plan D2).

287. **Every PART of a multi-part point was a whole feature (2026-09-18).**
      `cell_shares` divides a feature by its own extent -- length for a line, area for a
      polygon -- and a point has none, so the zero-extent branch handed **every part a
      share of 1.0**. Its own docstring, three paragraphs above, says fractions are of
      the WHOLE feature and sum to less than one where part of it lies outside; so does
      `mf.Spread`'s ("each cell receives ``value * share``, where ``share`` is the cell's
      fraction of the feature"). Both were false for a MultiPoint.
      **Measured on the default path, no `Spread` needed to trigger it and `Spread` no
      help against it:** a MultiPoint of 3 wells declared at `-1000` wrote **-3000**,
      identically wrapped and unwrapped -- and `mf.Spread` exists precisely to conserve a
      feature's total. Worse, a part that reached no cell simply vanished: the same file
      wrote `-2000` with one part 50,000 ft off the grid and `-3000` with all three on
      it, shares summing to 2.0 against 3.0 -- **indistinguishable from a complete
      two-part feature**. It never entered `missed` either, which records only a feature
      reaching ZERO cells, so nothing warned at any level.
      **Only points were affected, and the contrast is what isolates it**: a
      MultiLineString with one part off-grid already summed to 0.5000 and `Spread`
      already wrote `-500.0`, because the extent-based branch divides by the feature's
      own length. Lines and polygons were right the whole time.
      Each part carries `1 / nparts` now, accumulated per cell rather than collapsed into
      a set -- two parts landing on ONE cell owe it both their shares, and a set would
      drop the second and make a complete feature read as truncated. A single point is
      one part and so is unchanged.
      **This CHANGES WRITTEN VALUES** for a multi-part point wrapped in `mf.Spread`:
      the MultiPoint above now writes `-1000.0` where it wrote `-3000.0`, and `-666.7`
      where a third of it is off the grid. That is the number the declaration always
      meant, but a stored run holding such a package will report a moved digest, which is
      correct rather than noise. An UNWRAPPED value is untouched: it is copied whole to
      every cell a feature reaches, by the same documented rule that puts a plain
      conductance on all twelve cells of a polygon.
      **Why it landed before B2 item 7** (user decision, 2026-09-18): that commit's third
      deliverable is a declared-versus-written quantity, and the identity is wrong by a
      factor of N for every multi-part point until this is true. Fixing it inside the
      feature commit would have buried the reproducer, which is what splitting ledger 283
      out of 284 avoided.

288. **A feature that missed the grid was reported through a channel nobody hears
      (2026-09-18).**
      `gaps=` (`"warn"` | `"nearest"` | `"raise"` | `"ignore"`) and `snap_within=` on the
      seven `.gpkg` helpers and on `GeoPackageSource`, the miss moved to
      `warnings.warn`, and per-feature loss accounting in the message and in
      `PackageSpec.metadata`.
      **The channel was the whole of the invisibility, and the mechanism is not what it
      looks like.** `import myflopy` installs a `NullHandler` on the `myflopy` logger and
      root has none, so `Logger.callHandlers` counts a handler as FOUND and never reaches
      `logging.lastResort`, the stderr fallback. Measured: the partial-miss line produced
      **zero bytes** on stderr in a bare session and in a real ipykernel, while
      `warnings.warn` printed. The motivating case reproduced exactly -- 2 wells, one off
      the grid, **90% of the declared pumping gone, zero python warnings**. Both channels
      emit now; `logger.warning` is still right for a configured application.
      **The message had to become DISTINCT or the fix would not have worked.**
      `warnings.warn` dedupes on (text, category, module, lineno), and one GeoPackage
