        package WITH a source reads ``rebuilt`` and never reaches this engine. So the
        remap INHERITS the limitation rather than causing it. (b) The remap needs real
        cell polygons, so it refuses a ``mf.grid_ref`` target by name, leaving a built
        grid object in ``grid=`` -- itself unsaveable (ledger 257).
        **A fully PUBLIC route exists and is now pinned by a test**: remap against the
        built grid, then ``with_grid(mf.grid_ref(key))`` to re-point -- the ``remapped``
        verdict and the arrays both survive, which they do only because ``REMAPPED_FROM``
        is tested BEFORE the cellwise branch -- then ``add_package`` the array and
        ``mf.ref`` it, which is ledger 193's own documented escape hatch. Measured:
        ``simulations=1``, reloads, and a fresh ``prepare_run`` rebuilds the right values.
        What is deferred is collapsing that into one call, which would need a
        serializable carrier for the OLD mesh AND its values.
      * **``runs.drift()`` telling a remap from an edit.** The remapped values move the
        digest and the metadata stamp does not, so every run prepared before the move reads
        ``edited`` with ``source`` reading ``—``. Saying so is better than a stamp-reading
        special case nothing else needs yet.
      * **AMENDED 2026-09-23 (ledger 302):** the line above saying ``uzf``/``sfr``/``lak``/
        ``hfb.line`` are "measured ``stale``, not ``unverifiable`` -- they carry a
        ``grid_pin``" is true only for a declaration carrying a GRID. A GRIDLESS
        ``mf.uzf`` carried no pin at all and read ``unchanged``; ledger 302 closes that.
      * **A coupled pair under ``on=``.** Measured: ``on=`` strands the sibling on the old
        grid, and ledger 268's guard compares node counts and idomain only, so a same-ncpl
        sibling passes it. That is ledger 268's gap rather than this engine's, and
        ``on=None`` -- the default -- moves every model with a grid.
      * **A per-grid-pair weight CACHE**, a byte-identical A->B->A acceptance test, HFB
        through cell polygons, and a reducer for the discretization arrays: each measured
        and rejected during B3's scoping, and each still rejected.

302. **A UZF package declared without a grid moved to another mesh in silence
      (2026-09-23).**
      ``mf.uzf`` resolves its cells from the IDOMAIN and needs no grid -- measured, it
      touches exactly one grid attribute (``get_disv_gridprops``) and only from inside
      ``pin_metadata``, and it builds byte-identical ``packagedata`` against a bare
      ``ModelContext(domain=...)``. That gridless form is legitimate and two tests in
      ``test_uzf_builder.py`` declare it. It was also unclassifiable: no grid meant no
      pin, so ``package_move`` answered **``unchanged`` -- "names no cells"**, and a
      ``with_grid`` from 25 to 81 cells **BUILT CLEAN with 75 UZF objects sitting on
      columns 0..24 of 81** -- UZF over 31% of the domain, zero warnings. The same
      declaration WITH a grid pins and reads ``stale``, and the build refuses it. The
      documented path failed safe and the other one did not.
      **Three independent misses had to line up**, which is why it survived: (a)
      ``pin_metadata`` returns ``{}`` for a context with no grid; (b) ``_cellids_in``
      deliberately walks only ``stress_period_data``, and UZF has none; (c) the
      ncpl-exact fallback reads ``None`` from a UZF record list, because each record's
      second element is a cellid TUPLE and ``column_count``'s nested branch collapses.
      Any one of them holding would have caught it.
      **The fix is the two-branch shape ``_array_bc_spec`` already ships** (ledger 282):
      a PIN when there was a mesh to pin to, the weaker ``CELLWISE_OPTIONS`` marker
      otherwise. Both say "these options address cells"; only the pin can say WHICH mesh,
      so an unpinnable one classifies ``unverifiable`` rather than ``unchanged``.
      **UNCONDITIONAL here, unlike ``_array_bc_spec``'s ``if not cellwise: return spec``.**
      That early exit exists to protect a genuinely grid-free payload --
      ``mf.rch.array(irch=0)`` means the same layer on every mesh. A UZF package with no
      cell-addressing records does not exist: every row carries a cellid at index 1 by
      construction. So nothing legitimate is reclassified.
      **Costs a non-moving model nothing, and that is asserted rather than assumed.**
      ``package_digest`` excludes ``metadata`` by contract, so the stamp moves no digest
      and ``runs.drift()`` reports nothing -- without which closing the hole would have
      reported every stored run as edited on the day it landed (ledger 293's churn).
      **The limit, stated so the commit does not overclaim:** the marker is read by
      ``package_move``, which only ``with_grid`` and ``move_report`` consult. A model
      ASSEMBLED BY HAND against a different grid goes through neither and still builds --
      measured, and pinned by a test. That is the build-time consistency guard's job
      (ledger 249), and it is a range check rather than a proof.
      **Two rejected fixes, each with the reason:**
      * **Refusing a gridless declaration outright.** It would make the eager form
        narrower than the lazy one, which ``_lazy_resolution_context``'s own docstring
        records as the thing not to do (ledger 284) -- a bare ``ModelContext(domain=...)``
        is a supported shape and is correct for any model that never moves.
      * **Pinning from the DOMAIN's SHAPE.** A false pin. A domain shape is
        ``(nlay, ncpl)``, and two genuinely different meshes of the same ncpl fingerprint
        apart under ``grid_pin`` and identically under any shape test -- measured, a 2x8
        and an 8x2 irregular Voronoi both give ``ncpl=16`` with different pins. It would
        claim ``stale``/``rebuilt`` with confidence about a mesh it cannot tell apart,
        which is worse than a marker that only claims "this addresses cells".
      **One wording fix rides along.** The ``unverifiable`` sentence read "nothing can
      tell an ARRAY shaped for this mesh from one shaped for another", which was written
      for ``mf.rch.array`` and is wrong for UZF -- it supplies a RECORD per cell, and it
      is the record's cellid that goes stale, not an array's position. "Payload" covers
      both.

303. **A water mover kept pointing at a reach that no longer existed (2026-09-23).**
      ``mf.mvr``'s records name a provider and a receiver by PACKAGE NAME plus an
      INTEGER -- a reach number, a lake number, a UZF object number. None of the mover's
      OWN options change when the mesh does, so ``package_move`` answered **``unchanged``
      -- "names no cells"** beside a ``stale`` SFR while holding an index into the old
      reach network. Measured: one declaration puts the outlet at reach **9 of 10** on a
      36-cell mesh and **20 of 21** on a 144-cell mesh over the same footprint; after a
      move the mover still said 9, and the report called it a clean move.
      **A provider that is anything but ``unchanged`` invalidates the index, ``rebuilt``
      INCLUDED**, and that is the point rather than an oversight: a rebuilt SFR
      re-intersects its centreline and renumbers every reach, so a CORRECT move of the
      provider is exactly what makes a hand-typed index wrong. Today the provider's own
      pin refuses the build first, which is what has been hiding this -- which also means
      **any commit that makes SFR movable without this one is a net regression**, and
      that is the reason this landed first.
      **``package_move`` cannot see it, by construction**: it is handed ONE package and a
      mover's staleness lives entirely in its siblings. So the second pass is a new
      ``package_moves(packages, ...)``, and **all three** callers go through it --
      ``move_report``, ``ModelSpec.with_grid``'s stamping loop and ``Run.resolution``.
      Updating two of the three would leave the run table and the pre-build report saying
      different things about the same mover, which is the disagreement ``move_report``'s
      own docstring exists to prevent. A mutation reverting just ``with_grid`` fails two
      tests by name.
      **A new metadata key, NOT ``requires=``.** That tuple already means "build this
      first" and ``mf.hfb`` carries it as ``("disv",)``; reading it as an index reference
      would refuse every barrier whenever the discretization rebuilt, which is both wrong
      and constant -- a lazy DISV is always ``rebuilt``. ``INDEXED_PACKAGES`` is stamped
      in ``mvr_spec``, which is the funnel BOTH entry points reach, so
      ``mf.mvr.flopy(...)`` carries it too. **A mutation reading ``requires=`` instead
      passed all sixteen tests** on the first attempt, because a real ``mf.hfb`` is
      PINNED and so reads ``stale``, which the second pass skips -- the distinction only
      shows on a package that reads ``unchanged`` AND carries ``requires``, and the test
      now constructs exactly that and says why it is synthetic.
      **Deliberately conservative about WHICH provider counts.** A reach number is
      mesh-derived and a LAKE number is feature-derived, so a mover into a lake would
      usually survive a move that a mover into a stream would not -- and this names both.
      Two reasons: a lake number is only USUALLY stable, since a lake landing on no active
      cell of the new mesh (ledger 211) is dropped and renumbers the rest; and the errors
      are not symmetric -- a false refusal costs a re-declaration, a false pass routes
      water to the wrong reach under Normal termination.
      **The specific message appears on the PRE-move report only.** After ``with_grid``
      the mover carries ``MOVED_FROM`` and reports through that branch, exactly as every
      other refused package does -- "ALREADY DECIDED, by the ``with_grid`` that stamped
      it" (ledger 271). The pre-build report is the one the docs tell you to read, and it
      is where the sentence naming the providers lands.
      **Costs a non-moving model nothing**, asserted rather than assumed: the stamp is
      metadata, which ``package_digest`` excludes, so no stored digest moves.
      **Not built here:** a ``uzf_connection``. There is none anywhere in the tree and no
      ``MoverConnection("uzf", ...)`` is constructed, so UZF cannot currently be a mover
      endpoint at all -- the key would carry it if one ever appears. And nothing makes
      ``mf.sfr_connection`` SYMBOLIC: it still resolves to an ``int`` at declaration, so
      the mover is refused rather than re-resolved. That is Path A's job, and this entry
      is what makes it safe to do.

304. **`mf.uzf` needed a grid it never used (2026-09-23).**
      Declared without ``context=`` it now resolves at BUILD time, so one declaration
      builds correctly on two meshes and ``with_grid`` reads it ``rebuilt`` where the
      eager form reads ``stale``. Measured: 75 packagedata rows at ncpl 25 and 243 at
      ncpl 81, each byte-identical to a fresh EAGER declaration on that mesh.
      The first of Path A -- making the advanced packages replayable when the caller has
      the sources -- and the cheapest of the four by a wide margin.
      **``needs_grid=False``, and for UZF that is the whole truth rather than a
      concession.** An attribute spy shows ``UZFBuilder.build()`` touching exactly ONE
      grid attribute, ``get_disv_gridprops``, and only from inside ``pin_metadata``: the
      cell set, the ``iuzno`` numbering and ``ivertcon`` all come from the IDOMAIN alone,
      since ``uzf_cells`` walks each column, takes the first active layer as land surface
      and descends while active. So it needs strictly LESS than ``mf.rch`` (ledger 284),
      and demanding a grid would make the lazy form NARROWER than the eager one, which
      accepts a bare ``ModelContext(domain=...)`` and a model with no context at all.
      **That is also the one thing a full test file failed to hold.** Every model in the
      new suite carried ``ModelContext(grid=...)``, so a mutation setting
      ``needs_grid=True`` passed all 35 tests. The case only shows on a model whose mesh
      arrives through a HAND-WRITTEN discretization rather than the context, and the test
      now builds exactly that, twice -- with no context at all and with a domain-only one.
      **The recipe names no FILE**, which is what makes this the cheap one: alone among
      the lazy forms there is no path to anchor, nothing for
      ``project.save(bundle_sources=True)`` to archive, and no ``source_sha`` -- ledger
      293's churn-and-blindness problem cannot arise because there is no content to key
      on. A recipe of scalars also serializes, so a model carrying a lazy UZF **saves**
      where one carrying the eager form persists nothing (records are lists of cellid
      tuples).
      **FLAT, not nested**, for ledger 284's reason: a recipe entry sharing a name with a
      FloPy option -- ``boundnames`` is the live one -- must COLLIDE so
      ``packages.edit``/``with_options`` is refused by name instead of reaching the builder
      twice. A mutation nesting it under one key failed four tests.
      **The resolved package is recorded into ``model._myflopy_resolved``** so the run
      freezes RECORDS rather than the recipe (ledgers 251/270). And it falls back to
      ``disv_pin`` when the resolved context carries no grid: ``UZFBuilder`` pins from
      ``context.grid``, and without the fallback a lazily resolved package would go out
      under ledger 302's weaker cell-addressing MARKER -- which means "could not tell
      which mesh" -- when the built DISV names the mesh exactly.
      **REFUSED at the declaration, each still available with ``context=``:** an explicit
      ``cells=`` list, a per-cell value in any of the thirteen value fields, and
      ``nper < 1``. These are ledger 284's rule applied to UZF's own arguments, through the
      same function -- ``_refuse_caller_typed_cells`` grew a ``value_keys`` parameter
      because the areal helpers and UZF carry different ones (four against thirteen) while
      the RULE is identical.
      **``mover=True`` is refused lazily, and that is not a mechanical limit.** A UZF mover
      endpoint is a hand-typed ``iuzno``, which is an enumeration over the ACTIVE CELLS --
      measured, the column at one location is ``iuzno`` 18-20 on one mesh and 33-35 on
      another, **in range on both**. There is no ``uzf_connection`` anywhere in the tree
      and no ``MoverConnection("uzf", ...)`` is constructed, so nothing could make it
      symbolic. Ledger 303's mover verdict would catch the consequence after the fact;
      refusing the declaration says it at the call.
      **Not built here:** ``mf.sfr`` and ``mf.lak`` recipes (Path A's C5/C6, and SFR needs
      the ``{top, botm}`` fix to ``_layer_elevations`` first -- measured, an
      ``AttributeError`` for both today); ``mf.hfb``, which shares only the api_snapshot
      gate and is on its own track; and a ``uzf_connection``, which would be what unblocks
      ``mover=True``.

301. **A LAK budget could not be read at all on an ordinary output-control setting
      (2026-09-23).**
      Reported as `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'empty'` from
      `msw.packages.lak.budget.get()`. Four defects, one of them on the reporting user's
      own model and unrelated to the crash.
      **THE HEAD FILE'S CLOCK AND A BUDGET FILE'S CLOCK ARE TWO DIFFERENT CLOCKS.** One
      MF6 `OC` `saverecord` sets two INDEPENDENT flags -- `idvsave` from `SAVE HEAD`,
      `icbcfl` from `SAVE BUDGET` (`gwf.f90`) -- and LAK/SFR gate their STAGE file on the
      first while gating their BUDGET file on the second. So within ONE package the two
      outputs follow different schedules, which is almost certainly how
      `budget_tables.package_output_df` came to label package-budget records by zipping
      them positionally against `model.kstpkper`: that IS the right clock for stage, and
      has never been the right one for budget. Measured on a real MF6 run: `SAVE HEAD
      LAST` + `SAVE BUDGET ALL` at `nstp=5` writes **2 head records against 10 LAK budget
      records**. Records are now labelled from the budget file's own `recordarray` under
      FloPy's own `get_indices` mask -- the same selection, in the same file order, that
      `get_data(text=...)` returns, so the two zip exactly.
      **THE SILENT HALF IS WORSE THAN THE CRASH, and no length check could ever see it.**
      `SAVE HEAD STEPS 1` + `SAVE BUDGET STEPS 3` writes **two records each, naming
      different time steps**: head `[(0,0),(0,1)]` against a true LAK clock of
      `[(2,0),(2,1)]`. The lengths agree, so nothing raised and nothing warned, and every
      flow MF6 wrote at step 3 was stamped step 1.
      **A GUARD THAT `continue`s IS NOT A FIX.** The crash reached only LAK's `GWF` term;
      its eight siblings and the whole of SFR were on
      `if not isinstance(raw, pd.DataFrame): continue`, which DROPPED the term. Measured
      on the reporting user's model: `lak.budget.get(term="STORAGE")` returned **0 rows
      where a healthy read gives 38** (q sum -4232.68), and `packages.sfr.budget.get()`
      returned a well-formed, correctly-columned, completely EMPTY frame against a budget
      file holding 8 terms. A plot of that reads as "no flow". Those guards are deleted:
      `bud.get` returns a DataFrame or raises.
      **THE RAW-LIST FALLBACK IS GONE.** `LakBudget.get`/`SFRBudget.get` caught the
      length-check `ValueError`, warned, and returned the raw record list from a method
      documenting a dataframe -- a silent return-type change no caller can guard against.
      `return_df=False` already asks for the list and had zero callers; the fallback had
      zero legitimate users. The warning was effectively invisible: Python's default
      filter is once per `(message, category, module, lineno)` and IPython does not reset
      `__warningregistry__`, so a kernel that hit it once earlier (via a plot) shows only
      a bare `AttributeError` afterwards -- which is what the reporting user saw.
      **A BUDGET FILE IS NOT ALWAYS `<name>.cbc`.** `LoadedMf6Run._get_budget_reader`
      hardcoded the extension. On a real 38-period model whose `OC` says `BUDGET FILEOUT
      tentrails.cbb`, **every** cell-budget surface raised `FileNotFoundError` for a file
      MF6 never wrote -- `model.bud(pkg)`, `model.budget.<term>`,
      `packages.<pkg>.results.q` for all five list BCs, HFB flow. Now read from the OC
      record. Parsed from the `.nam`/`.oc` TEXT rather than from the loaded package,
      because `_ensure_packages_loaded` triggers a FULL FloPy load -- which is the cost
      this accessor exists to avoid. `prt.py`'s `_output_filename` had the rule already.
      **A MODEL WITH TWO PACKAGES OF ONE TYPE OVERRAN THE MODEL-BUDGET CLOCK.** Found by
      sweeping the same shape one tier up rather than by report. `budget_df` zipped a
      package's records against the budget file's UNIQUE save times, which is one per
      record only when the model has ONE package of that type. The reporting user's model
      declares two `RIV6` entries -- a main stem and a named tributary -- so the file holds
      **76 RIV records against 38 save times** and `model.bud("riv").df` raised
      `IndexError` on record 38. Labelled from the same per-text selection that produced
      the records now; the two packages' cells merge into one `riv` table, which is what
      `packages.riv.results.q` already did.
      **TWO CLOCKS SHARED ONE CACHE SLOT.** `LoadedMf6Run._get_budget_kstpkper` cached the
      model-budget clock into `_kstpkper`, the attribute `accessors.get_kstpkper` caches
      the HEAD clock into, so whichever was touched first answered for both for the life
      of the object -- both directions measured wrong on a 6-head/2-budget model. Split
      into `_budget_kstpkper`. `SimulationBase._get_budget_kstpkper` does not cache and
      was never affected; that asymmetry is what hid it.
      **WHY THE SUITE NEVER SAW ANY OF THIS: every `saverecord` in `tests/` is
      symmetric** -- both `ALL` or both `LAST` -- so the two clocks were equal in every
      fixture and the mismatch branch had never executed under test. Not one test drove
      `packages.lak.budget.get()` at all. `tests/test_budget_clocks.py` is deliberately
      asymmetric, and each test asserts the mismatch ACTUALLY HOLDS before asserting the
      behaviour (ledger 96's lesson); all five fixes are certified by reverting each one
      and watching a NAMED test fail. It costs 1.1 s. Nothing in the suite had two
      packages of one type in a budget-reading test either.
      **NOT FIXED, and recorded rather than quietly left:**
      * **The STAGE-clock family, ~12 sites, same root shape.**
        `LakStageOutput.get` reshapes with no clock at all and
        `build_lak_stage_result_table` labels `per` by SAVED-RECORD INDEX (measured
        `per = 0..5` on a 2-period model; a `LakeStageTargets` keyed by period reads
        through it, ledger 331); `group/lak.py` pairs stage records with
        `model.kstpkper` and truncates; `group/sfr.py` decodes `SFRStageOutput`'s
        reach-indexed frame as if it were LAK's time-indexed array, so `per=` and `reach=`
        both select the wrong thing; `_coerce_kstpkper` and `XSection.__init__` index the
        head-clock LIST by a stress-period number, which is only correct at one save per
        period; `budget_tables.sfr_stage_df` reshapes by `model.nper` and raises;
        `budget_obs_df` swallows the mismatch with `except KeyError: continue`.
        Scoped OUT by the user to keep this pass to the reported defect. They are a
        genuinely larger surface -- the group tier and the PEST observation path -- and
        each needs its own measured fixture. `SFRStageOutput.get`
        (`modflow/utils/outputs.py`) is the reference pattern to converge them on: it
        already labels from its own reader's `get_kstpkper()`.
      * **`budget_tables.lake_stage_array` is a dead duplicate** of
        `LakStageOutput.get`, carrying the same false "(nper, nlakes)" docstring, with no
        caller anywhere. Left alone rather than deleted in a bug-fix pass.
      * **`locs.filter_cells_by_pkg` reads the head clock to index a budget-indexed
        frame, AND falls off the end returning `None` unconditionally.** No callers
        anywhere, so nothing is broken today; it is deleted-or-fixed work, not this.
      * **`_kstpkper` is still never invalidated.** Nothing resets it -- not
        `run_simulation`, not `Run.execute` (`Run.open` clears `_model_views`, `execute`
        does not) -- while `get_hds` rebuilds its reader on EVERY access, so the heads
        refresh and their clock does not. That is how the reporting user's object got a
        short clock in the first place: a read taken while MF6 was still writing, 23
        minutes before the run finished. Left because invalidation needs a decision about
        where a run's "outputs changed" signal lives, which is bigger than this fix, and
        because with the clock corrected a stale `_kstpkper` no longer reaches any budget
        table. `model._kstpkper = None` still clears it; so does reloading the run.

305. **A map of an unrun model drew node numbers, and so did any `type` it did not know (2026-09-23).**
      Two silent fallbacks shared one symptom -- the values 0..ncpl-1 under a colorbar:
      ``_grid_of`` bound a model to the map only when it had RESULTS, so an unrun model was
      drawn as a bare grid (``type='ks'`` could not read K, and ``select="all_streams"``
      fell through to opening a FILE of that name); and ``type`` was never checked, so a
      typo, ``'trans'``, the documented ``'rch'`` (no branch) and ``'HDS'`` (one lookup
      lower-cased, the other not) all reached the cell-index branch. Measured on the
      canonical model, each drew ``arange(441)``.
      **Two questions, two attributes.** ``Choro.model`` still means "whose RESULTS";
      ``_inputs`` means "whose inputs and names" and falls back to an input-only model the
      free verb passes when the source is a model without results. K, idomain, layer
      elevations and region names read from ``_inputs``. The results binding is
      deliberately NOT faked for an unrun model -- the heads hover, the timing reader and
      the animation clock all assume results and would each have needed a guard.
      **A results map of an unrun model now RAISES** (``type`` in ``hds``/``conc``/``temp``/
      ``rch`` with no ``values=``), naming the input spellings. It used to draw node
      numbers under a head colorbar, so nothing correct depended on it -- but it is a
      behaviour change for any script that called ``model.plot.map()`` before running.
      ``values=`` still draws on any model.
      **``'rch'`` now draws what it documented** (output recharge, the ``'output_rch'``
      branch; the latter stays as an undocumented alias). **CORRECTED by ledger 311:**
      that branch shifted every rate onto the PREVIOUS cell, and the test written here
      compared ``'rch'`` against ``'output_rch'`` -- the same function -- so it passed on
      wrong data; it now compares against FloPy's own budget-file reader. **``'input_rch'`` is RETIRED by
      name**: it read ``stress_period_data.data[37]`` whatever period was asked and raised
      ``KeyError`` on any model with fewer periods; nothing in ``src/``, ``tests/`` or the
      live notebooks used it, and the noun ``packages.rch.inputs.recharge`` maps declared
      recharge for any period. Its reader was deleted rather than kept unreachable.
      **``layer`` is checked at the call**: ``layer=4`` on 4 layers and ``layer=None``
      built a picture that died at ``.fig``, and ``layer=-1`` drew the BOTTOM layer through
      numpy's negative indexing. ``-1`` keeps its one meaning, "above ground", beside
      ``show_mounding=True``. A bare grid has no layer count, so there the value is only
      type-checked, as it was never checked before.
      **``type`` is now swept both ways** (``tests/test_map_unrun_and_type.py``): the
      documented set equals the accepted one minus the ``'output_rch'`` alias.
      ``test_plot_vocabulary``'s value sweep still excludes ``type`` for its own reason
      (``conc``/``temp`` need a GWT/GWE model), which is why the sweep lives beside the
      check rather than there.
      **Not done:** ``'ks'`` on a GWT/GWE model still fails at render inside FloPy (the
      transport model has no NPF) -- pre-existing; the transmissivity types that follow
      refuse by name there instead.

306. **The composers named `zmin`/`zmax` and pooled over them; the static ones dropped every overlay (2026-09-23).**
      Measured on the canonical model: ``hds.mosaic(by="layer", zmin=100, zmax=120)`` put
      the shared axis at 79.04..153.76 on BOTH backends (``npf.k.mosaic(zmin=1, zmax=10)``
      at 0.02..59.74), while ``animate`` honoured the same arguments -- the composers have
      named both since ledger 258, forwarded them to every panel, and then pooled the
      colour axis over the data regardless. And ``_mpl_mosaic``/``_mpl_animation``
      re-plotted each panel's cells with ``gdf.plot`` instead of calling the panel's own
      static renderer, so ``npf.k.mosaic(backend="mpl", features=..., select=...)`` drew
      one collection per panel where ``npf.k.map(backend="mpl", ...)`` draws three.
      **The rule: a caller-set limit beats the pooled one, each side independently, and
      the WIDEST across panels wins.** Widest because panels a caller built separately
      may disagree, and a bar that clips one of them misreports it; per side because
      ``zmin`` alone must not freeze the top. That rule also CLOSES ledger 71's
      centering half: a ``change`` panel carries symmetric limits about 1x, the widest
      of symmetric pairs is symmetric, so a hand-built mosaic of them keeps its white
      point at 0.5 without ``diff=True`` (pinned by a test). IES ``mean``/``std`` panels
      set no limits, so their mosaics are unchanged.
      **One static renderer.** Both static composers now call
      ``Choro.plot_mpl(ax=, norm=, colorbar=False)``, which gained ``norm=`` for exactly
      this. Anything a static map learns to draw -- ``extent=`` next -- reaches every
      panel and frame without a third copy of the drawing code.
      **Not done:** the static animation still draws no colorbar (it never has; a
      colorbar beside an axis that ``clear()``s every frame needs its own axes), and
      ``plot_mpl`` still draws no contours, so a static mosaic of contoured panels
      loses them silently -- both pre-existing.

307. **A plotly map was fitted for a canvas nothing draws (2026-09-23).**
      ``_initial_map_zoom`` assumed a 1000x700 viewport and no caller ever passed a size.
      Measured in a browser (MapLibre ``getBounds``) on the canonical model: a single map
      at 1084x584 showed 88.6% of the grid's height; every panel of a 4-panel
      ``hds.mosaic`` showed ~10% of the grid, because each subplot got the SINGLE-map
      zoom; ``.save("x.png")`` at kaleido's 700x500 kept 78.6% of the height. A
      ``hillshade_path=`` then reset every view to zoom 12 centred on the RASTER, after the
      fit, overriding ``fit_bounds`` and an explicit ``zoom`` alike.
      **The rule: fit the canvas plotly will draw -- the figure's own ``width``/``height``
      when it names them, else plotly.js's OWN defaults (700x450) -- less the resolved
      margins, times the subplot's domain** (``viz.map_canvas``). **AMENDED by ledger
      311:** "the resolved margins" must be the ones plotly DRAWS, which it grows for a
      colorbar and an animation's controls after the fit -- the declared ones made the
      fitted canvas the LARGER one. The real inline size is
      unknowable from Python (an inline figure is as wide as its notebook cell), and the
      asymmetry decides it: fitting a canvas SMALLER than the real one only adds margin,
      fitting a larger one crops. So a wide notebook shows the grid with room around it,
      never cut off.
      **A map mosaic now sets its height** (320 px per row plus plotly's margins): the
      default 450 px was the WHOLE figure, ~115 px per row on a 2x2 grid once plotly's own
      margins were taken -- a canvas too small to be worth fitting.
      **A PNG is refitted for the export's size** (``Picture.save`` asks the picture for
      ``export_map_view(size)``, kaleido's defaults when the caller names none) and the
      screen view is put back after -- deep-copying a ``viz.Fig`` to avoid the swap returns
      an EMPTY figure (measured), so the swap is the safe form.
      **One centre**: the standalone map centred on the grid's area centroid while the
      subplots used the bounding-box midpoint; both use the midpoint now, the only one that
      keeps a fitted box inside the view on an irregular domain.
      **Not done, deliberately:** a JavaScript ``map.fitBounds`` post-script, which would
      make ``show()``/``html()`` exact. It reaches MapLibre through plotly's private
      ``_fullLayout.map._subplot.map``, and inline notebook display -- where this user
      works -- runs no post-scripts at all (``Fig._repr_mimebundle_`` merges only
      ``config``), so it would fix the environments that already show the whole grid under
      the default-size rule. ``layout.map.bounds`` is not the answer either: measured, it
      is MapLibre's ``maxBounds`` pan lock, which COVERS the box (cropping to 56% of its
      latitude) and clamps zoom-out.

308. **Transmissivity maps and nouns: saturated by default, and the choices behind it (2026-09-23).**
      ``model.plot.map(type="trans" | "trans_max")`` and
      ``model.packages.npf.transmissivity`` / ``.transmissivity_max``, one computation
      (``modflow/mf6/hydraulics.model_transmissivity``, import layer 0) that all four read.
      **SATURATED IS THE DEFAULT -- the user's decision, against the scoping's
      recommendation** of geometric K x b. The two differ where it matters: on the
      canonical model the water-table layer's saturated/full ratio has median 0.404, and
      15 of 441 cells are zero (head below the layer bottom, kept wet by NEWTON). The
      maximum is the option (``trans_max``), and the one an unrun model can draw; a
      saturated map of an unrun model raises NAMING it.
      **The thickness is MF6's, not "head minus bottom" everywhere**: ICELLTYPE != 0 ->
      ``min(head, top) - bottom`` floored at 0; ICELLTYPE 0 -> the full thickness whatever
      the head; ICELLTYPE < 0 under THICKSTRT -> from the STARTING head. Measured against
      MF6's own ``DATA-SAT`` at every saved time: max difference 5e-7 (the binary's
      precision), confined layers included. ``idomain <= 0`` is a gap -- MF6 removes a
      ``-1`` pass-through cell from horizontal flow as well as a ``0``.
      **K is ``npf.k``**, the major-axis horizontal conductivity the house labels "Kh".
      ``k22``/``angle1`` anisotropy is not folded in: a T along the minor axis is a
      different quantity, and none of the models here set ``k22``.
      **Spellings (user):** the nouns are the per-layer mosaic
      (``npf.transmissivity.mosaic()``), NOT ``model.plot.mosaic(type=)`` -- the free
      mosaic takes finished pictures, and giving it a subject would break the pinned
      free/bound mirror. ``trans_max`` is spelled the same on the map and as a noun.
      **The nouns draw THROUGH the free map** (``StaticArrayFieldExplorer._map_type``),
      so there is one picture and one hover (T in the model's units, from DIS/TDIS -- a
      product of two units, so never guessed -- with K and the thickness under it).
      They are properties on ``NpfPackageExplorer``, not entries in the declared field
      table: that table is what the package file STORES, which ``summary()`` and
      ``ModelPackages.mosaic`` enumerate.
      **The noun's ``per`` is the period's LAST saved step**; an exact
      ``kstpkper``/``per_timestep`` is the free map's (``model.plot.map(type="trans",
      kstpkper=...)``). Naming those two on the noun would have meant overriding its
      ``map`` -- a second 25-parameter signature and a new docstring target -- for a
      selector the free verb already carries.
      **Deleted as unfalsifiable:** a mask turning MF6's no-head sentinels into zero
      thickness. A dry ACTIVE cell's head is DHDRY (-1e30), below every bottom, so the
      clip already gives zero; a mutation removing the mask passed every test.
      **DEFERRED:** total transmissivity over layers (``layer="total"`` would widen
      ``layer`` at every scope, where it is pinned an int); groups and diffs have no
      ``npf`` noun at all, so comparing T across scenarios is not reachable.

309. **`extent=` -- the window a map opens on, at every scope and backend (2026-09-24).**
      Asked for by the user because a Matplotlib map cannot be zoomed. **Three rules are
      the user's:** an extent sets the VIEW only -- no cell is cropped and the colour scale
      still spans the whole field, although a 1/16-area window measured using a median 25%
      of the ramp (a quarter window ~60%); ``zmin``/``zmax`` is the lever for a close-up,
      which is why ledger 306 made the composers honour them first. One extent frames
      every panel of a mosaic; a LIST frames each panel on its own. And it is a box,
      points, a geometry's bounds, or a NAME (the name lookup lands with the area
      registry; the resolver already takes a ``names`` mapping).
      **One resolver, run at the call** (``utils/datatypes/extent.resolve_extent``, import
      layer 1), so a bad box raises where it was typed, like ``select=``. Numbers and bare
      geometries are in the GRID's CRS, the ``features=`` rule; a ``GeoDataFrame`` is
      reprojected from its own. The box is densified before it goes to WGS84, since its
      edges are not straight there.
      **Shapely order, and the trap it cannot close:** ``(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)``, as
      ``LayerStack.draft_grid(extent=)`` already had it. FloPy's and matplotlib's
      ``(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)`` is REFUSED only when it produces an inverted box; when
      it happens to be a valid box inside the grid -- ``(500, 1000, 600, 1100)`` on the
      canonical model -- it frames the wrong window in silence. No check can tell.
      **What refuses by name:** an inverted box, a box off the grid (both boxes and both
      CRSs printed -- a lon/lat box given to a feet model lands here), a geometry with no
      area (a point frames nothing), a list given to a single map or to ``animate`` (one
      view), ``fit_bounds=False`` beside an extent (it IS a fit), and a list of the wrong
      length (naming the panels).
      **A list is told from one extent by its ITEMS, never its length** -- four numbers
      are one box, four ``(x, y)`` pairs one set of points, four boxes or four names one
      per panel. The rule lives in ``viz.is_extent_list`` because the free ``mosaic`` is
      ``viz.mosaic`` and ``viz`` imports nothing from myflopy.
      **Panels on different windows are not synced.** The sync script copies ABSOLUTE
      centre and zoom, so the first pan would snap every panel to one window;
      ``sync_views`` now defaults to ``None`` (sync exactly when the panels share a
      window) on ``viz.mosaic``, ``ModelPlots.mosaic`` and ``SpatialView.mosaic``, and an
      explicit ``True`` with different windows raises.
      **Renderers:** plotly reads ``Choro.latlon_bounds``/``map_view`` (so the standalone
      map, mosaic subplots, animation frames and ledger 307's PNG refit all follow);
      ``Choro.plot_mpl`` sets the padded limits LAST, and only when an extent was given --
      a default static map still autoscales, including out to a feature off the grid.
      The static mosaic and animation draw through ``plot_mpl`` (ledger 306) and the PNG
      animation renders each frame through it, so they needed nothing further. The PRT
      plan view (FloPy's ``PlotMapView``) and the stack thickness map each set the same
      padded box; both still refuse every OTHER base-map option.
      **NOT on the ``grid`` verb** (the bare 2-D mesh / 3-D volume): it is not a map of
      values, and giving it ``extent=`` changes its signature at four scopes and its chain
      of mirrored defaults. Nor on ``section``/``surface``, which are not plan views.
      **Not built:** the JavaScript ``fitBounds`` (ledger 307's reason), so an inline
      notebook figure still frames by the default-canvas estimate.

310. **Named areas of interest: defined on the model, kept by the project (2026-09-24).**
      ``model.aoi`` / ``project.aoi`` -- an ``AoiLibrary`` of ``mf.Area`` (a geometry and
      the CRS it is in) -- and ``add_aoi(name, place)`` on both. A name works wherever a
      place does: ``extent="site"``, ``select="site"``, ``features=model.aoi``.
      **The user's design, and the three calls it settled:** areas are DEFINED ON THE
      MODEL and propagate to the project when the model belongs to one; they are
      ``model.aoi``, NOT ``model.plot.aoi`` (``model.plot`` holds exactly the six drawing
      verbs, and areas serve arrays and selections too); and a model with no LIVE project
      -- a bare ``load_run``, a later session -- keeps what it adds for the session ONLY.
      Only ``project.save()`` writes a project's files; a model that wrote them would be
      the one place that did.
      **How a model finds its project: a WEAK, root-keyed registry, not injection.** The
      scoping planned to hand the live library to each ``Run`` at construction -- and the
      critic found FIVE construction paths (``prepare_run``, ``reopen_run``,
      ``RunLibrary.discover`` behind ``project.runs[...]``, ``discover_runs``,
      ``discover_native_runs``), which is five places to forget one. Instead a live
      ``Project`` registers its library under its root in ``myflopy.areas`` (import layer
      0, so the model -- layer 8 -- can reach it without importing the workspace, layer
      10), and ``Run.model`` records ``view._project_root``. Weak, so a view never keeps
      a project alive; by ROOT, so several projects in one session never collide.
      **Found when moved:** a copied project's runs still record the ORIGINAL root, so a
      model also looks at ``<workspace>/../..`` for a ``project.json``. **AMENDED by
      ledger 312:** the project a run physically LIVES IN is asked FIRST (nearest
      ancestor), and the registry holds every live library of a root, newest first.
      **Saved INLINE** in ``project_spec.json`` as WKT + CRS at FULL precision (shapely
      rounds WKT to 6 decimals by default -- ~0.1 m on a lon/lat vertex), like an eager
      package: the file an area came from is read once and kept only as provenance, so an
      archive needs nothing extra and a lower import layer reads saved areas straight from
      the JSON (``areas.saved_areas``) without loading the project. A project saved before
      this loads with none.
      **``crs=None`` means the grid's frame** -- the ``features=`` rule -- and is never
      filled in with ``DEFAULT_CRS``, so a box typed in model coordinates lands where it
      was typed; a file or frame keeps its own CRS and a conflicting ``crs=`` raises
      rather than relabelling it.
      **Assignment coerces** (``model.aoi["x"] = (0, 0, 10, 10)`` stores an ``Area``) and
      replaces, as a dict does; ``add_aoi`` refuses an existing name unless
      ``overwrite=True`` (ledger 208's rule). Registration goes through ``add_aoi``, not a
      public ``.add`` on the library, per the libraries' design.
      **Names are looked up only when a NAME is passed:** ``model.aoi`` can open the
      project's saved spec, so a box, a geometry or a cell list never asks (pinned).
      ``select=`` tries a region, then an area, then a file; a name that is BOTH a region
      and an area is refused rather than guessed (a region is cells, an area a shape --
      they need not select the same cells), and a name that is none of them now raises
      listing both sets instead of pyogrio's ``DataSourceError: No such file``.
      **The trap that nearly shipped:** every "no live project" test first passed because
      the pytest fixture held the ``Project``, keeping it in the weak registry -- two
      mutations survived. The tests now build and drop the project inside the test and
      assert ``live_areas(root) is None`` first.
      **NOT built:** areas in ``hds.get(cells=)``, a section line from a named
      LineString, ``Surface.within``/zones, a clipped ``to_xugrid``, and a bridge turning
      an area into a model region -- each is a later wiring of the same library.

311. **An adversarial review of 305-310: the map defects the tests certified rather than checked (2026-09-24).**
      A 3-reviewer / skeptic-per-finding review of the six commits; every confirmed finding
      reproduced independently, none was refuted. The theme worth carrying: in each case a
      test was written against the code's own model of the answer.
      **``type='rch'`` drew each cell's recharge on the PREVIOUS cell (high).**
      ``bud('rch').df`` is ZERO-based over the whole model and the reader subtracted one
      more, so map[i] == truth[i+1] (166 of 441 cells); it also matched on the whole node,
      dropping recharge applied below layer 1. The shift predates this work in
      ``'output_rch'``; ledger 305 routed the DOCUMENTED ``'rch'`` onto it and tested
      ``'rch'`` against ``'output_rch'`` -- the same function. Now ``node % ncpl``,
      ``bincount``, and a test against FloPy's own ``CellBudgetFile``.
      **A saturated-T map drew its FIRST time forever.** The cache had no key, so every
      ``.ani`` frame and a reassigned ``per`` showed the first kstpkper's field under an
      advancing footer. Keyed by ``(type, kstpkper)``.
      **``map_canvas`` fitted the DECLARED margins; plotly draws wider ones.** Measured in
      a browser: the colorbar grows a standalone map's right margin 0 -> 81 px, an
      animation's controls grow both sides to 80 px -- so a wide window showed 97.3% / 91.4%
      of itself. ``COLORBAR_MARGIN`` (100) and ``CONTROLS_MARGIN`` (80) are reserved now;
      after the fix every picture CONTAINS its window (standalone 1.135x, animation 1.142x,
      mosaic panels 1.113x at 5% padding). The tests had taken ``map_canvas`` itself as the
      truth; they now assert on the literal DRAWN canvases (619x430, 540x310), with
      ``bounds_padding=0`` and a WIDE window -- on the square canonical grid height is always
      the tighter axis, so a width error was invisible, and 5% padding absorbed the
      controls' 10 px. Reproducer: ``docs/reproducers/map_canvas_margins.py``.
      **``Picture.save`` fitted the figure's size over the caller's, restored an ALIASED
      centre, and overwrote a view the caller set.** An explicit ``save(width=)`` wins now,
      as it does in plotly's ``to_image``; the restore holds plain copies (``layout.map
      .center`` is a live object ``update_layout`` mutates in place -- pinned on a stub,
      since a map's own export centre equals its screen one); and a view the caller MOVED
      on ``.fig`` is written as it stands (``Choro._fitted_view``).
      **Lower findings, also fixed:** a diff mosaic with one caller-set limit filled the
      other side with the raw data max and dropped the zero centre on plotly while the
      static backend mirrored the pooled magnitude -- both mirror now; a composer
      ``extent=`` over panels drawn with ``fit_bounds=False`` is refused, as a single map
      refuses it; the PRT pathline and capture mosaics, the IES field mosaic and
      ``model.packages.mosaic`` hand ``extent=`` to ``viz.mosaic`` instead of to every panel
      (a list had raised "only a mosaic can use" from inside a mosaic, and
      ``packages.mosaic`` had swallowed a bad box per panel into "no package could be
      drawn") -- their ``sync_views`` default to ``None`` like the rest; a bare grid given a
      field ``type`` raises instead of drawing node numbers under its colorbar;
      ``npf.transmissivity.long()/wide()`` key on the period (they repeated every
      ``(layer, cell)`` once per period) and ``map(per=None)`` is the default time.

312. **The same review, for the areas of interest: who a model's project is (2026-09-24).**
      Ledger 311's review, its ``areas`` findings -- three confirmed, one proven and not
      yet verified, three low -- each now pinned by a test that fails without its fix.
      **A copied project's models used the ORIGINAL's areas, and ``add_aoi`` wrote into
      the original.** The recorded root was asked first, and a copy's runs record the
      original's. Now the project a run physically LIVES IN wins: the NEAREST ancestor of
      its workspace that is a live root or holds a ``project.json`` -- which also finds the
      runs the old ``<workspace>/../..`` guess could not (``runs/scenarios/x``,
      ``imports/usg/converted``, a discovered run or a ``load_mf6_run`` that records no
      root at all, on an UNSAVED live project).
      **A second, short-lived ``Project`` of one root unregistered the first.** A single
      weak slot per root: the newcomer overwrote it and, when collected, removed it. The
      registry keeps every live library of a root, NEWEST alive first.
      **``project.aoi = project.aoi | {...}`` disconnected every model** -- the registry
      held the old object. ``Project.aoi`` is a property whose setter re-registers.
      **``|=``, a reflected ``|`` and the constructor bypassed the coercion**, storing raw
      tuples that broke ``save()`` AFTER it had written ``project.json`` and before the
      spec -- so a first save left a manifest naming a missing file, which ``load``
      refuses. ``AoiLibrary.__init__``/``__ior__`` coerce; and ``save()`` now builds the
      document BEFORE writing anything.
      **Also:** ``mf.plot.Feature(area, color=...)`` crashed (only the bare
      ``features=area`` spelling knew areas); ``Area.coerce(area, crs=26910)`` refused
      ``"EPSG:26910"`` as a relabel (compared as strings; now ``pyproj`` equality).
      **Still true, stated:** "nearest ancestor with a ``project.json``" can name an
      UNRELATED project that happens to enclose a model's directory; a run inside a
      project's tree is the case it is built for.

313. **Transmissivity is written as a whole number with separators: 112,000 ft²/d (2026-09-24).**
      The user's request: the hover wrote the house's four significant digits, so
      ``1.12e+05 ft²/d``. Now ``112,000`` -- the WHOLE number, not three significant
      figures of it -- in the hover (the value, the per-layer strip and table) and on every
      colorbar: plotly single maps (d3 ``","``), log bars (decade and fallback labels with
      separators), the mosaic's and animation's pooled bars, and the static single and
      mosaic bars.
      **Transmissivity ONLY.** K and thickness keep significant digits (a K of 0.001 would
      read 0), and every other map's ticks are unchanged -- ``HoverSpec.formats`` is per
      FIELD and ``Choro.number_style`` is ``"thousands"`` only for the two
      transmissivity types. **Below 1 it keeps significant digits**, so the canonical
      aquitard's 0.24 ft²/d does not read as 0 -- a judgment call on "whole number", since
      rounding there would erase the value.
      **One rule, ``hover.format_number(style="thousands")``;** the static bars format
      through it (``hover.thousands_formatter``). ``viz`` cannot import ``hover`` (both are
      import layer 0), so the plotly side is d3's own ``","`` plus the decade labels --
      expressions of the same rule, pinned by tests, not a second implementation of it.
      **Not done:** the noun tables (``get()``/``summary()``) stay numeric -- a formatted
      string there would break arithmetic -- and the static animation still draws no
      colorbar (ledger 306).

314. **A 3-D surface was drawn across every concavity of its domain, and the heatmap beside it was upside down (2026-09-24).**
      Reported as ``InterpolatedSurface(xs, ys, zs, vor).show()`` looking "clipped to a
      convex hull but not the actual domain" while ``plot_heatmap()`` was clipped.
      **Nothing masked ``.fig``** -- it was ``clipped_fig(clip=False)`` -- so its edge was
      ``griddata``'s: NaN outside the convex hull of the points, which spans every
      concavity of a domain that is not convex. On an L, 15,406 of 72,141 drawn pixels
      (21.4%) lay outside the model.
      **``.fig``, ``surface_trace()`` and ``stack.plot.surface`` (both backends) now draw
      ``clipped_surface``**: masked to ``clip=``, else the grid's FOOTPRINT; a bare point
      cloud has neither and is drawn as interpolated. ``clipped_fig(clip=)`` defaults to
      ``None`` (mask when there is a region); ``clip=False`` is the spelling for the old
      picture, and ``clip=True`` with no region raises. **One mask rule** -- pixel centre
      inside, ``geometry_mask`` on ``transform``, which is what ``rasterio.mask.mask``
      applies -- so the figure, the heatmap and a saved raster keep the same pixels, and a
      test holds them equal.
      **The heatmap's clip had three defects of its own.** ``transform`` put a pixel CORNER
      on the first cell centre, where ``xy_meshgrid`` puts a pixel CENTRE, so the clip was
      tested half a pixel east and south of what is drawn (177 pixels wrong on the L). A
      saved GeoTIFF and ``XSection(interpolate=True)``'s samples sat there too, so BOTH
      MOVE by half a pixel now -- a correction, but a change in their numbers. The clip
      filled with 0 and ``clipped_fig``/``save_raster`` then turned every 0 into NaN
      (38,004 real zeros erased on a linearND field); the fill is NaN and the in-memory
      raster declares NaN no-data. And ``plot_heatmap`` gave plotly no ``y``, so row 0 --
      the NORTH edge -- was drawn at the bottom. It is drawn on the model's x/y now, north
      up, at one unit to one unit (a judgment call: a map in real coordinates that
      stretches is still wrong), with the outside blank rather than the value 0 that
      dragged its colour scale down.
      **``clip=`` now reaches the drawn surface, and a ``str`` path or a ``MultiPolygon`` is
      no longer dropped** by a setter that had no branch for them; any other type raises.
      Supplied ``zs`` no longer resolve the clip's cells first -- that needs a grid, which
      the stack's ``clip=`` comes without, and it refused a point cloud that never came
      from one. **A mask that leaves nothing to draw RAISES**, naming both extents: points
      and a region that do not meet are a location or a CRS, and an empty scene says neither.
      **Not done, deliberately.** The RIM: up to half a cell inside the boundary, past the
      outermost centres, there is no interpolated value (859 pixels on the L); masking
      removes overshoot, not this, and filling it is extrapolation -- ledger 248's call. The
      footprint is every cell, ACTIVE OR NOT, as ``plot_heatmap`` always used, so a head
      surface still spans an inactive region inside it. ``memfile`` (what ``XSection``
      samples) stays unmasked. ``plot_heatmap`` still shows and returns ``None``, the pre-8.1
      shape; making it a ``Picture`` is a separate change to a ``plot_foo()`` the view layer
      would not add today.
      **A faithful mask shows the grid's own holes:** ``GridSpec.voronoi`` leaves a 77.4 ft²
      gap in its footprint at the L's inner corner, and the surface is blank there. The gap
      is FloPy's ``tri2vor``, and general at reflex corners: ledger 316.
      Reproducer: ``docs/reproducers/surface_domain_mask.py``; tests:
      ``tests/test_surface_domain_mask.py``, where each of fifteen single-piece mutations of
      the fix fails a named test.

315. **A head surface kept every DRY cell as a sample at -1e30 and erased real heads above 10,000 ft; the head map and the plain section still keep -1e30 (2026-09-24).**
      ``InterpolatedSurface.zs`` cut MF6's no-value sentinels at ``> 10_000``. A DRY cell's
      -1e30 (measured, non-Newton) is not above 10,000, so it stayed a sample, and the cubic
