      (``rbf`` overshoots by 0.16 ft, as it does on any field); a dry region at the
      domain's edge draws blank, not extrapolated into (ledger 248's call).
      **One rule, ``headsplus._is_sentinel``: ``|value| >= 1e29``, both signs** (MF6 writes
      +1e30 inactive, -1e30 dry). A judgment call where the brief could not be followed as
      written: it asked to reuse a masking helper in ``headsplus.py``, and there was none,
      only three inline copies, ``get()``'s ``>= 1e29`` and ``array()``/``to_xugrid()``'s
      ``> 1e29``. All three and the surface now share the helper, so ``array()`` and
      ``to_xugrid()`` also blank a value of exactly 1e29, which MF6 never writes.
      ``interactive_plotting._clean_head_values``, ``canonical.py`` and ``parallel.py`` keep
      their own copies of the same ``1e29`` rule, untouched.
      **Not fixed here, measured on the same run.** ``hds.map()`` (``choros.py``) blanks
      only ``== 1e30``, so a dry cell maps and hovers as -1e30, and with no ``zmin``/``zmax``
      the colour range is -1e30 to 50: every wet cell draws one colour. Its mounding branch
      reads a dry cell as 0, since the negative is clipped. Whether that should be 0 or
      blank is the design fork that kept the map out of this change. ``hds.section()``
      without ``interpolator=`` masks nothing: 6 of 14 head points at -1e30. With
      ``interpolator=`` it samples this surface and is fixed. Revisit when either is next
      touched; the rule to use is the same helper.
      Reproducer: ``docs/reproducers/head_surface_sentinels.py``; tests:
      ``tests/test_raster_nodata.py``, where reverting the surface fix fails the five tests
      that read a real MF6 run, by name.

316. **``GridSpec.voronoi`` cells do not tile a boundary with a reflex corner: two defects in FloPy's ``tri2vor``, measured and NOT yet repaired (2026-09-24).**
      Ledger 314's 77.4 ft² hole at the L's inner corner is the grid, and the grid is
      FloPy's: ``gdf_vorPolys`` is ``tri2vor``'s ``verts``/``iverts`` verbatim, and flopy's
      own ``Triangle`` + ``VoronoiGrid`` fails the same way with no myflopy code. flopy
      ``develop`` has the same code, and a search of flopy's issues finds neither defect.
      **Mode 1, a cell whose node IS a reflex corner.** ``get_sorted_vertices`` orders a
      cell's vertices by angle about their MEAN. The corner cell is not convex, so an angular
      sort is right only from its kernel -- the wedge of 360 - theta at the corner -- and the
      mean lands beside the node (0.06 ft on the L), either side. On the wrong side the
      polygon cuts across the notch and dips to the corner: a hole inside the boundary, cell
      area outside it, and the face to the cell across the hole gone. The same six vertices
      sorted about a point 0.01 ft inside the wedge give the right cell exactly. On the
      default path, one corner per grid: **327 of 504 failed -- all 36 at 270 deg, all 144
      at 300 or more, none of 108 at 210 or less**; the hole a median 14-19% of the corner's
      own cell, 18 ft² at ``max_area`` 500 to 190 ft² at 20,000. ``min_angle`` 20-34 does not
      remove it.
      **Mode 2, a Voronoi vertex exactly ON the boundary** -- a right triangle's
      circumcentre, its hypotenuse a boundary segment. ``point_in_polygon`` is a half-open
      ray test that drops it on a right-hand or top edge, and the INTERIOR cell needing it
      loses a triangle. Dropped in 15 of 504 default-path grids; no convex grid had a gap
      (0 of 72), where plain flopy left one in 12-13 of 72, 7.0% of a square at worst. Large
      when it lands: the L at ``max_area`` 10000 loses 4,043 ft² (0.63%) in three cells.
      **What reads it, on the L.** MF6 connects cells by shared vertex pairs, so the face is
      gone from the MODEL: at 5000 one face, flow around the L -0.14%; at 10000 seven faces,
      **flow -5.12%** and 0.58 ft of head on a 10 ft drop, the mode-2 cells beside both CHD
      edges. ``get_grid_edge_cells`` counts faces against neighbours, so interior cells beside
      a hole come back as GRID EDGE, 7.7-8.9 ft inside the boundary. A point in a hole reads
      "outside the grid"; a line or polygon across the corner keeps ~80% of its shares, which
      ``mf.Spread``'s ``clip`` writes as is. ``cell_coverage`` between two grids of ONE
      boundary reports 47.6 and 4,018 ft² uncovered; remapped VALUES do not move (ledger
      300's covered-area denominator). The DISU adjacency loses the same faces.
      **Not done, deliberately: no library change**, on the user's instruction to report
      first. The reproducer's rebuild -- each bad cell re-ringed from vertices the grid
      already has -- shows the defect is repairable: both L grids tile exactly and every
      missing face returns. A design pass then went further, and its forks are the user's to
      choose: take each cell from Triangle's OWN mesh (the circumcentres of the node's
      triangles, walked around it) rather than from qhull's Voronoi of every node, keeping
      ``tri2vor``'s vertex ids for each cell it got right. A sort about the node alone is not
      enough at the sharpest corners, where the vertex a cell needs is not among
      ``tri2vor``'s. **The cost:** ``grid_pin`` hashes each cell's ring IN ORDER, so a
      repaired grid re-pins though no cell is renumbered, and runs built on the old grids read
      as another mesh. An upstream report is outward-facing, the user's to send.
      **Found on the way, not pursued.** A boundary that is not ONE simple polygon is worse
      -- ledger 317. And not ``tri2vor``: profile "balanced" simplifies the DOMAIN by 2 ft
      before meshing, so a curved boundary is not the footprint either -- a 904,032 ft²
      corridor was meshed 3,899 ft² away from itself -- and nothing in ``docs/`` said so.
      **A trap for the next reference:** ``shapely.voronoi_polygons`` returns a
      region that is not a Voronoi cell for cocircular nodes; the reproducers build it from
      bisector half-planes.
      Reproducers: ``docs/reproducers/voronoi_tiling_gaps.py`` (mechanism, MF6, consumers;
      15 s) and ``docs/reproducers/voronoi_tiling_sweep.py`` (the rates; 1,266 grids, 2 min).
      Revisit on the user's call, repair or record, or a flopy release that changes
      ``get_sorted_vertices`` or the domain test.

317. **A ``GridSpec.voronoi`` boundary in two parts silently keeps cells in ONE, and one with an interior ring does not build (2026-09-24).**
      FloPy's ``tri2vor`` tests every Voronoi vertex against ``tri._polygons[0]`` ALONE and
      reads ``_polygons[1..nholes]`` as the holes. A boundary drawn as two features,
      1,000,000 ft² each, is meshed in both (Triangle: 353 and 372 nodes) and the grid keeps
      **0 and 372 cells** -- the part that comes first in the unioned boundary survives, the
      other is dropped cell by cell for having fewer than three vertices left, and nothing
      warns or logs. With an
      interior ring (an island, a lake cut out) the build raises ``IndexError``: flopy's
      ``add_polygon`` hands the ring to ``add_hole``, which wants a POINT, and the ring never
      becomes a polygon.
      **Not done, deliberately:** found while measuring ledger 316, and a different repair,
      designed separately and waiting on the user's call: holes handed to Triangle as ring
      plus interior point, and cells built for every part. A hole's corners are reflex
      corners, so ledger 316's mode 1 will apply to them once holes build.
      Reproducer: ``docs/reproducers/voronoi_tiling_gaps.py``, section 7. Revisit before
      anyone meshes two aquifer pieces, an island or a cut-out.

315. ~~**A head surface kept every DRY cell as a sample at -1e30 and erased real heads above 10,000 ft; the head map and the plain section still keep -1e30 (2026-09-24).**~~
      **RESOLVED 2026-09-24 for the map and the section**, in the commit after 379d27f.
      The rule and its one helper stand. What is undone is the deferral: every read of
      the head table in ``choros.py`` now goes through ``Choro._layer_field``, masked by
      ``headsplus._is_sentinel``, and ``XSection.xsect`` masks the same way.
      **The deferral was wider than recorded.** Measured on one run with 25 dry and 4
      inactive cells: the colour range of the map, the static map, ``mosaic`` and
      ``animate`` all ran from -1e30. ``contours=True`` and ``contours="heads"`` drew
      NOTHING, because levels from -1e30 in steps of 10 hit numpy's "Maximum allowed size
      exceeded", which was swallowed at DEBUG. The mounding hover said 1e30 at an inactive
      cell, because the map computed mounding a second time with its own mask. Depth
      below ground drew ±1e30, and the plain section drew both kinds at ±1e30.
      **Two calls were the user's.** On the mounding map a DRY cell reads 0: it has no
      water above the datum, like any cell whose head sits below it. An inactive cell is
      blank. On the depth-below-ground map a dry cell is blank, not the depth to its
      bottom, which would be a lower bound drawn as a value. The generated docs had
      both flags wrong: ``bgs`` "draws the basemap", which it never did (it maps head
      minus the model top), and ``show_mounding`` is "head-above-initial", which it is
      not (it is head above the layer bottom). They now say what each flag does, in all
      five places they are spliced.
      **The import layers moved.** ``choros`` now imports ``headsplus``, so it goes from
      layer 2 to 3, and the seven modules that import it move up one
      (``docs/import_layering.md``). The rule stays in the reader that owns it, rather
      than moving to layer 0 to spare the map a layer.
      **Not done.** ``cross_section_plotting._resolve_head_data`` still reads raw heads,
      but flopy's ``plot_surface`` draws no segment at a sentinel (measured: none of the
      drawn head segments at ±1e30), so nothing reaches the picture.
      ``hds.section(fill=...)`` silently draws a profile: the noun forwards ``fill=`` to
      ``XSection``, which keeps it for a surface it never builds without
      ``interpolator=``. That is not a sentinel defect, so it is left for its own change.
      **RESOLVED by ledger 334 (2026-09-26):** the noun names what acts on it, and
      ``fill=`` raises there, naming ``model.plot.section(fill=...)``.
      Reproducer: section 5 of ``docs/reproducers/head_surface_sentinels.py``; tests:
      ``tests/test_dry_and_inactive_cells.py``, on the ``sentinel_run`` fixture, which
      moved to conftest and marks its tests slow. Reverting the fix fails all seven by
      name. Undoing either of the user's calls fails the mounding test alone.

318. **Lake inputs that `mf.lak`, `LakeTableBuilder` and `LakeTable` accept without checking: found while rewriting their docstrings, documented, NOT fixed (2026-09-25).**
      The rewrite gave every lake-family parameter its own entry and measured each claim
      against MF6 (6.8.0.dev0). It changed no behaviour: what these calls accept is a
      separate decision, so each defect below is stated as behaviour where a reader looks
      -- the parameter's own entry -- with its symptom, and left.
      - **A numpy array or Series as a per-period value** (a forcing, or `LakeOutlet.rate`)
        is not split by period: every period's record carries its repr (`1  RATE  [-1.
        -2.]`) and MF6 dies with a segmentation fault reading it, for RATE and RAINFALL
        alike. The loudest item, and the first to fix.
      - **All-integer keys are read as PERIODS.** With integer-like lake ids,
        `rainfall={101: 0.5}` writes nothing at all, silently. `tables={101: ...}` raises
        `unknown lake '101'`, which prints the int exactly as the string id it missed.
      - **`LakeTableBuilder(footprint=)`**: a `str` path is refused (so are a GeoDataFrame
        and a GeoSeries) while `dem=` takes one; it is never REPROJECTED, and a footprint in
        EPSG:4326 coordinates over an EPSG:2927 raster, one off the raster, and one narrower
        than a pixel centre each build all-zero rows with no warning, which MF6 refuses; a
        multi-layer GeoPackage reads its first layer only (`(10, 3, 2)` where both layers
        give `(10, 4, 3)`), behind pyogrio's generic warning.
      - **`storage_coefficient` is unvalidated**: 0 builds all-zero volumes, a negative
        value raises `Lake table volumes must be nondecreasing` without naming the field.
        MF6 never sees it past the last row: at stage 12.5, a 0.5 table stopped at 11 held
        10.0 where the same table run to 13 held 7.0.
      - **`LakeTable` passes tables MF6 refuses** -- equal volumes, a falling area -- and a
        NaN or negative volume. `rows=` a bare DataFrame fails on its column LABELS
        (`could not convert string to float: 's'`, or `'int' object is not iterable`).
      - **A `"rectangular"` lake drops a VERTICAL connection silently** where `lake_bottom`
        is in no active layer or outside `only_layer` (8 horizontal, 0 vertical, nothing
        raised under `-W error`); `"bathy"` raises there.
      - **`nlakes=` through `**options` replaces the lake count** (5 written for one lake).
      - **`pname=`/`filename=` through `**options` rename only what FloPy writes**: the
        spec's name, the `lak_index` `mf.lak_connection` hands `mf.mvr`, `LAKBuilder.connection`
        and each table child keep `name` (`pname="zz"` left all three at `"lak"`). The
        docstrings say to rename with `name=`.
      - **`mf.lak.flopy` compares no count with its block.** FloPy RAISES `NOUTLETS`/
        `NTABLES` to the rows given but never lowers them, and writes `nlakes` as given, so
        a count above its rows, a count with no block, and an `nlakes` either side of
        `packagedata` all reach MF6, which refuses each by name; a boundname column
        without `boundnames=True` fails the FloPy build. It is the escape hatch, so the
        records stay the caller's; the docstring states each case.
      - Loud, one run late: `mf.lak` passes `status` and the forcings through, and MF6
        refuses an unknown status and a negative rainfall, evaporation, runoff, inflow or
        withdrawal by name; `LakeConnection`'s 0.0 length is refused on a HORIZONTAL
        connection, and its 0.0 width runs carrying nothing.
      **What the docstrings now state as MF6's own rule, not a defect:** MF6 ignores the
      BELEV/TELEV written on a VERTICAL connection and uses the cell's top (written 3.0, 6.0
      or 0.0 under a cell topped at 8.0: VOLUME 400.0 each time), so `bathy` bathymetry
      reaches MF6 only through each connection's LAYER and the HORIZONTAL faces -- which
      both generated modes write on the lake cell itself, not the neighbour, and whose
      BELEV MF6 does read: held at 6.0 under that top, the lake held VOLUME 0.0 and its
      VERTICAL connection carried nothing while a face from the bed (3.0) carried 3.46
      out in a steady period. **In a TRANSIENT period MF6 caps what leaves a lake at its
      storage plus what arrives**, so the same face carried 0.0 (2.0 with an INFLOW of
      2.0) while water from the aquifer still came in (5.15). That is the excavation
      design's subject, not this entry's. A `SPECIFIED` outlet's positive rate ADDS water
      (+5 on a 100 ft2 lake raised it 0.05 ft/d).
      **`LAKBuilder` repeats `mf.lak`'s Parameters TEXT** (it is public, and `mf.lak` is it
      plus a `lak_index`) rather than pointing at it, because an editor shows only the
      class's own text for `LAKBuilder(`; `tests/test_lake_docstrings.py` holds the two
      equal entry for entry, four deliberate differences named (`tables`, `name`, `mover`,
      `options`). Not generated: `scripts/derive_docstrings.py` splices only `plot` verbs.
      Reproducer: `docs/reproducers/lak_docstring_claims.py` (every number above, ~10 s,
      needs `mf6`). Revisit on the user's call; the array SIGSEGV and the integer keys are
      silent or fatal, the rest refuse by name somewhere.
      **Amended (2026-09-25, the excavation design's C3).** `mf.lak`/`LAKBuilder` now take
      `layer=`, the vector layer of each `lakes` file (a multi-layer GeoPackage read its
      first layer only), and read, cover and sample through three shared helpers --
      `grid.geometry.read_footprints`, `footprint_cells`, `refuse_footprint_misses` and
      `surfaces.sample_bed` -- that `LayerStack.excavate` uses too. LAK output is
      byte-identical: the canonical model's written `.lak` and six toy lakes (a bathy
      raster bed, two disjoint lakes, a detached part, a rectangular basin, an EPSG:4326
      file, two files named by stem) compared equal, warnings included, before and after.
      **Not routed through the shared reader, deliberately:** `LakeTableBuilder(footprint=)`
      -- the bullet above still stands (first layer, no reprojection, no `str`); it takes
      a raster's frame rather than the grid's, and changing what it accepts is the
      separate decision this entry defers. Files in different CRSs still raise
      (`Cannot determine common CRS`) rather than being reprojected to the first. The
      grid selectors' and `features=`' layer readers became the same function
      (`readers.read_vector_layer`); `features=`' refusal now reads
      `Layers: 'a', 'b'.` where it read `layers: ['a', 'b']`.
      **`layer=` on `mf.lak`/`LAKBuilder` (and `excavate`) is a NAME, as the design typed
      it -- an integer is REFUSED** (review of C3-C4). It shipped taking `str | int`,
      and beside `only_layer` an int reads as a MODEL layer, the meaning `layer=` has on
      `mf.rch.array`/`evt.array` and PRT's `from_points`; `mf.lak(layer=0)`, which raised
      before C3, was then accepted as the file's first layer -- the default -- and
      changed nothing. In a layer stack an int reads as a model layer too. The generic
      reader and the grid selectors/`features=` still take an index; those have no
      model layer beside them. Same pass: `read_vector_layer` sent a `numpy.int64` index
      down the NAME branch (`has no layer np.int64(0)`, ledger 265's class) -- any
      `numbers.Integral` is an index now, and a `bool` is refused.

319. **"The top active layer" is ONE rule, `idomain > 0`: the array form read `!= 0` and sent recharge into pass-through cells (2026-09-25).**
      `grid/geometry.top_active_layer(domain)`, beside `domain_active`, is now the only
      statement of it -- zero-based, and `-1` for a column with no active cell, which
      each caller still reads its own way (the array form writes layer 0, the areal
      builders and UZF skip the column, SFR's default `reach_layer` refuses the reach).
      Five copies used two predicates: the areal RCH/EVT builders, UZF and SFR already
      read `> 0`; `mf.rch.array`/`mf.evt.array` (`irch`/`ievt="top_active"`) and
      `UsgModel.uppermost_active` read `!= 0`. For the array form that was the defect
      (found as D4 in the excavation scoping): an MF6 `-1` is a removed cell, and MF6
      drops a flux addressed to it without a word. Measured
      (`docs/reproducers/top_active_passthrough.py`, a stack pinched with
      `pinch="passthrough"`): 40 of 92 columns, 207.98 of 360.00 ft3/d applied (57.8%),
      0.00 in those columns, Normal termination, discrepancy -0.01%. After: 360.00.
      **What it moves.** An EAGER array package (`context=` given) on a domain with a
      `-1` above a column's first active cell resolves a different `irch`, so its
      DIGEST moves and `runs.drift()` reads it edited -- correctly, it builds
      differently. A LAZY one digests the string `"top_active"` and does not move; what
      it builds does. Counted: **0 of 25** array RCH packages in the 19 stored runs on
      disk (every one Ten Trails, no `idomain < 0` anywhere), and **0 of 47** array-form
      resolutions across the full test suite (36 tests, none on a domain holding a -1),
      so no stored digest in reach moves. The other three callers are byte-identical by
      construction (`> 0` already). **The USG importer is routed through it too**, and
      that is neutral by construction rather than by luck: a negative USG IBOUND is a
      CONSTANT HEAD -- an active cell, the opposite of MF6's -1 -- and `UsgModel.idomain`
      maps it to 1 before `uppermost_active` reads it; a test pins that, since letting
      a -1 through there would move every constant-head column's ETS target down a
      layer.
      **Found while documenting the two helpers, and NOT changed** (their docstrings
      were rewritten because `irch` changed meaning and wrongly said "1-based", D5):
      `mf.evt.array(surface=<any str>)` is read as "the model top" whatever the string
      names -- `surface="dem.tif"` wrote the same 162.35 ft3/d as omitting it -- and
      `surface=mf.Surface(...)` is accepted at the call and refused by FloPy at build
      (`MFDataException`); a lazy `irch`/`ievt` word other than `"top_active"` is
      accepted at the call and refused only at build. Each is stated in the parameter's
      own entry. The first is silent and the one worth fixing: refusing any string but
      the internal `"model_top"` sentinel is a three-line change that moves no digest.
      `fixed_cell=True` losing the recharge of a DRY cell is MF6's documented meaning of
      `FIXED_CELL`, now said: on the reproducer's model, where 207.98 of 360.00 ft3/d
      falls on 52 dry fill cells, the default applied 360.00 and `fixed_cell=True`
      152.02 (the reproducer runs it). First written "207.98 -> 0.0", which is what the
      OLD `irch` gives -- it also dropped the pass-through columns' 152.02 -- and a
      review caught the pre-fix number in the docstring, here and in the commit.
      Tests: `tests/test_top_active_layer.py`, 10, one of them an MF6 run asserting the
      budget and the percent discrepancy. Reverting the array form to `!= 0` fails 5 by
      name; turning the helper's `> 0` into `!= 0` fails 6.

320. **`LayerStack.excavate`: a pond is a VOID cut after reconcile and pinch, absorbing rather than deepening -- the calls made, the deviations from the design, and what is interim (2026-09-25).**
      `stack.excavate(bottom, within, *, name, layer, min_remnant=0.1)` and
      `LayerBuildResult.excavate` (the excavation design's C4, F1-F4 and F14 as the user
      approved them): inside the footprint every surface above the bed is lowered to it,
      so the first active cell under the bed starts EXACTLY at the bed; the cells above go
      idomain 0, never -1; the ground outside is untouched. The cut is the LAST step of
      `build()` because cutting before reconcile and pinch was measured wrong under every
      policy (the design's section 3.1). The footprint, its cells and the bed come from
      the helpers `mf.lak` uses (C3, ledger 318's amendment), so record cells == lake
      cells and the record's bed is the lake's float -- pinned on a hand-built grid and on
      two `GridSpec.voronoi` grids (ledger 265's `int64`). `stack.to_disv` is now
      `build().to_disv()`: 12 of 12 raster stacks kept their digest, every option and the
      published table (`docs/reproducers/excavation_build_checks.py`, part 1).
      **Judgment calls that differ from the design, each deliberate:**
      - **`min_remnant=0` stops SLIVER absorption only.** An inactive or pass-through cell
        directly under the bed is absorbed whatever `min_remnant` says. The design says
        both "`0` turns absorbing off" and "a LAK vertical connection cannot reach through
        [an inactive cell]"; the second is the one geometry depends on (C7's build check
        wants the vertical cell's top at the bed).
      - **A FOURTH result field, `absorbed`** (each absorbed cell's OWN thickness under
        the bed), beside the design's three. An absorbed cell and a cut cell both end with
        `botm == bed`, so the count, volume and unit the report must give are otherwise
        unrecoverable -- and like `excavated` it is a fact of the build. OWN, not
        `bed - botm`: in a chain (a 0.05 ft silt remnant, then a 0.01 ft pass-through
        cell) the cumulative figure counted the silt twice, 0.11 ft where 0.06 lay
        between the bed and the connected top. The absorbed cells are the excavated ones
        from a column's first positive entry down, because a zero-thickness cell absorbed
        below one (`reconcile=False` leaves those) holds 0.0.
      - **A bare `fill="propagate"` bed is accepted; algebra over one is REFUSED at the
        call**, alongside the relative surfaces. Where the source has no data it reads the
        surface above: bare, that is the ground, so the cell is a rim and is not cut, and
        `mf.lak` reads the same unchanged top -- idempotent. `raster(p, fill="propagate")
        - 2` gave the stack `ground - 2` there, which IS cut, and the lake `ground - 4`
        off the excavated top: 14 of 27 cells 2.0 ft apart. Some composites happen to be
        idempotent (`Min(propagate, 90)`, a `max`); all are refused, one rule -- a false
        refusal costs filling the raster's gaps, a false pass a lake bed that disagrees
        with its own cut. Not taken: recording the ground each bed was sampled against so
        `mf.lak` could sample against it too, which ties the lake to a surface the model
        no longer has.
      - **`ExcavationRecord.min_remnant`**: a declaration value, not derived, so the
        record still holds "the declaration resolved on this grid"; the report's
        `kept_slivers` needs it.
      - **`sample_bed(refresh=)`, `refresh()` and `cache_status()`** reach an excavation's
        bed now (keys `"excavation:<name>"`), and **`for_grid` copies the excavations** --
        both listed for the lifecycle commit (C6), done here because leaving them meant a
        stale contour bed under `build(refresh=True)` and a pond dropped SILENTLY by
        `for_grid`, which `mf.disv` uses to copy an array-holding stack.
      - `excavation_report(thinner_than=)`, omitted, judges each connected cell's UNIT --
        what is left of it in the column, a split unit judged whole -- against the unit's
        `min_thickness`: the rule `qc()` and `report()` count `thin` by. Per slice, a
        connected FULL 10 ft slice of a 30 ft unit with a 20 ft minimum read thin while
        `qc()` read nothing. Given, it compares the CELL; the result does not store the
        build's `min_sep`, so pass it there.
      **Interim, closed by later commits of the design:** ~~an excavated stack REFUSES
      `to_dict` (`NotImplementedError`, which `stamp_source_hashes` does not catch) rather
      than dropping the pond, so `mf.disv(<gridless excavated stack>)` raises at the call
      and such a stack cannot be saved or digested -- `mf.disv(stack.build(vor))` can
      (C6)~~ -- closed by ledger 323, the excavations are written down. ~~**`mf.lak` reads
      no record yet**: on a cut pond `bathy` still writes the old
      rule -- zero side walls and a false "flat bed" warning (design section 4.3) -- so the
      cut alone is the geometry, not yet a better lake model (C7)~~ -- closed by ledger
      325, an excavated lake is written by its own rule. ~~Nothing refuses a
      package declared against a context from BEFORE the cut (C5)~~ -- closed by ledgers
      321 and 322.
      **Measured, and what the tests assert because of it.** A steady NEWTON toy on the
      excavated stack read -0.41% under IMS's DEFAULT closure and its un-excavated twin
      -0.21% (+0.59% each with the water table below the fill), all under Normal
      termination; closed tight both read 0.00%. So the MF6 test tightens the solver and
      asserts BOTH discrepancies (reproducer part 2). MF6's own `.disv.grb` holds the cut
      exactly (top, bottoms, idomain).
      **Found, NOT fixed:** a PRT release point's partial miss (`PRTReleasePoints.
      from_points`) is reported through the LOGGER only -- ledger 288's `warnings.warn`
      rule never reached it, so in a notebook the "left out" line reaches nobody. The
      excavation test reads it from the logger. **NOT built** (the design's section 10):
      recovering an excavation in `from_modflow` (it re-imports a smeared top over thin
      layers); an `edges_only` marker; a dashed ground line in `stack.plot.section`;
      excavating by centroid.
      `LayerStack.add`'s docstring said `pinch="passthrough"` was the default; `build`'s
      is `"floor"`, and it says so now. Tests: `tests/test_excavate.py`, 50 (one MF6);
      each rule mutated in turn fails a named test (16 mutations).

321. **A package still naming a cell the built DISV REMOVED is refused at build -- a boundary, an observation, an array recharge/ET index (2026-09-25).**
      The excavation design's C5, landed right after the cut (ledger 320) so no commit
      ships the cut without its guard. `_discretization_complaints` range-checked
      cellids, and a cell can be in range and still REMOVED by the DISV's idomain -- which
      is exactly what a context declared BEFORE `stack.excavate` leaves behind. It now
      also refuses, off the BUILT DISV's own idomain (`idomain <= 0`, 0 and -1 alike):
      a list boundary's record (chd/drn/ghb/riv/wel/rch/evt, and the GWT/GWE list
      types), an OBS6 cellid (`id`/`id2`, model-level files and a package's own
      `observations=` alike), and an `irch`/`ievt` given PER COLUMN -- an array, or
      `"top_active"` resolved eagerly or at build -- naming a removed cell in a column
      that has an active one. It names the excavation when a record reaches the model
      (`grid_identity.excavation_cells`: `context.surfaces`' records, a table's
      `attrs["excavations"]`, then `grid.excavations`) and, for an array, the rate MF6
      would drop. A lazy `rch.array()` is not immune: it resolves `"top_active"` against
      the MODEL'S context, which declared before the cut still has layer 1 there -- and so
      does a lazy `.gpkg` boundary. **For a LAZY package the refusal names the MODEL's
      context**: the first wording told everyone to "declare the package without
      context=", which is what a lazy package already was, so following it got the same
      refusal again. It now says to rebuild that `ModelContext` from the excavated result
      or leave `domain=` out (the build then reads the DISV's own idomain -- measured, it
      builds with `irch` 1 under the pond). Lazy is read off the spec: an index left in
      the declared spec's `inputs`, a boundary that recorded its resolution on the model.
      **A spec is paired with its FloPy package by the OBJECT it built**
      (`ModelSpec.build`'s `built_packages`), not by name: a bare `PackageSpec` with no
      `pname` is named `chd_0` by FloPy, so a name lookup skipped it -- a CHD on a dug
      cell built clean and MF6 refused it at read unnamed, and a stale per-column `irch`
      on a bare RCHA was warned as "irch left out" instead of refused.
      **Measured premises, one of them against the design.** The design said FloPy
      refuses a list boundary's inactive cellid at construction; it does not -- a CHD at
      a dug cell built clean (FloPy's `_check_valid_cellids` fires for HFB and LAK, not
      for a list BC), so every list BC is checked here, whatever its order. A list BC
      declared BEFORE any discretization cannot be constructed at all ("Unrecognized
      model grid"), so that ordering never reaches the check. MF6 refuses both a list
      record (`BoundaryPackageExt.f90`, "Cell is outside active grid domain") and a head
      observation ("Error reading data from ID string") on a removed cell, so for those
      two the guard refuses no model MF6 runs -- it is the earlier, NAMED form. For an
      array index MF6 says nothing: `nlarray_to_nodelist` maps it to node 0 and
      `rch_cf` skips it.
      **HFB is deliberately exempt**: MF6 WARNS about a barrier touching an inactive cell
      and drops it (`gwf-hfb.f90`), so refusing one would refuse a model MF6 runs.
      Unreachable through FloPy 3.10, which refuses the cellid at construction, so it is
      pinned on the rule (the same records typed as a CHD are refused).
      **Head targets** already refused an explicit inactive cell and reported a point on
      no active cell as a miss; both now name the excavation and say the head belongs to
      the cell under the bed. **Found, NOT fixed:** that partial miss reaches the LOGGER
      only (`observations/_shared._report_missed_features`) -- ledger 288's
      `warnings.warn` rule has not reached the target families, as ledger 320 found for
      PRT; changing it moves every target family's warnings and is its own commit.
      **Not covered:** a DIS (structured) model -- the activity checks are DISV-only, as
      the mesh checks beside them are; advanced packages (`packagedata`/`connectiondata`,
      which `_cellids_in` deliberately does not walk -- LAK's are C7's); a package a
      hook attaches after the build. **Cost:** the list walk repeats the range check's,
      0.55-0.62 s on a 654,480-record EVT against 0.45-0.48 s for the range walk it sits
      beside (`docs/reproducers/active_cell_guard.py`, which also shows every premise in
      this entry: FloPy accepting the CHD and the observation, MF6's two refusals, FloPy
      refusing the HFB, and MF6 dropping the dug columns' recharge under Normal
      termination with the budget closed).
      Tests: `tests/test_active_cell_guard.py` (on the hand-built grid and
      `triangulated_grid`); reverting the call fails 14 by name, dropping the excavation
      note 14, treating every index as the opt-out 6, the head-target naming 2, the HFB
      exemption 1; after the adversarial review, the lazy wording 4, the object pairing 2.

322. **`irch=None` -- one layer for every column -- stays the documented opt-out, and the build now SAYS what it loses (2026-09-25).**
      Ledger 163 made `"top_active"` the default and kept `irch=None` (and a single
      integer) as the explicit opt-out; `tests/test_run_record.py` and
      `tests/test_spec_libraries.py` declare it, and MF6 then puts the flux in that layer
      in every column and skips, without a word, every column whose cell there is
      removed. The design (C5) weighed refusing it with the array form (ledger 321) and
      did not: it is legal, correct wherever the layer is active everywhere, and the one
      spelling that means "the same layer on every mesh" (`mf.rch.array(irch=0)` is
      grid-free by design, ledger 267). So it WARNS -- `warnings.warn` and the logger
      (ledger 288) -- naming the columns, the excavation that dug them, and the rate:
      the declared rate times each skipped column's DISV area, against the total over
      columns with an active cell, in the first period that loses flux and the worst
      when that is a later one. For RECHARGE the number is MF6's: on a steady NEWTON model
      with the pond dug out of layer 1, the RCH inflow in MF6's budget file is the
      declared total less the warned loss to 1e-6, and the budget closes
      (`test_the_warned_loss_is_what_mf6_drops`, slow). **For ET it is an UPPER BOUND**,
      stated as one ("up to X of Y ft3/d at the maximum ET rate"): the declared `rate` is
      the MAXIMUM ET rate, which MF6 scales by the head's depth below the surface, so what
      it drops lies anywhere from zero to that. The first wording read as the actual flux,
      and nothing checked it against MF6 -- the test asserted rate x area, the maximum by
      construction. Measuring the real ET loss needs the solved heads, so it is not done.
      (Reverting the "up to" wording fails 2 named tests.) What decides refusal against warning is the DECLARED value
      (`None`, a scalar, a per-period dict of scalars), read off the resolved spec, not
      the FloPy data -- FloPy stores `irch=0` as a full array of zeros, so the built
      package cannot tell the two apart. Silent where the layer is active in every column
      with an active cell (0 warnings across the 4,163-test suite).

323. **An excavated layer stack is written down, archived, hashed and moved like the rest of the stack -- the lifecycle calls (2026-09-25).**
      The excavation design's C6 (section 6), closing ledger 320's interim `to_dict`
      refusal. Excavations ride in the `$layer_stack` payload ONLY when there are any, so
      an un-excavated stack's payload and digest are what they were: 16 of 16 lazy-DISV
      digests identical between the trees before and after (eight stacks naming a raster,
      contours, a `where` zone, a split, per-unit names, units and algebra, each under two
      build-kwarg sets), and no stored manifest on disk holds a stack at all (0 under
      `examples/` and the model tree). An entry is `{name, bottom, zone | area, layer?,
      min_remnant, source_shas?}`, pinned by `test_layer_stack_serialization.py`.
      **Judgment calls, each deliberate:**
      - **The footprint file rides under `"zone"`**, the key `Surface.where` already
        uses and `specs.SURFACE_INPUT_KEYS` already lists, so the four machines that find
        a stack's files by walking its payload -- the bundler, the build-time anchor,
        `drift()`'s `built_from`, the hash stamping -- find it with NO specs.py edit and
        no spec token. A new key would have needed all four taught, and a missed one is
        the silent kind (ledger 293's archive that cannot open).
      - **`source_shas` is a STORED field of the excavation**, carried both ways. The
        stamping rebuilds the stack through `from_dict`; a `from_dict` refusing the field
        raises now (C2), and dropping it would leave the footprint digested by PATH --
        bundling a byte-identical archive would then read as an edit. "The hash replaces
        the path" is ONE helper, `surfaces._content_keyed`, which `Surface.digest_payload`
        now uses too.
      - **An inline `mf.Area`'s `source` and `note` are not digested**: provenance and a
        comment. Its WKT and CRS are.
      - **`from_dict` builds entries DIRECTLY**, never through `excavate()`, whose
        declaration reads the file: a bundled payload names a project-RELATIVE path that
        only the build anchors, and reading it at load would check it against the working
        directory (measured: with an existence check at load, the bundled archive failed
        to load). A missing file is found at build, where it is read. **Only the file read
        is skipped**: every other refusal `excavate()` makes runs at load through the same
        two helpers (`layers._checked_scalars`, `_refuse_declaration`). Building entries
        unchecked -- the first version -- let a hand-written payload
        (`SimulationSpec.from_yaml`) repeat a name, and one excavation's RECORD vanished
        while its cut stayed in the arrays (records `{'pond': cell 0 at 85.0}` beside a
        top of 93.0 at cell 4), past the overlap refusal too, which is keyed by name; dig
        an `offset_below(9)` bed from the ground (the +5 ft stack-vs-lake mismatch the
        verb refuses); and take `layer=` or a column floor beside an inline `area`. An
        empty name is refused by both now (the verb accepted `name=""`).
      - **`from_dict` REFUSES unknown keys, the stack's own as well as an entry's.** An
        excavation is exactly the kind of addition an older reader drops in silence -- a
        stack without its pond builds clean -- so from here on a payload from a later
        version refuses rather than degrades. It cannot reach back: C4's reader ignores
        `"excavations"`.
      - **The lazy `mf.disv` publishes a table built from the RESULT** (design D9), not
        `grid.gdf_topbtm` -- with `attach=False` that is whatever was published before
        (a top of 500.0 against the DISV's 100.0, ledger 270's amendment) -- and it
        carries the records in the table's `attrs["excavations"]`, so a model's elevations
        and records come from ONE result. `grid_identity.excavation_cells` reads them
        there (the C5 guard names the excavation on a lazy `attach=False` model through
        it) and C7's resolver is to. Not publishing the `LayerBuildResult` itself: the
        frozen snapshot drops one silently (design D8, still open), and a lazy run would
        then freeze with no elevations. **The table is marked as the DISV's own**
        (`attrs["published_by"] = "disv"`), and `specs._layer_elevations` does not warn
        that a marked table disagrees with the grid's: with `attach=False` that is the
        GRID's table left alone on purpose, and the warning said the CONTEXT was stale and
        to rebuild it -- which would put the old elevations back (measured: a lazy drain
        at `model_top - 2` correct at 98.0, beside 11 such warnings). The limit: a marked
        table carried by hand into ANOTHER model's context is trusted too. **An `ExcavationRecord` copies as ITSELF**
        (`__copy__`/`__deepcopy__`): pandas deep-copies a frame's `attrs` into every frame
        derived from it, which cost ~35 us per derived frame for a 612-cell record (329
        against 225 us for three column reads on a 9,405-cell table; 233 us shared), and
        the record is immutable -- frozen, a tuple of cells, a read-only bed.
      - **`_layer_elevations`' context-vs-grid warning goes through `warnings.warn`** too
        (design D11; ledger 288's rule): logged alone it reached nobody.
      **Measured, pinned by tests** (`tests/test_excavation_lifecycle.py`, 28): every
      footprint form (path + layer, a column floor, an `mf.Area`, a GeoDataFrame, a bare
      geometry) round-trips through JSON and YAML in plain types with numpy scalars fed
      in, and rebuilds the identical arrays and records on `triangulated_grid`; moving the
      footprint and the bed keeps the digest, editing either moves it; a bundled project
      rebuilds with every source deleted (boundary, footprint, bed), and so does a run
      from its frozen snapshot; `drift()` reads `ok` and then `edited` after the
      footprint moves; one declaration covers 28 and 92 cells -- `mf.lak`'s own cells on
      each mesh -- and `with_grid` 28 -> 92 reads `rebuilt`. Each rule reverted fails a
      named test (10 mutations; and after the adversarial review, the load-time refusal
      9, the scalar checks 3, the frozen records 2, the published-table mark 1).
      **The frozen snapshot carries the RECORDS** (`freeze._excavations_block`): name,
      cells, bed, `min_remnant` -- two arrays and two scalars each, nothing derived -- read
      in `excavation_cells`' order (the context's surfaces, their `attrs`, then the grid)
      and restored onto the thawed table's `attrs` AND the thawed grid. Section 6 said
      freeze needed no change, and for the ARRAYS it did not; but the snapshot kept only
      the table's numeric columns, so a reopened run held the pond's elevations with no
      record naming it (8 cells live, 0 thawed): the C5 guard could not name the
      excavation there, and C7's `mf.lak`, declared against a thawed context, would have
      found no record and fallen back to the legacy rule on an excavated geometry.
      Additive to the payload, so `freeze.FORMAT` does not move: an older snapshot thaws
      with no records, as before.
      **NOT changed, by design (section 6):** the specs.py walkers, bundling and
      `package_move` (no edit needed, given `"zone"`); the remap (`remap.py`: a pit's
      cells come out unreached and the lazy DISV makes them inactive). `refresh()`,
      `cache_status()` and `for_grid` already carried the excavations (ledger 320).
      Design D8 -- a `LayerBuildResult` given as `ModelContext(surfaces=)` freezes with no
      elevations -- is still open; its records now survive, on the thawed grid.

324. **A typed `ievt` beside an omitted ET `surface` was DROPPED, and a numpy-integer `irch`/`ievt` died inside FloPy (2026-09-25).**
      Predates the excavation work (present at myflopy `90de983`), found by the C5
      review. `mf.evt.array` goes LAZY when `surface` is omitted with no `context=`
      (ledger 285), and the lazy branch of `_array_bc_result` built its options from the
      VALUE fields and the other keywords -- a non-string `ievt` is in neither, so it was
      thrown away: `ievt=1` wrote no IEVT at all and MF6 took the ET from layer 1,
      silently; an `ievt` array or per-period dict likewise, and `ievt=0` happened to mean
      what was written. It rides in `options` now, and `_build_lazy_array` pops it back
      out, as it already did for the index name. **It moves the digest of every such
      declaration** -- deliberately: they were writing a different layer from the one
      declared. Counted: 0 stored manifests hold a lazy array spec at all (no
      `_build_lazy_array` in any JSON under the repo or the model tree), and no
      declaration in the repo types an `ievt` with the surface omitted. `ievt=None` and
      the `"top_active"` default carry nothing new, so their digests do not move.
      Consequences, both right: the C5 guard (ledger 321) now REFUSES a stale typed
      `ievt` array there, where the dropped one read as "ievt left out" and was only
      warned; and `with_grid` reads such a package `unverifiable` (it names cells by
      position) where it read `rebuilt` while writing no index.
      **Same pass, ledger 265's class:** a numpy INTEGER scalar index -- `irch=np.int64(1)`,
      or one per period -- died inside FloPy with "object of type 'numpy.int64' has no
      len()", an `MFDataException` naming neither argument, on the EAGER form of both
      helpers. `_array_bc_values` converts it to `int` (digest-neutral: `package_digest`
      already canonicalized it). Tests: `tests/test_lazy_areal.py` (the typed index
      written as given, five shapes; the numpy index on rch, rch per period and evt;
      `ievt=None`/default unchanged) and `tests/test_active_cell_guard.py` (the stale
      typed array refused). Reverting the carry fails 7 by name, the conversion 4.
      `docs/reproducers/lazy_typed_ievt.py` shows each premise: the EVT file written with
      no IEVT block before and `IEVT CONSTANT 2` after, the numpy index an
      `MFDataException` before and a build after, and the manifest count.

325. **`mf.lak` reads the excavation RECORD: an excavated lake connects at its bed and into its neighbours' cells; every other lake keeps its rule byte for byte and is told what MF6 will not see (2026-09-25).**
      The excavation design's C7 (section 4, F6/F7/F9/F13 as the user approved them).
      Each generated lake gets a RULE -- `LAKBuilder.lake_rules`, stamped as metadata
      `lake_rules` -- chosen from the excavation record, found through ONE resolver
      (`specs._layer_elevation_source`) that returns the records from the same place as
      the elevations, in `_layer_elevations`' order: a `LayerBuildResult` as `surfaces`,
      else the grid's `excavations` (`attach=True`). **Excavated** (the lake's cells ARE
      one record's cells): a VERTICAL connection to the top cell with idomain > 0 AND
      thickness -- activity alone picks a zero-thickness layer when the context carries
      no `domain` -- whose top is the bed; walls INTO the neighbouring columns wherever a
      neighbour's model top is above the bed, `CONNLEN` the neighbour's DISV centre to
      the face line and `CONNWIDTH` the shared edge, both from `get_disv_gridprops`
      (`grid/connectivity.DisvFaces`, MF6's `shared_edge`/`distance_normal`, not
      `grid.cl12` -- which since ledger 328 is that same rule, read from the neighbour's
      row). `lake_bottom=None` takes the record's bed (F13); a declared one must
      equal it within `max(1e-6*|b|, 1e-6)`, before capping. A partial match, a lake on
      two records, `rectangular_interior=True` and an `only_layer` other than the top
      active layer are REFUSED whatever `unexcavated=` says. **Legacy** (no record
      touches it): the old rule, plus the `unexcavated=` guard ("warn" default, F7).
      Faces thinner than 1e-6 are dropped in every mode (F9); ~~nothing else in the legacy
      rule moved~~ -- **REVERSED 2026-09-25 by the user, see 328**: a legacy wall's
      `CONNLEN` is now its lake cell's own side of the face (`grid.cl12` per side), about
      half the centre-to-centre spacing this entry kept "byte for byte". Every other
      column still is the old rule.
      **Measured** (`docs/reproducers/excavated_lake_rule.py`): a pit lake below the water
      table in uniform flow carries 1.0054 / 1.0053 of the same pit's through-flow as a
      K = 1e4 inclusion (two grids), where the legacy rule on the un-excavated stack gives
      0.392 / 0.398 (0.523 / 0.525 since ledger 328); GWF and LAK discrepancy 0.00 -- the
      `slow` test asserts ratio 1.00 ± 0.01 AND both discrepancies. The legacy rule writes
      the SAME rows as before (every column but `CONNLEN` since 328) on five
      synthetic fixtures and the canonical lake (`tests/data/lak_legacy_golden.json`,
      written by the pre-change tree `8b3ce9d`), and on a 612-cell reconstruction of a real
      pond from COPIES of its MF6 files (1,753 connections, 1,141 walls, thinnest face
      1.32e-4) -- that last one is not reproducible from the repository. The guard on the
      canonical lake: 33 of 33 verticals above the 96.0 floor, up to 13.45 ft.
      **Judgment calls, each deliberate:**
      - **A lake with explicit `LakeConnection`s is matched against no record** (rule
        `"explicit"`): its connections are the caller's. An excavation shared between an
        explicit lake and a generated one is therefore refused as a partial match.
      - **A `{lake_id: ...}` `lake_bottom` that leaves an excavated lake out takes that
        lake's record**, so a package mixing excavated and legacy lakes can declare only
        the legacy beds -- F13 read per lake.
      - **A bare elevation table carries no record, EXCEPT the grid's own live
        `gdf_topbtm` object** -- `surfaces=vor.gdf_topbtm`, the spelling `mf.lak`'s own
        example uses, would otherwise read an excavated pond as legacy. A COPY is bare.
      - **The "looks excavated" warning rides `unexcavated=`**, so `"raise"` refuses it
        too: a record that never arrived is exactly what `"raise"` is for.
      - **The four build warnings (section 4.8) fire for EXCAVATED lakes only.** MF6's
        IWETLAKE also switches recharge/ET off on a legacy lake's vertical cell whenever
        the stage rises above that cell's top, but there it is occasional; warning on
        every legacy lake would fire on the canonical model and every lake not yet
        re-declared, and the guard already names the geometry. The transparent-bed test is
        the design's: half-cell share > 90% at the median vertical AND a > 10x thickness
        spread (a uniform floor is mesh-dependent but consistent).
      - **The DISV check (`grid_identity.lak_geometry_complaints`) runs in two places**:
        the LAK builder before FloPy constructs the package (FloPy's own refusal names only
        a cellid) and `_discretization_complaints` after every package (a lake declared
        before its DISV). Its "face inside its cell" comparison uses the same 1e-6 relative
        tolerance, NOT MF6's exact compare: it exists to catch a lake resolved against
        another build (feet, not ulps), so a hand-written face within 1e-6 of its cell
        passes here and could still be refused by MF6. `mf.lak.flopy` packages carry no
        `lake_rules` and are not checked.
      - `lake_rules` and `lake_connections` (each connection's owner cell and role,
        `floor`/`wall`/`rim`) are METADATA -- no digest moves -- and `void_pin` drops them
        when an edit replaces `connectiondata`, pinned or not.
      - The canonical lake stays unexcavated (F8): `tests/conftest.py` filters the guard in
        its two canonical fixtures, and `canonical_example.py` is untouched.
      **NOT built:** LAK `IMPLICIT` (ledger 326); excavating the canonical lake (F8, a
      follow-up that moves every canonical baseline); masking MF6's -1e30 dry lake stage
      in the stage views (the design's D10 -- an excavated pond reads dry every recovery
      day; **RESOLVED by ledger 329**); a geometric rule choice (section 4.1: measured wrong three ways). Tests:
      `tests/test_excavated_lake.py` (22, one MF6); reverting each piece -- the record
      rule, the neighbour walls, `DisvFaces`' CONNLEN, the thickness test, the bed check,
      both refusals, the guard, both DISV-check call sites, the warnings, the metadata
      void, the rim bed, the face tolerance -- fails a named test (14 mutations).

326. **`mf.lak(implicit=True)` writes MF6's LAK `IMPLICIT`, which FloPy 3.10 cannot: a SECOND WRITER for the LAK file, in one place, and what a FloPy round trip loses (2026-09-25).**
      The user asked for it ("I will want to try using it"), reversing the excavation
      design's F15, which had recommended waiting for FloPy. `IMPLICIT` makes each lake
      stage one more unknown of the flow matrix, solved WITH the heads; on the user's
      excavated pond the design measured +81% outer iterations and 16 ATS failures by
      the default formulation against +11% and 0 with it. It is in MF6's develop branch
      (commit `e2dfc84c`, PR #2860) and the 6.8 line only, and FloPy 3.10's
      `ModflowGwflak` -- generated from an older DFN -- has no keyword for it.
      **The flag** rides in the spec's `options` (`True` only: `False` adds no key, so no
      existing digest moves), so it is serialized, frozen and digested; the builder
      `_build_lak_with_tables` consumes it, so FloPy never sees it. `np.bool_` is
      converted with `bool()`; anything else is a `TypeError`.
      **The writer is the PACKAGE**: `lak_implicit.ModflowGwflakImplicit`, a
      `ModflowGwflak` whose own `write` lets FloPy write the file and then inserts
      `IMPLICIT` above `END OPTIONS` (`insert_implicit`, idempotent -- a block already
      holding it, any case, is left alone). Every path that WRITES the package reaches
      its `write` -- `Run.write`/`execute`, `build_flopy` + `write_simulation`, a run
      reopened from its frozen snapshot (rebuilt through the builder) -- each tested.
      **The flag IS the class, so a path that REBUILDS a LAK package loses it unless it
      carries the class** -- and four did, silently, found by the adversarial review:
      FloPy's model splitter builds each split package through `package_factory`, which
      answers FloPy's own class (measured: a source `m.lak` holding `IMPLICIT` split into
      an `m_0.lak` without it), so `split_model` gives each split LAK its source
      package's class, matched by package name in the `<source>_<n>` models; a package
      ARTIFACT captured options through FloPy's datasets and restored a plain
      `ModflowGwflak`, so it records `implicit` (only when set -- no stored artifact
      changes); `model.config` read the same datasets, so `diff().config` compared two
      runs differing only in `implicit=True` as EQUAL -- ledger 286's NEWTON trap
      reopened -- and it now reads the class as the lake's `implicit` row (only when
      set, like a FloPy keyword); and FloPy's loader, below. The artifact path also
      carried no `BOUNDNAMES`, so restoring ANY `mf.lak` lake (its id is a boundname) died
      in FloPy's recarray -- never exercised for LAK before; it is carried now.
      **Trap, measured:** FloPy's `MFPackage.__init_subclass__` registers
      EVERY subclass as the class its LOADER builds for that package type
      (`PackageContainer.packages_by_abbr`), so merely defining the subclass made every
      LAK file loaded afterwards -- IMPLICIT or not -- a `ModflowGwflakImplicit`, and a
      rewrite inserted the keyword into files that never had it. The registry entry is
      put back to FloPy's own class right after the class statement, and a test loads a
      file without the keyword through FloPy and through `Run.open`.
      Not chosen: patching the file after `write_simulation` at each call
      site (four sites, and a fifth written tomorrow would silently drop it) or FloPy
      class regeneration from MF6's DFNs (outside myflopy, per environment).
      **Loading, measured:** `flopy.mf6.MFSimulation.load` reads a LAK file holding
      `IMPLICIT` WITHOUT A WORD and keeps no trace of it -- a rewrite of the loaded
      simulation wrote no `IMPLICIT`. myflopy's two load paths (`Run.open`,
      `mf.load_mf6_run`) now call `keep_implicit`, which re-classes such a loaded package
      as `ModflowGwflakImplicit` so writing it again keeps the option. **A bare FloPy load
      and write still loses it**, silently, and that is pinned by a test as the limit.
      **MF6's requirements, measured and enforced:** a CG linear acceleration STOPS MF6
      ("... ASYMMETRIC COEFFICIENT MATRIX, BUT THE CONJUGATE GRADIENT METHOD WAS
      SELECTED"), and CG is what `complexity="SIMPLE"` and an IMS declaring neither
      option default to (both measured), so a CG solution is REFUSED when the simulation
      is built, and the IMS `mf.simulation` makes for you picks BICGSTAB
      (`_asymmetric_matrix`); MODERATE and COMPLEX default to BICGSTAB (measured).
      **A library lake through `mf.ref` is invisible to `mf.simulation`** -- the library
      is not reachable there -- so it generated SIMPLE (CG) and the build refused a solver
      the caller never declared (measured). The generated solver is marked
      `GENERATED_SOLVER` (metadata: no digest moves, and it survives the frozen snapshot)
      and `SimulationSpec.build_flopy` gives it BICGSTAB once the refs resolve to an
      implicit lake -- only when it still names no `linear_acceleration`, and only for
      the models it solves. Chosen over documenting the caveat because the choice was
      myflopy's to begin with; a DECLARED solver is never changed, so a CG one is still
      refused by name. The written IMS then says BICGSTAB where the declared spec says
      SIMPLE -- the build finishing a choice it made, not an edit. A lake
      with NO connection STOPS MF6 under `IMPLICIT` ("lake 2 has no connections; the
      IMPLICIT option requires ...", measured; the default formulation runs it) -- refused
      at declaration. MF6's DFN recommends NEWTON for lakes that may perch -- a WARNING at
      build. `maximum_iterations`/`maximum_stage_change` are then inert (MF6's DFN), and
      the package-convergence CSV record is left out because MF6 does not write it
      (it would print a warning instead).
      **The executable is probed** once per executable FILE (real path, mtime, size): a
      two-cell model with `IMPLICIT`, written as plain MF6 text so the probe needs nothing
      but the binary, run in a temporary directory -- under a second. `Run.execute`,
      `SimulationBase.run_simulation` and `LoadedMf6Run.run_simulation` ask before running; a
      build that refuses the option, or no executable found, is WARNED about, naming the
      path and `--version`, and the run GOES AHEAD (MF6 stops in seconds with its own
      message, which lands in the run's report). No older MF6 exists on this machine, so
      the refusing case is tested with a fake executable that answers like one; the text
      an old MF6 really prints for an unknown LAK option was read from source
      (`BoundaryPackage.f90`), not run. A bare `sim.run_simulation()` is not probed.
      **Measured** (the `slow` test): a transient pit filled at 2,000 ft3/d runs to Normal
      termination with and without `IMPLICIT`, the listing saying the stage is solved in
      the matrix, stages equal to 1.0e-8 ft, GWF and LAK discrepancy 0.00 (asserted
      < 0.1%, every period).
      **Reproducer:** `docs/reproducers/lak_implicit_requirements.py` runs MF6 on each
      claim above -- the five IMS variants and a CG control without `IMPLICIT`, a lake
      with no connection both ways, FloPy's silent drop and `keep_implicit`, and the pit's
      stages (1.0e-8 ft apart, discrepancies 0.00) -- printing MF6's own ERROR REPORT, so
      the premise of every refusal can be checked against the executable in hand.
      **NOT built:** `mf.lak.flopy(implicit=)` (the escape hatch builds a plain
      `ModflowGwflak`; FloPy refuses the keyword there); the probe for a direct
      `flopy` `run_simulation` (a split run's `run_serial`/`run` included); carrying
      `IMPLICIT` through a bare FloPy load (a split of a model loaded that way has
      nothing to carry). **The config reads what is LOADED**: a run opened with
      `mf.load_mf6_run` and never `load_all()`ed has not loaded its LAK at all, so its
      config has no `lak` section -- true of every package option outside the core set,
      not of `implicit` alone, and left as it was.
      Tests: `tests/test_lak_implicit.py` (14, one MF6); reverting each piece -- the
      write hook, the loader-registry restore, `keep_implicit` on each load path, the
      CG refusal, the automatic BICGSTAB, the NEWTON warning, the zero-connection
      refusal, the probe's cache and its warning, the split re-class, the artifact's
      capture, class, boundnames and convergence record, the config row, and the
      generated-solver marker, its build-time call and both its guards -- fails a named
      test.
