332. **`section(fill=...)` draws on Plotly too, and draws what Matplotlib draws: one `FilledSection`, one FloPy `PlotCrossSection`, two renderers (2026-09-26).**
      Asked for by the user when the section's defaults came up ("i wouldn't mind a
      plotly 'filled' section, equivalent to mpl. we just haven't built it yet"), and
      built FIRST, before any default moves, so that `fill="layer"` can be the default
      on both backends rather than a default that depends on the backend.
      Undoes ledger 177's "`fill=` is Matplotlib ONLY"; its refusals stand.
      **Equivalent by construction, then checked.** Both renderers read ONE
      `PlotCrossSection` -- `polygons` for the cells, `projpts` for the water levels
      exactly as its `plot_surface` walks them, `extent` for the framing -- and one set
      of resolved arrays (`_masked_to_layers`), colours and labels. Plotly re-derives
      none of the geometry; a second derivation is what would let the two drift.
      `tests/test_filled_section_plotly.py` reads BOTH drawings back and compares them
      polygon by polygon -- cells and colours, outlines, water-level segments and their
      colours, legend entries in order, both axis ranges -- over ten option sets, an
      array fill and the bare-grid scope: on the canonical model 124 cells in 4 colours
      (up to 92 under `fill="results"`) and 31 segments per water level. Four
      deliberate breaks each fail named tests (palette off by one 8, `reverse` ignored
      2, subset crop dropped 3, field colours unnormalized 4).
      **Judgment calls.**
      - **The cell edges go OVER the fill on Plotly.** Matplotlib adds `plot_grid`
        first, so under the 85%-opaque fill its hairlines barely show, and the edges one
        sees there are the seaborn style's white patch edges, not `show_grid`'s. Same
        cells outlined, deliberately different z-order.
      - **`fill_cmap` stays a MATPLOTLIB colormap name on both.** Plotly's colorscale is
        built from that colormap's own 256-entry lookup table -- the quantization
        Matplotlib applies -- so the colours are equal, not similar; one trace per
        distinct colour, since a scatter fill takes one. A Plotly-only name
        (`"earth"`) raises at the call. `viz.mpl_colormap_for` converts the other way
        (Plotly to Matplotlib, for maps) and was not reused: this parameter already
        was a Matplotlib name.
      - **The legend reads the same resolved `(loc, anchor)` from `legend_placement`**,
        so one word is one placement and an unknown word is already refused. `"auto"`
        (Matplotlib's `best`) is Plotly's own default; the outside placements sit
        farther out on the left and bottom than Matplotlib's anchors, because Plotly's
        axis titles live in that margin; an inside legend gets a 60% white box, where
        an opaque one would hide the cells (Matplotlib's is frameless).
      - **Everything is validated at the CALL.** `.fig` is lazy, so the constructor
        builds the `PlotCrossSection` (refusing a line that crosses no cell) and checks
        `fill`, `layers`, `head_layers`, `legend` and `fill_cmap`, rather than failing
        at the first `.fig`.
      **Fixed in passing, on both renderers:** `layer_labels=` named the layers and
      stopped there -- with two water levels the legend read "sand, clay, ..., Head,
      Layer 1". `section_head_surfaces(names=)` takes the same list now; passing it
      nowhere fails the two tests that pin it, one per backend.
      **Not done here.** No default moved: `section()` is still the Plotly line profile. `viz.mosaic` takes maps and Plotly `Figure`s, not a
      `FilledSection` (its `.fig` works). The grid's outline picture without `fill=`
      (`GridSection`) is untouched, and `reverse=` there still needs `backend="mpl"`.
      Plotly adds what Matplotlib cannot: a hover naming each cell's layer, number, top
      and bottom along the line, and its value under a field fill.

333. **`section()` draws the model's cross-section by default -- `fill="layer"`, `backend="mpl"` -- and `fill=None` is the one spelling of the line profile (2026-09-26).**
      The user's call: "It just feels like a quirky API that is confusing. I want
      model.plot.section(line=line) to default to fill='layer' and backend='mpl'", with
      Plotly to draw "something else" until it could fill -- and then "i wouldn't mind a
      plotly 'filled' section, equivalent to mpl". Built first (ledger 332), so the
      default is the SAME picture on both backends and nothing defaults by backend.
      **Four forks, answered by the user:** the Plotly filled section first; a profile
      argument without `fill=None` RAISES and names it, rather than switching to the
      profile on its own (the picture would then depend on which OTHER arguments were
      passed); `model.hds.section()` stays the head profile (the next change); and the
      new default returns a bare `Figure`, as `backend="mpl"` does everywhere (ledger
      176), not an `MplPicture`.
      **Where it reaches:** the free verb, `model.plot` and `vor.plot` (a bare grid:
      its layers, or with `fill=None` its `GridSection` outlines). `stack.plot.section`
      already drew the filled layers. The noun `model.hds.section()` and the
      `kind="section"` composers are unchanged -- the head profile, Plotly. The
      signature is reordered so an editor lists the cross-section's parameters first,
      and the docstring opens with a table of the two pictures and says which
      arguments belong to which. `FilledSection.__init__` joins the section chain in
      `test_plot_vocabulary`, so `fill`'s default is pinned to the renderer that owns it.
      **What the default costs, measured in the tree:** a `section(...)` with no
      `backend=` returns a Matplotlib figure, so `.save()`, `.ani`, and a panel of
      `plot.animate`/`viz.mosaic` need `backend="plotly"` (and `fill=None` for `.ani`):
      9 test call sites, 4 notebook cells (`plotting_vocabulary_tour` 3,
      `master_large_model_visualization_prt_workflow` 1) and 6 doc examples, edited;
      `.save(...)` on the default became `.savefig(...)`.
      **Fixed on the way -- each accepted and IGNORED before, measured byte-identical
      2026-09-26:** `fill_cmap=`/`fill_label=` on the profile (the refusal listed the
      other five cross-section arguments and not these); `show_model_top=False` and
      `show_model_btm=True` on the Matplotlib profile (`combined_section_frame` forced
      the top on and the bottoms off; it reads the section's own flags now, and the
      defaults draw as before, so the noun and the composers do not move);
      `animation_kstpkpers=` with `backend="mpl"`, which has no `.ani` (refused); and
      a bare grid's cross-section took `per`/`kstpkper`/`head_layers` and drew the
      same geometry without them (refused, naming them).
      **Found and LEFT, stated in the docstring** (RESOLVED by ledger 337, the user's
      calls: both arguments removed, both pictures open on the first saved time):
      `spacing` is read by nothing, and
      `extrapolate_beyond_section_ends` only ever raises `NotImplementedError` (on a
      path of two or more cells). Both stay, documented as having no effect: removing
      them is an API change nobody was asked about, and `XSection`, the engine behind
      the profile, takes them too. The two pictures open on DIFFERENT times by default
      -- the cross-section on the last saved time (`section_time`), the profile on the
      first (`XSection` takes `model.kstpkper[0]`) -- documented, not changed, because
      either change moves every existing figure of that kind, the noun's included.
      Tests: `tests/test_section_defaults.py`, 16. Reverting the free verb's default
      fails the free scope's test by name; forcing the profile's flags again fails 1;
      dropping the bare-grid refusal 3; the `fill_cmap` refusal 1; the
      `animation_kstpkpers` refusal 1.

334. **A field noun's `section` names what acts on it and refuses the rest: `fill=` and the cross-section's arguments raise, naming `model.plot.section(fill=...)` (2026-09-26).**
      Closes ledger 315's "Not done". `model.hds.section(line=..., fill="layer")` returned
      the plain head profile, byte-identical, and with `interpolator=` raised `TypeError`
      from `InterpolatedSurface.__init__`, a class the caller never named: the noun took
      `**kwargs` into `XSection`, which keeps its tail only for the surface it builds
      when interpolating. **Measured** (`docs/reproducers/section_noun_kwargs_tail.py`, at
      a69ac87): of 28 keywords passed one at a time -- every parameter the verb names and
      the noun did not, `InterpolatedSurface`'s extras, `extent=`, two typos -- 24 came
      back byte-identical on `model.hds`, `group.hds` and `diff.hds`, on both backends;
      `section_name=` crashed the group and the diff ("got multiple values"); the
      `kind="section"` composers swallowed the same set and `kstpkper`; the verb's line
      profile swallowed every typo.
      **Refuse, not route -- the user's call**, for the reasons put with the fork: a noun
      fixes the field it draws (why map nouns refuse `values=`/`type=`), and `fill="layer"`
      draws the geology while an array draws any field; a group, a diff and the section
      composers have no one model's cells to fill, so routing would have split one
      `SpatialView` method into two behaviours; and the model scope teaches the
      cross-section (ledger 177). The refusal names what draws it, and
      `group.models[name].plot.section(...)` for a group or a diff.
      **What the noun names is what measured to act:** `kstpkper`, `layer`,
      `interpolate`, `interpolator`, `use_rbf`, `num_points`, `clip`, `x_or_y`,
      `show_model_top`, `show_model_btm` (`NOUN_SECTION_PARAMS`; the last two act since
      ledger 333's frame fix). Deliberately NOT named: `spacing` and
      `extrapolate_beyond_section_ends` (they never act, ledger 333);
      `animation_kstpkpers` (a noun returns a figure, never `.ani`); `section_name` (it was
      the group's and the diff's crash, and `title=` labels a figure); `resolution`/`crs`
      (the verb takes them only through its tail, and a narrower scope may not offer what
      the wider does not name); `surf_type` (the noun fixes its field; the refusal gives
      the verb spelling that sections the layers).
      **`**refused` stays on the signature and forwards NOTHING.** With no tail, a stray
      `fill=` gets Python's own `TypeError`, naming `SpatialView.section` -- a class nobody
      typed -- and no way to the picture; with it the refusal names the verb, and a typo
      gets its nearest accepted spelling. Named `refused` so an editor's popup says what
      it is for.
      **The funnel closes too.** `XSection` checks its tail when BUILT against
      `SURFACE_OPTIONS`, the names `InterpolatedSurface` takes that `XSection` does not
      pass itself -- the SAME names as before, checked always rather than only when
      interpolating -- so the verb's line profile refuses a typo as well. An unknown
      keyword is a `TypeError` on both of the verb's pictures now (the cross-section's
      leftover check raised `ValueError`); an argument the verb DOES name, given to the
      other picture, stays a `ValueError` naming that picture. The composers check their
      tail with the same helper, and refuse `kstpkper` (each panel reads its own time;
      `per=` chooses them).
      **Fixed in passing:** `cells=<int>` died at `len()` on the line profile at both
      scopes, where both document `int or list of int` and `XSection`'s own docstring
      shows `cells=69`.
      **Why no test saw it:** `test_noun_signatures` discovers subjects by a body
      mentioning `plot.map(`/`plot.section(`/`_choropleth_factory`, and the noun's
      `section` renders through `render_xsections` -- ledger 258's gap, one verb over. It
      reaches it now only through its docstring's pointer at the verb, so it is swept
      explicitly as well, the measured set is verb-aware, and every `Class.section` in
      `src/` with a `**kwargs` tail is pinned, exact in both directions.
      **Not done** (RESOLVED by ledger 337, all three):
      `surf_type="lyr"` while interpolating crashes on the verb (`'NoneType'
      object has no attribute 'loc'`); each line-profile section reloads the simulation
      through FloPy at its default verbosity, which prints; and `XSection` reads `per` as
      an index into the SAVED times, the stage-clock family CLAUDE.md lists as open.
      Tests: `tests/test_section_noun.py`, 48, and three in `tests/test_noun_signatures.py`.
      Reverting the noun's refusal and `XSection`'s check together fails 32 of the 48 by
      name -- both agreement tests and all four typo tests among them; the noun's alone
      28 (the typos are still caught at `XSection`); `XSection`'s alone the 4 typo tests;
      the composers' check 4; the `cells` fix 1.

335. **A test session writes its temp files in its OWN root and a leak fails by name; `layers.py` no longer leaves a directory behind per 3-D stack view or draft grid (2026-09-26).**
      /tmp here is a 16 GB tmpfs with a per-user quota. On 2026-09-26 it held 13,926
      `/tmp/tmp*` entries (5.9 GB), the quota was hit, and EVERY write the user made there
      failed, Claude Code's own tool output included. They were deleted with the user's
      consent; none was held open.
      **Measured, the suite was NOT the source of that volume** -- a correction to the
      premise this work was asked on. A full run at 720dd4b, serial and `-n 8` alike,
      left **50** entries in an isolated TMPDIR: pytest's own `pytest-of-<user>` (24.6-26
      MB, which pytest rotates, keeping three runs) and **49 leaks totalling about 2 MB**
      -- 17 `layer_view_*` and 7 `draft_grid_*` from `layers.py`, 22 from test helpers,
      2 from subprocess probes, and pyemu's `port_locks`, attributed by instrumenting
      `tempfile` per test. At 2 MB a run the suite could not have made 13,926 entries or
      4 GB in an hour; that rate had been blamed on concurrent test runs from their
      timing alone, and the real source (another session's branch, a script, a notebook)
      was not identified before the entries were gone.
      **The library half, which leaks for users as well:** `_vtk_plotter` (every 3-D
      stack view) built a throwaway FloPy model in `mkdtemp(prefix="layer_view_")` only
      to reach FloPy's VTK exporter -- nothing is written there, and the mesh is in
      memory by the end -- and `LayerStack.draft_grid` left Triangle's files in
      `mkdtemp(prefix="draft_grid_")` although `build()` reads the mesh back into memory
      before the Voronoi grid is made. Both are `TemporaryDirectory` blocks now; the tests
      of both pass unchanged.
      **The test half:** helpers and fixtures write under `tmp_path`/`tmp_path_factory`;
      the two subprocess probes use a self-removing `TemporaryDirectory`. The tour
      notebook's `tempfile.mkdtemp()` is ASSERTED by its test (a reader running it
      litters nothing in the repo), so the notebook keeps it and the test points
      `tempfile.tempdir` at its `tmp_path` instead. No assertion changed.
      **The guard, `tests/conftest.py`:** each session gets its own root,
      `mkdtemp(prefix="myflopy-pytest-")`, with one subdirectory per xdist worker so one
      worker's entries are never blamed on another's test. An autouse function-scoped
      fixture fails the test that leaves an entry, naming it; the session-end sweep fails
      the run over what a fixture or a process left (exit code 1, a red section, "temp
      leaks" in the count); the root is removed either way, so even a failing run leaves
      nothing. Judgment calls:
      - **The root sits under the usual temp dir, not in the repo:** multiprocessing puts
        an AF_UNIX socket in the temp dir, and its path may not exceed 107 bytes -- a
        repo path inside a `.claude` worktree is about 85 characters before the socket's
        own name.
      - **pytest's `tmp_path_factory` area keeps its place and its retention**
        (`PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT` is set to the prior temp dir) instead of being deleted
        with the root: pytest already bounds it to three runs, and a failed run's fixture
        output stays there to inspect.
      - **`port_locks` is allowed by name:** pyemu's `PortManager` makes it once under
        `tempfile.gettempdir()` with a fixed name, so it cannot accumulate, and the
        root's removal takes it anyway. `pymp-*` (multiprocessing's per-process
        directory, removed at exit) is NOT allowed ahead of need: no test was measured to
        leave one at teardown.
      - **A per-test failure does not delete the entry**, so the sweep lists it again;
        deleting could remove a directory a still-live fixture made lazily.
      - **A subprocess started with an environment that drops TMPDIR** writes to /tmp
        outside the root and the guard cannot see it; none does today.
      Broken three ways to check it: a test writing into `mkdtemp` again ERRORS at its
      teardown naming the entry; the 3-D view regressing errors every test that draws a
      scene; a module fixture's `mkdtemp` fails the run at the end (exit code 1).
      **After:** a full run leaves nothing in the temp dir but pytest's own rotating area
      (28 MB), and no session root is left behind.
      **Not done:** the source of the 13,926 entries is unidentified; user notebooks and
      scripts that call `tempfile.mkdtemp()` themselves (the tour notebook, run by a
      reader) are unchanged.
336. **A period's flow is its END-of-period flow: the SFR and DRN flow targets added every step a period saved, and every target family now reads the record that ends the period through ONE rule, refusing a period whose end was not saved (2026-09-26).**
      The user's call, on ledger 331's open item: "a period's flow should be end of
      period value". `SfrFlowTargets` and `DrnFlowTargets` ADDED every saved step on their
      budget-file route: the canonical model (testing profile, `nstp=3`, `SAVE ALL`) read
      its outlet reach at **113,453.29 for 37,817.76** and a one-cell spring zone (cell
      317) at **-292.51 for -97.50**. Adding a zone's CELLS within one step stays -- that
      is what a lumped seepage measurement is (`kind="extensive"`); adding its STEPS goes.
      Both now route through `_aggregate_named_series(kind="extensive", ends=...)`.
      **ONE rule, and where it lives.** `myflopy.modflow.mf6.period_end.period_end_steps`
      picks each period's record for heads and concentration (`_simulated_field_by_period`),
      SFR stage, SFR flow and DRN flow (`_aggregate_named_series`), LAK stage (the refusal
      only, below) and PEST's forward-run head/concentration writers, which each held a copy
      (`by_period[kper] = ...`). It reads the FILE's own clock (the reader's `recordarray`,
      ledger 301) -- a flow the budget file's, a head or stage the head file's -- and the
      module imports numpy and pandas only, because the forward run imports it on every
      model run: importing the observations package measured 2.36 s against 0.05 s. That is
      also why `pest.forward_run`'s deferred imports go 1 -> 3 in the ratchet: pyEMU copies
      only a function's source, so its imports cannot be hoisted. Its model-level wrappers,
      `period_lengths(model)` and `period_ends(model, reader=, ...)`, live there too, not in
      the observations package, so the head noun (import layer 2) reaches them.
      **The END is found by TIME, not by step count** -- judgment call. A record ends its
      period when its `pertim` is the TDIS `perlen` (to 1e-8 of it, below), not when `kstp`
      is `nstp - 1`: under ATS the step count is decided at run time (periods declared
      `nstp=1` took 7 and 6 steps in one probe, 4 each in the tests), so `nstp` would
      refuse every ATS period, and MF6 writes the final step's `pertim` as the `perlen` it
      READ, EXACTLY (measured at `tsmult` 1.2 and 0.9 and under ATS).
      **The tolerance is FloPy's WRITE precision** -- judgment call, from review. What MF6
      read is FloPy's 8-decimal rendering (`{:15.8f}` from 0.001 to 1e5, `{:.8E}`
      outside), while the check compares the `perlen` FloPy HOLDS: an hour held as `1/24`
      is written `0.04166667`, 3.3e-9 off. At 1e-9 x max(1, `perlen`) a LIVE model
      (`run.model()`) with hourly, 1/3- or 4/3-unit periods had every period refused --
      heads, flows and the forward run given the lengths the build records -- while the
      same run reloaded read fine, and the refusal read "ending 0.0416667 into a period
      0.0416667 long". `END_RTOL` is 1e-8 now, twice FloPy's worst (5e-9 x max(1,
      `perlen`), measured at 100000.00049 written `1.00000000E+05`), and the refusal prints
      digits enough to tell its two numbers apart. **Considered and not taken:**
      round-tripping `perlen` through FloPy's formatter (exact for a live model, WRONG for
      one loaded from a file written with more digits than FloPy writes, whose values ARE
      what MF6 read) and parsing the TDIS file (OPEN/CLOSE and missing-file fallbacks for
      a number the tolerance already settles). **Limits:** a FloPy `float_precision` below
      its default 8 (myflopy sets none) is refused, loudly; a last time step shorter than
      1e-8 of its period (`tsmult=0.5` over 27+ steps) would let the step before it read
      as the end.
      **A period whose end the file does not hold is REFUSED, not warned** -- judgment call,
      the user's rule arguing for it. Under `SAVE ... FIRST`, `STEPS` short of the end or
      `FREQUENCY`, the end-of-period value does not exist, and the old rule silently read
      an earlier step (the toy zone at step 1 of 3: -27.02 where the period ends at
      -709.47). The error names the periods, the steps saved and `SAVE BUDGET LAST` (or
      `HEAD`). **Measured cost: nothing seen.** All 26 MF6 OC files under
      `/home/lukem/models` save `ALL` or `LAST` (16 `LAST`/`LAST`, 8 `ALL`/`ALL`, 2 `HEAD
      ALL` + `BUDGET LAST`); every tracked `saverecord` is `ALL`/`LAST` except
      `tests/test_budget_clocks.py`'s `STEPS 1`/`STEPS 3` fixture, which no target reads;
      the canonical model saves `ALL` (`steps_per_period` 2, the testing profile 1);
      `OutputControl` and `simplemodel` default to `LAST`; and every existing target and
      PEST test passed with the refusal in place, three after their doubles gained a clock
      (a fake head file's `recordarray`, a fake SFR budget's `types`). A warning would have
      left the wrong number in PEST's files. **Applied to every family for consistency**:
      heads, concentration, SFR stage, LAK stage, SFR flow, DRN flow, and the forward run,
      whose calls now carry `perlen=[...]` from the build so a realization whose ATS moved
      a `STEPS` save off the end fails rather than hands PEST an early value (a forward run
      generated before this reads unchecked). A period that saved NOTHING is absent, not
      refused: nothing is read for it, so nothing can be wrong. A model with no TDIS -- only
      a duck-typed double -- reads each period's last saved step unchecked.
      **LAK keeps its record clock** (ledger 331's limit, `build_lak_stage_result_table`,
      open under 301): its table has no `kstpkper` to reduce. What it gains is the refusal,
      which catches the worst of it -- one `FIRST` record per period made the record index

      **Found on the same route and FIXED:** the SFR flow route asked FloPy for `TO-MVR`
      unconditionally, which RAISES on every stream without a mover ("The specified text
      string is not in the budget file") -- it reads only the terms the file holds now;
      and an OUTLET reach had no row, its water leaving as `EXT-OUTFLOW`, which was not
      read. A reach's flow is outbound FLOW-JA-FACE + `TO-MVR` + `EXT-OUTFLOW` now, equal to
      MF6's own `DOWNSTREAM-FLOW` at every period end (toy reaches 0 and 3; canonical

      **`model.hds`/`conc`/`temp.get()` read the rule too** (review). Documented as

      **The VIEW layer is LEFT, deliberately** -- scope cut (MOVED by ledger 337, on the

      `cross_section_plotting.section_time`, `package_plotting._period_end_kstpkper` and

      **The observation route, recorded and NOT changed** (the period-end rule does not

      **Not built:** a time-weighted mean over the period (the user chose the end); the LAK

      Reproducer: `docs/reproducers/flow_targets_period_end.py` (the toy under five OC

338. **Every public parameter has a `name : type` entry with a description, and a test holds it: 1,968 missing entries, types or descriptions across 476 callables were written, then checked against the code by a second pass (2026-09-27).**
      The user's rule, asked for repeatedly ("I've been through this a million times"),
      made mechanical. `tests/test_public_parameters_documented.py` DISCOVERS the surface
      -- `__all__`, `__engine__`, the helper objects' methods (`mf.chd.gpkg`,
      `mf.rch.array`, ...) and every public method myflopy defines on an exported class,
      each function once however many classes inherit it: 715 callables -- and requires of
      each: an entry per named parameter whose head reads `name : type` and whose body is
      not empty; an entry for a `*`/`**` tail saying where it goes; no `Parameters` entry
      naming something the callable does not accept (unless it has a `**` tail); and no
      column-0 prose inside the block, which `help()` renders as a parameter (`mf.ims`
      had one, read as three fake parameters). Before it only the plot verbs were checked.
      **No allowlist** -- judgment call: the gaps were closed in the same commit, so the
      test is strict from its first run. **Floors, not an exact count** (`MIN_CALLABLES`)
      -- judgment call: a discovery that finds nothing must fail, a new public method must
      not. **Its own parser** -- numpydoc is not a dependency, and `plot._documented_names`
      reads names only, which passed `LakeTableBuilder` with all 11 parameters untyped.
      **A dataclass may document its fields under `Attributes`** -- judgment call: for a
      record users RECEIVE (`Run`, `SaveReport`, `BuiltModel`) that is the idiomatic
      section; any other class must use `Parameters`.
      **What the test cannot see is whether an entry is TRUE** -- it checks that a type is
      written, not that the code accepts it. Every new entry was read against the code by
      an agent that did not write it: 2,004 entries, 175 corrected -- defaults that did not
      match the signature, "optional" where `None` raises, a precedence stated backwards,
      a type the code refuses (`GridSpec.resolve` is keyword-only; `ModelContext.grid` is
      duck-typed; a module-level lambda serializes but cannot be read back). The test
      stops the next GAP; review is still what stops the next wrong entry.
      **Docstrings describe what the code does TODAY**, including where the pass found it
      wrong -- scope cut: 82 code defects were reported and none fixed here (only
      docstrings changed; a docstring-stripped AST of every touched module is identical to
      its parent). The ones that reach PEST are fixed in the entries after this one; the
      rest were listed for the user. Fixing one means correcting its entry too (e.g.
      `mf.sfr`'s per-stream `rainfall` mapping, documented as landing on the stream's
      first reach).
      **NOT covered** -- scope cut: the read-grammar views reached as

      them from `__all__`; their plot verbs are checked by `test_noun_signatures`, their

339. **One package is `model.<pkg>`, and FloPy's package object is `model.fl.<pkg>`; `model.packages` keeps only the all-packages verbs (2026-09-27).**
      The user's call: `model.drn.inputs.map()` in place of `model.packages.drn.inputs.map()`.
      `model.drn` already existed -- 4.7.7's accessors returned FloPy's `ModflowGwfdrn` -- so
      this CHANGED what the name means rather than adding a forward. FloPy's object moved to
      `model.fl.drn` (`FlopyPackages`: the ten registry packages as typed properties, anything
      else -- `npf`, `disv`, `tdis` -- by name through `model.package`, which raises naming the
      model). **No transition shim and no warned alias** -- the user is the only user (their
      call); the 35 reads of the FloPy object in `src/`, three in tests and one reproducer were
      repointed, found by a sweep for the ten names on a model receiver.
      **Kept, deliberately:** `model.packages`. It carries `summary()` and the cross-package
      `mosaic()`, and `model.summary()` already means the model's own table, so there was
      nowhere to move them. `model.packages.<pkg>` still resolves -- it is what `model.<pkg>`
      returns -- and is no longer taught; 274 teaching sites were rewritten.
      **NOT done -- scope cut:** the group and diff scopes keep `group.packages.<pkg>` /
      `diff.packages.<pkg>`, so the grammar's first hop now differs by scope. The ledger, the
      reproducers and the old reports and plans keep the old spelling as the record of their
      day. Promoted beside the ten: `hfb`, `ic`, `npf`, `sto`, `surface_water`. There are five
      hand-written namespaces now, each held complete by
      `test_every_namespace_exposes_every_registry_package` and listed in the payoff test's
